article_content_zh:
对我来说，成为一名程序员是一种妥协。在我大学三年级的时候，我清楚地意识到，作为一名来自韩国的国际学生，我很可能无法在毕业后留下很长时间，除非我将专业从哲学改为 STEM 领域，从而使我有资格获得签证延期。显而易见的选择是计算机科学，这已经是我的辅修专业了。

这种转变伴随着一种羞耻感，现在回想起来，这有点儿戏剧化的感觉。我想我受到了伊恩·麦克尤恩（Ian McEwan）曾经所说的“现代形式的势利”的困扰，在描述一个人物时，她在接受了书生气十足的大学教育后，开始认为“一个拥有化学学位的人作为一个人来说是不完整的”。化学、计算机科学——同样的差异。可以肯定地说，我在 CS 部门没有很多朋友。

但我不认为我的娇气完全是错误的。在 2010 年代 Facebook 首次公开募股后的骚动中，这个国家的计算机科学部门新涌现出了一批在另一个时代可能会去华尔街的奋斗者。我的理论是，许多美国人对技术怀有敌意，他们是通过对这些暴发户的敌意而获得这种敌意的。也就是说，与其说他们是反技术，不如说他们是反技术专家。

无论如何，我半途而废地完成了很多计算机科学作业，这意味着我从来没有面临进入人工智能研究生院的危险。但幸运的是，凭借韩国强大的公共数学教育，我进入这门学科并没有太坎坷。如果说有什么不同的话，那就是理论计算机科学和分布式系统似乎是哲学的延续。

但我无法消除这样的感觉：编程是一种无意义的浪费精力。我必须阅读的每一行代码，我必须编写的每一行代码，都浪费了我本来可以用来阅读我关心的内容的时间。也许我的前两种语言是Java（丑陋而乏味）和C（令人钦佩但不可原谅），这对我没有帮助。时至今日，Java 代码就像一颗有毒的玛德琳蛋糕，会唤起不受欢迎的回忆。

大学毕业后，我的签证规定我必须从事与我的专业直接相关的工作，并且我找到了一家愿意赞助我的绿卡的科技公司。问题是，我可能需要很多年才能获得绿卡——结果是四年——所以我想我最好找到一种让编程变得愉快的方法。

工作的头几个月并不快乐。我在一家医疗保健初创公司工作，我认为这给了我一种有用的道德感，以应对持续不断的技术冲击，并为我后来作为一名作家提供了一种补偿。但我喜欢我的同事，其中一些人也怀有艺术抱负，下班后我们会定期去麦克纳利杰克逊举办文学活动，距离我们办公室一个街区。

然后，有一天，我发现了一种叫做 Haskell 的语言。我的任务是使用从中借用概念的库重写代码库。我对 Haskell 的模糊印象是，它是一种困难的语言，涉及数学的一个分支，称为范畴论。它周围有一种令人生畏的光环，很诱人，当我尝试编写基本程序时，这种语言确实具有挑战性，但又很吸引人。

我开始潜伏在 Haskell 论坛中，在那里，编程语言（众所周知的“PL”）领域的研究人员炫耀他们对该语言的丰富掌握。 PL 研究人员也可能是计算机科学的诗人：一个由专注的偏执狂组成的小社区，他们从事一项基本无利可图的事业（这在计算机科学中很少见），并伴随着所有随之而来的争吵和内讧。与人工智能不同，无利可图意味着该领域具有廉洁的尊严。

很快，令我惊讶的是，我发现自己在工作之外编程。经过几个月的对 Haskell 的修改，我发现了一本名为《用 Go 编写编译器》的书。事实证明你甚至可以自己发明一种语言。我制作了一些玩具语言，在实践中毫无用处，但对于揭开编程语言工作原理的神秘面纱却非常有价值。

编码还有一种间接的方式可以帮助写作。在第 4 号草案中，记者中的记者约翰·麦克菲 (John McPhee) 表示，他仍在使用一种名为 Kedit 的古老文本编辑器，这是普林斯顿大学的一名程序员于 1984 年向他推荐的。 （“我从未使用过文字处理程序，”他写道。）当我自己改用文本编辑器时，我明白了他为什么坚持使用它。通过开源代码，我可以添加一些愚蠢但有用的功能，例如以显眼的颜色突出显示“TK”（新闻业中占位符文本的常见简写），以便以后轻松找到。

如果不出意外的话，我开始意识到，编程是进入一种称为“心流”的难以捉摸的模式的可靠方式，在这种状态下，我们不知何故既健忘又警觉。

在业界，人们普遍认为对编程语言的挑剔是幼稚的。如果求职者表现出对语言的热情，这很可能是一个危险信号。如果你能阅读五种语言的菜单，但无法用一种语言写出像样的散文，那么成为“通晓多种语言”的人就毫无美德。根据流行且有影响力的文章“选择无聊的技术”，使用奇特、新颖的语言与严肃、稳健的工程相矛盾——就像前卫诗学不适合起草法律合同一样。

不幸的是，对于我的雇主来说，我对严肃的工程毫无兴趣。然而，在我拿到绿卡之前，我确实非常在意在日常工作中度过愉快的时光。如果他们给我一个使用新语言的机会，我就会接受项目，这是一个愚蠢的原因，出于同样的原因，我什至自愿更换团队，这通常是一个糟糕的职业决定。在强制性的公司黑客马拉松周中，我将特定领域的语言（那些专门用于特定目的的语言）组合在一起。我通过向官方 TypeScript 编译器提交了几个简单的补丁，做出了微薄的公共贡献。我在 Stack Overflow 上获得了一些金色徽章。几年过去了，你知道吗，我成为了一名相当不错的程序员。

title: Trump hosts crypto traders as demand for his meme coin fades
title_en: Trump hosts crypto traders as demand for his meme coin fades
author: Isaac Arnsdorf
article_content:
In a reception room here where chandeliers abounded and women less so, top collectors of President Donald Trump’s novelty crypto token gathered to graze on fall harvest salad and filet mignon.

Some wore rented tuxes. At least one wore a red cap. A pump-up dancer in a Trump mask greeted them. VIP guests received gold-tone Trump diver watches and Trump-branded “Victory” fragrances at his Northern Virginia golf club, where they rubbed shoulders with retired athletes Floyd Mayweather and Tristan Thompson. Mentalist Lior Suchard claimed to read their minds.

Trump spoke for about 40 minutes. He predicted Wall Street would increasingly embrace crypto currencies and called for Congress to pass legislation establishing federal rules for digital assets — a measure that previously failed because Democrats objected to ethics exceptions for Trump and his family.

The biggest political news to start your morning. Sign up for free

He took questions from the group, including from a Chinese woman who asked for his favorite Chinese dish. He didn’t specify. He also sidestepped a question about how Viktor Orban’s loss in Hungary would affect the U.S. relationship with that country. He praised Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and declined to criticize Elon Musk for disavowing MAGA. He repeated that he would support former CEO Jensen Huang returning to Nvidia.

In response to a question about the situation in Haiti, Trump began criticizing Somali immigrants in Minnesota. And when one attendee urged Trump to run for a third term, he said the Constitution was clear that he could not.

The value of Trump’s meme coin has crashed, as most meme coins do. The digital assets are a way of monetizing attention, usually highest at their debut. This dinner was an effort to rustle up more interest, but a Washington Post analysis showed a seat could be secured for as little as $518, compared to $55,000 for the first gala in May 2025.

In the interim, his popularity plummeted, young men deserted him, and his party suffered its biggest midterms defeat in 52 years.

While most investors in the coin lost money, Trump reported earning $635 million from the meme coin last year.

When Trump announced the venture on the cusp of his second inauguration, Democrats and ethics experts decried it as a cash grab that could present an opportunity for lobbyists and favor-seekers to pay him off. The venture has been enormously lucrative for Trump, though the feared market for presidential influence is less clear. The buyers have been mostly Trump fans and crypto enthusiasts, sometimes both, according to attendees. Organizers and attendees said no one received individual time with the president at Sunday’s event.

The meme coin was the latest thing — this time a virtual one — for Trump to put his name on and sell, coming after skyscrapers, steaks, wine, casinos, clubs, neckties, vodka, a magazine, an airline, gold sneakers and a business seminar that paid $25 million to settle fraud claims. A company called Celebration Cards pays Trump to use his name for the crypto venture.

“Nobody seemed disappointed about the midterms or the price of the token,” said Morten Christensen, a crypto investor who attended Sunday’s dinner and met people there from countries including China, India, Saudi Arabia, the United Kingdom and Ukraine. “It was fun to be there.”

article_content_zh:
在这里的一间接待室里，枝形吊灯比比皆是，而女性则较少，唐纳德·特朗普总统的新奇加密代币的顶级收藏家聚集在一起，品尝秋收沙拉和菲力牛排。

有些人穿着租来的礼服。至少有一个人戴着红色帽子。一位戴着特朗普面具、精神抖擞的舞者迎接了他们。贵宾在他的北弗吉尼亚高尔夫俱乐部收到了金色的特朗普潜水手表和特朗普品牌的“胜利”香水，他们在那里与退役运动员弗洛伊德·梅威瑟和特里斯坦·汤普森擦肩而过。心灵学家利奥尔·苏查德声称能读懂他们的想法。

特朗普讲话约40分钟。他预测华尔街将越来越多地接受加密货币，并呼吁国会通过立法，建立数字资产的联邦规则——这项措施此前因民主党反对特朗普及其家人的道德例外而失败。

他回答了大家的问题，其中包括一位中国女士提出的问题，她询问了他最喜欢的中国菜。他没有具体说明。他还回避了欧尔班·维克托在匈牙利的失败将如何影响美国与该国关系的问题。他赞扬了 Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei)，并拒绝批评埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 否认 MAGA。他重申，他将支持前首席执行官黄仁勋重返英伟达。

在回答有关海地局势的问题时，特朗普开始批评明尼苏达州的索马里移民。当一名与会者敦促特朗普竞选第三个任期时，他表示宪法明确规定他不能竞选。

与大多数模因币一样，特朗普模因币的价值已经暴跌。数字资产是一种将注意力货币化的方式，通常在首次亮相时最高。这次晚宴是为了吸引更多人的兴趣，但《华盛顿邮报》的分析显示，仅需 518 美元即可获得席位，而 2025 年 5 月首届晚宴的费用为 55,000 美元。

在此期间，他的支持率直线下降，年轻人抛弃了他，他的政党在中期选举中遭受了 52 年来最大的失败。

尽管该币的大多数投资者都亏损了，但特朗普去年却从这款迷因币中赚了 6.35 亿美元。

当特朗普在第二次就职之际宣布这一合资企业时，民主党人和道德专家谴责这是一种抢钱行为，可能为游说者和寻求恩惠的人提供了向他买单的机会。尽管令人担忧的总统影响力市场尚不那么明朗，但这一合资企业为特朗普带来了巨大的利润。据与会者称，买家大多是特朗普的粉丝和加密货币爱好者，有时两者兼而有之。组织者和与会者表示，没有人在周日的活动中与总统单独相处。

模因币是特朗普冠上自己名字并出售的最新产品——这次是虚拟的——此前，摩天大楼、牛排、葡萄酒、赌场、俱乐部、领带、伏特加、一本杂志、一家航空公司、金色运动鞋和一个支付 2500 万美元解决欺诈索赔的商业研讨会之后。一家名为 Celebration Cards 的公司付钱给特朗普，让他在加密货币企业中使用他的名字。

“似乎没有人对中期选举或代币的价格感到失望，”参加周日晚宴并会见了来自中国、印度、沙特阿拉伯、英国和乌克兰等国家的人士的加密货币投资者莫滕·克里斯滕森 (Morten Christensen) 表示。 “在那里很有趣。”

title: Behind China’s A.I. Anxieties, Fear of a Nuclear Checkmate
title_en: Behind China’s A.I. Anxieties, Fear of a Nuclear Checkmate

inline_images.alt: An early-warning radar scanning the horizon at a U.S. Space Force base in Greenland. China, the United States and Russia use radars, satellites and sensors to monitor one another’s nuclear weapons.

author: Chris Buckley
article_content:
When Xi Jinping, the Chinese leader, set about expanding China’s nuclear forces a decade ago, his goal was to ensure that enough missiles could survive an initial attack so Beijing could deliver a devastating counterattack.

That ability to withstand a strike and hit back would deter any enemy from risking nuclear blackmail or war against China in the first place, Chinese strategists have said.

But now, researchers in the Chinese military worry that American advances in artificial intelligence could weaken Beijing’s nuclear hand in a crisis or conflict. They have been warning that artificial intelligence could make it easier for U.S. forces to find and wipe out Chinese nuclear missiles, giving Washington a menacing advantage.

The worries over A.I. complicate the growing nuclear tensions between Washington and Beijing, and could make China more reluctant to consider limits to its smaller arsenal. At a summit on Thursday, Mr. Xi, President Trump and President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia spoke of reducing nuclear risks. But Mr. Xi has shown no interest in Mr. Trump’s calls for China to join arms control commitments.

A review of more than 100 recent studies by Chinese civilian and military researchers, as well as interviews with experts and former U.S. officials, points to a deep wariness in China about the American pursuit of A.I. in nuclear systems. At the same time, Chinese military institutes are also exploring how A.I. could make Chinese missiles harder to detect and knock from the sky.

China, the United States and Russia use radars, satellites and sensors to monitor each other’s nuclear weapons. Breakthroughs in A.I. could help create technology to detect, track and strike nuclear weapons more quickly and accurately. Experts in China worry that it could lag the United States in applying such advances.

A study from China’s top military institute described a scenario in which artificial intelligence accelerated U.S. actions in a crisis to mere moments, potentially overwhelming slower rivals.

“By embedding A.I. and other technologies into nuclear decision-making systems, the United States could compress the decision-making process from the traditional 15 to 30 minutes to 90 seconds or less, drastically increasing the speed of response,” two researchers from the Academy of Military Science in Beijing wrote in an overview of global nuclear trends published several months ago.

China has about 620 nuclear warheads that could be delivered by land- or submarine-based missiles, or by bombers, the Federation of American Scientists estimates. China’s arsenal is widely forecast to grow to about 1,000 warheads by 2030. (The United States and Russia each have around 1,800 nuclear warheads deployed for missiles and bombers, with thousands more stockpiled.)

China fears that A.I. advances could enable the United States “to rapidly engage in strikes as soon as something pops out from a hiding spot or mobilizes,” said Gerald C. Brown, a former analyst with the State Department who studies China’s nuclear strategy. “Basically, in their view, it could make survivability a lot more difficult.”

China’s missile force is closely watching the U.S. Strategic Command, which controls nuclear missiles and has said that it wants to use A.I. to enhance “decision-making capabilities.” Chinese military analysts are also studying how American conventional forces use A.I. to coordinate operations and pick targets.

The U.S. edge in making advanced chips is adding to Chinese concerns that the United States can move faster to incorporate A.I. into its military, including in nuclear-related systems, said Jacob Stokes, a senior fellow at the Center for a New American Security in Washington.

Official history reinforces China’s anxieties. Chinese military officers studied the Korean War and crises over Taiwan in the 1950s, when the United States signaled that it could drop atomic bombs on Mao Zedong’s forces, which then had no nuclear weapons, said Mr. Brown, now an international affairs fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations.

China has already been diversifying its nuclear weapons to enhance their “survivability.”

In July, it held a test launch of a long-range missile from a submarine, showing its intention to create an undersea nuclear deterrent that could be harder for the United States to detect and destroy. China has also built about 320 launch silos in its northern deserts, which could make it harder for an enemy to determine which ones hold nuclear-armed missiles and knock them all out with precision strikes.

But Chinese experts now warn that breakthroughs in military A.I. could help the United States overcome China’s efforts to protect its arsenal and, in an extreme case, could tempt Washington to attempt a crippling first strike against those forces.

“I believe these risks weigh heavily in China’s strategic considerations,” Sun Chenghao, a senior fellow at the Center for International Security and Strategy at Tsinghua University in Beijing, wrote in emailed answers to questions.

“What China needs to assess is whether, under extreme circumstances, the U.S. might rely on A.I. reconnaissance, precision strikes and missile defense to weaken China’s capabilities to launch nuclear retaliation after an attack,” he wrote.

China’s leaders appear determined not to fall too far behind. In July, Mr. Xi held a meeting of senior officials to study the military implications of A.I. and other technological advances. He demanded steady progress toward their deployment.

In China, there is “great optimism that A.I. is the tool that is going to allow you to finally catch up to or surpass the United States militarily,” said Sam Bresnick, a research fellow at the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University.

Studies published by China’s Rocket Force, which controls most of its nuclear missiles, show a wide interest in A.I.

One study involving a Rocket Force scientist published last year examined how A.I.-enabled “deep reinforcement learning” could help hypersonic glide vehicles — weapons designed to dodge and weave as they approach their targets — better evade missile defenses.

The researchers simulated millions of possible flight paths to train an A.I. system to guide a hypersonic vehicle in flight. They used no-fly zones around Alaska as real-life examples of the challenges a hypersonic weapon might encounter, and test if A.I. could help the weapon navigate the defenses.

In another study, Rocket Force scientists used computer simulations to model how A.I. could help a ballistic missile get back on course after swerving to evade high-speed interceptors. An A.I.-assisted autopilot could calculate when to fire steering thrusters, secondary rocket engines that help change direction, while conserving fuel.

China should “apply cutting-edge technologies such as artificial intelligence and hypersonics, strengthening deployment of forces, and improving their survivability and retaliatory capabilities,” five scholars from a Rocket Force university wrote in a paper published this year that examined other countries’ nuclear exercises.

But even some researchers in the People’s Liberation Army have warned against rushing to introduce the technology in nuclear weapons systems.

In the most dire projections, rogue A.I.-generated internet viruses could commandeer nuclear weapons controls, disabling or launching the weapons.

But short of that, A.I. could incorporate and magnify false data, leading to dangerous, even disastrous, errors in crisis decision-making. Commanders could put too much trust in A.I.-generated conclusions or advice, experts say. Chinese studies have pointed to U.S. battlefield errors in conventional wars that they say reflect too much faith in automated targeting.

Erroneous information magnified through A.I. creates “enormous decision-making risks,” researchers from China’s National University of Defense Technology and the Academy of Military Sciences wrote in a study this year. “This is becoming the core obstacle to its deep application in the highly serious, high-risk field of command and control.”

Nuclear weapons systems have long contained high levels of automation to ensure accuracy, speed and security. But A.I. advances could reduce the role of human oversight in ways that can be dangerous during a fast-moving crisis, said Philip Reiner, the chief executive officer of the Institute for Security and Technology, a California-based group based that examines the implications of A.I. for nuclear weapons security and stability.

“This is a technology that is moving faster than anything any human has ever seen before,” he said of advanced A.I. “Nobody’s turning launch decisions over to A.I., but everything that tells you whether you should launch is now going to be shaped by A.I. And so, does that make it riskier? Yes.”

Yet even as the need for safeguards has become greater, the United States and China have made little progress in discussing them. Mr. Xi agreed with then-President Biden in 2024 to maintain human control over the decision to use nuclear weapons, but no official talks on the issue have followed. Mr. Xi, Mr. Trump and Mr. Putin did not mention the role of A.I. in nuclear weapons during their summit last week.

article_content_zh:
十年前，当中国领导人习近平着手扩大中国的核力量时，他的目标是确保有足够的导弹能够在最初的攻击中幸存下来，以便北京能够发动毁灭性的反击。

中国战略家表示，这种抵御打击和反击的能力将首先阻止任何敌人冒核讹诈或对中国发动战争的风险。

但现在，中国军方的研究人员担心，美国在人工智能方面的进步可能会削弱北京在危机或冲突中的核力量。他们一直警告说，人工智能可能使美军更容易发现并消灭中国的核导弹，从而给华盛顿带来威胁性优势。

对人工智能的担忧使华盛顿和北京之间日益加剧的核紧张局势复杂化，并可能使中国更不愿意考虑限制其较小的核武库。在周四的峰会上，习近平、特朗普总统和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·V·普京谈到了减少核风险。但习近平对特朗普呼吁中国加入军控承诺没有表现出兴趣。

对中国民间和军事研究人员最近进行的 100 多项研究的回顾，以及对专家和前美国官员的采访，表明中国对美国追求人工智能深感警惕。在核系统中。与此同时，中国军事院校也在探索人工智能如何应用。可能会使中国导弹更难被空中探测和击落。

中国、美国和俄罗斯利用雷达、卫星和传感器来监测彼此的核武器。人工智能领域的突破可以帮助创造更快速、更准确地探测、跟踪和打击核武器的技术。中国专家担心，中国在应用这些进步方面可能会落后于美国。

中国最高军事研究所的一项研究描述了这样一种情况：人工智能将美国在危机中的行动加速到了瞬间，有可能压倒速度较慢的竞争对手。

“通过将人工智能和其他技术嵌入到核决策系统中，美国可以将决策过程从传统的15至30分钟压缩到90秒甚至更短，大大提高了反应速度，”北京军事科学院的两名研究人员在几个月前发表的全球核趋势概述中写道。

美国科学家联合会估计，中国拥有约 620 枚核弹头，可以通过陆基或潜基导弹或轰炸机发射。人们普遍预测，到 2030 年，中国的核弹头数量将增至约 1,000 枚。（美国和俄罗斯各部署了约 1,800 枚用于导弹和轰炸机的核弹头，还有数千枚库存。）

中国担心人工智能。研究中国核战略的前国务院分析师杰拉尔德·C·布朗(Gerald C. Brown)表示，这些进展可能使美国“能够在有东西从隐藏地点出现或动员起来时迅速发动打击”。 “基本上，在他们看来，这可能会让生存变得更加困难。”

中国的导弹部队正在密切关注美国战略司令部，该司令部控制着核导弹，并表示希望使用人工智能。提升“决策能力”。中国军事分析人士也在研究美国常规部队如何使用人工智能。协调行动并挑选目标。

美国在制造先进芯片方面的优势加剧了中国的担忧，即美国可以更快地将人工智能纳入其中。华盛顿新美国安全中心高级研究员雅各布·斯托克斯表示，美国的军事行动包括核相关系统。

官方历史加剧了中国的焦虑。现任美国外交关系委员会国际事务研究员的布朗表示，中国军官研究了 20 世纪 50 年代的朝鲜战争和台湾危机，当时美国暗示可以向毛泽东的军队投掷原子弹，而当时毛泽东的军队还没有核武器。

中国已经使其核武器多样化，以增强其“生存能力”。

inline_images.alt: California Governor Gavin Newsom posted on X that President Trump has failed on AI safety while Cali

inline_images.caption: ‘Climate Change Is a Scam’: California Governor Gavin Newsom Faces Outrage After Declaring the State Will Continue to Lead the Nation While Trump Falls Behind
inline_images.alt: ‘Climate Change Is a Scam’: California Governor Gavin Newsom Faces Outrage After Declaring the State

author: Bloomberg
article_content:
California Governor Gavin Newsom posted on X that President Donald Trump has failed America on AI safety and that the state is moving forward with mandatory safety standards and real accountability, according to the message, which shared a video and linked to new recommendations for California’s AI framework. The post from California drew hundreds of replies, with many users pointing to Newsom’s 2024 veto of a major AI safety bill and the state’s record on large projects, while experts connected to the recommendations offered support for the proposals.

The video shows Newsom seated at a table in a suit, speaking to the camera. He states that “two-thirds of all the large AI companies in terms of market cap are in the state of California,” calling the state “the center of this debate” and “the center of the responsibility to address” the issue “in the absence of any federal leadership.”

He refers to recent incidents at Microsoft, the FAA, the NSA, banks, and Apple, asking, “Is this all coincidental?” and whether “there’s no one at the helm taking responsibility.” He adds that the administration’s main step has been “a desire to preempt states like California to actually create guardrails.”

The remarks accompany the November 18 release of recommendations from the California Governor’s Office to strengthen the state’s AI framework. These include baseline safety standards, mandatory third-party oversight, emergency shutdown authority, and limits on recursive self-improvement.

The proposals follow a September executive order and have not yet been enacted as law. Newsom vetoed SB 1047 in 2024, which would have required testing of large models for catastrophic risks.

Some users criticized Newsom’s record in California, with one writing, “Gavin Newsom has FAILED California on literally everything,” and another stating, “You can’t spell CATASTROPHE without CA. California is a 24/7 dumpster fire.”

Others focused on his earlier veto, noting, “This is exactly the problem: big talk about AI regulation, but when SB 1047 reached his desk, Newsom vetoed it.”

A number of replies questioned the state’s ability to manage the issue, including comments such as, “You are a failure to Californians,” and “Gavin can’t even keep the storm drains functional. Everything Gavin does turns into disaster.”

Experts tied to the recommendations offered a different view. Alondra Nelson, a former acting director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, said, “That irresponsible culture cannot continue. I was proud to work with Governor Newsom and his team to advance the same standard that Americans rightfully expect from every other sector: no experimenting on the public.”

Jason Goldman, who served as the first White House Chief Digital Officer, stated, “This report tackles the hardest open questions in AI safety regulation, including how emergency shutdown of a frontier model would work in practice.”

The exchange adds another moment to the ongoing debate over who should set rules for artificial intelligence as California advances its recommendations and federal policy remains limited.

article_content_zh:
加州州长加文·纽瑟姆 (Gavin Newsom) 在 X 上发帖称，唐纳德·特朗普总统在人工智能安全方面让美国失望，该州正在推进强制性安全标准和真正的问责制，该消息分享了一段视频，并链接了针对加州人工智能框架的新建议。加州的这篇帖子吸引了数百条回复，许多用户指出纽瑟姆在 2024 年否决了一项重大人工智能安全法案，以及该州在大型项目上的记录，而与这些建议相关的专家也为这些提案提供了支持。

视频显示，纽瑟姆穿着西装坐在桌子旁，对着镜头讲话。他表示，“就市值而言，所有大型人工智能公司的三分之二都在加利福尼亚州”，并称该州是“这场辩论的中心”，也是“在没有任何联邦领导的情况下解决问题的责任中心”。

他提到了最近在微软、美国联邦航空局、美国国家安全局、银行和苹果公司发生的事件，问道：“这都是巧合吗？”以及是否“没有人负责”。他补充说，政府的主要步骤是“希望先于加利福尼亚州等州实际建立护栏。”

加州州长办公室于 11 月 18 日发布了加强该州人工智能框架的建议，同时发表了上述言论。其中包括基线安全标准、强制性第三方监督、紧急关闭权限以及递归自我改进的限制。

这些提案是根据 9 月份的行政命令提出的，尚未颁布为法律。纽瑟姆在 2024 年否决了 SB 1047，该法案要求对大型模型进行灾难性风险测试。

一些用户批评纽瑟姆在加州的记录，其中一位写道，“加文·纽瑟姆几乎在所有事情上都让加州失败了”，另一位则写道，“没有加州，你就无法拼出灾难。加州是一场 24/7 的垃圾箱火灾。”

其他人则关注他之前的否决，并指出，“这正是问题所在：大肆谈论人工智能监管，但当 SB 1047 到达他的办公桌时，纽瑟姆否决了它。”

许多回复质疑该州处理这一问题的能力，包括诸如“加州人的失败”和“加文甚至无法保持雨水渠正常运转。加文所做的一切都会变成灾难”等评论。

与建议相关的专家提出了不同的观点。白宫科技政策办公室前代理主任阿隆德拉·尼尔森表示：“这种不负责任的文化不能继续下去。我很自豪能与纽瑟姆州长及其团队合作，推动美国人理所当然地期望其他行业遵守的标准：不对公众进行实验。”

担任白宫首任首席数字官的贾森·戈德曼 (Jason Goldman) 表示：“这份报告解决了人工智能安全监管中最棘手的开放性问题，包括前沿模型的紧急关闭在实践中如何运作。”

随着加州提出建议，而联邦政策仍然有限，此次交流又为正在进行的关于谁应该制定人工智能规则的争论增添了又一​​个时刻。

lead_paragraph: Chinese physical AI startup Simplexity Robotics received $100 million in a funding round led by Jack Ma-backed Ant Group Co., marking one of the fintech giant's most significant bets on next-generation embodied intelligence.
lead_paragraph_zh: 中国具身智能初创企业行者AI（Simplexity Robotics）完成新一轮1亿美元战略融资，由马云支持的蚂蚁集团领投，标志着这家金融科技巨头在下一代物理智能领域的重大战略布局。
paragraphs_zh: 中国具身智能初创企业行者AI（Simplexity Robotics）完成新一轮1亿美元战略融资，由马云支持的蚂蚁集团领投，标志着这家金融科技巨头在下一代物理智能领域的重大战略布局。
总部位于苏州的机器人创新领军企业在此次交易中发行了可转换优先股。此前，该公司的工业级双足与灵活移动操作机器人在真实制造车间完成了高强度作业验证，整体估值大幅攀升。
蚂蚁集团的此次重注凸显了中国科技行业向“物理人工智能（Physical AI）”加速渗透的宏观趋势，前沿软件大模型正与先进高精度执行器、多模态触觉末端及空间导航硬件深度融合。
行者AI计划将本轮资金重点投入通用人形机器人平台的规模化量产，并加速迭代面向复杂工业装配产线的专有强化学习具身大模型。
此项战略投资使蚂蚁集团与国内主流云厂商及风投机构形成共振，在欧美巨头消费级人形机器人商业化落地前夕，抢先锁定了核心物理AI生态与高价值工业资产。

author: Axios
article_content:
Compute Desk, a startup aiming to make compute an asset that can be traded and hedged, raised $45 million in a Lightspeed Venture Partners-led seed funding, CEO Andrawes Bahou tells Axios Pro exclusively.

Why it matters: The red-hot space is producing multiple well-capitalized startups, setting up a battle over how and who prices a compute market participants believe could be worth trillions.

author: Bloomberg
article_content:
China has warned that it will take action to defend its interests after US President Donald Trump's administration introduced tougher restrictions on advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips, escalating tensions over technology access just as the two countries prepare for high-level talks.The measures could also disrupt Southeast Asia's rapidly expanding technology industry, where billions of dollars are being invested in data centres powered by American-made processors.On Monday, 16 November, Washington announced that it would tighten controls on advanced semiconductors and overseas computing facilities that could give Chinese businesses access to restricted American technology, Reuters reported.On Tuesday, 17 November, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun condemned the restrictions as economic coercion, accusing Washington of interfering in normal trade and technological cooperation.

He said Beijing would take necessary measures to safeguard its legitimate and lawful rights and interests.Washington Targets Overseas Access to NVIDIA ChipsThe new regulations are intended to close a route through which Chinese companies have obtained access to powerful American processors without purchasing the hardware directly.

Although Washington already restricts sales of its most advanced AI chips to China, businesses there have been able to rent computing capacity from overseas data centres equipped with the technology.The latest restrictions require US export licences for covered advanced semiconductor shipments to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, countries Washington considers at higher risk of technology diversion.

The rule includes an exemption for shipments destined for US-headquartered companies, or businesses whose ultimate parent is based in the United States, provided specified reporting requirements are met.NVIDIA is particularly exposed because its processors are widely used to develop and train advanced AI systems.

The restrictions could complicate sales and infrastructure partnerships across the region, although the rules do not amount to a blanket prohibition on every shipment or data centre operation in the affected countries.Southeast Asia's $100 Billion AI Industry Faces UncertaintyThe market reaction was already apparent on Tuesday, 17 November, when investors sold shares in companies exposed to the region's data centre expansion.

Malaysia's MN Holdings and Critical Holdings each fell nearly 20 per cent, while YTL Power, an NVIDIA partner in AI infrastructure, dropped almost 10 per cent.The sell-off also spread to semiconductor suppliers and other technology-related companies across Asia, reflecting concerns about the potential impact of the new licensing requirements.The potential disruption is significant for a region that has attracted enormous investment in digital infrastructure.

Malaysia has recorded 385.7 billion ringgit (£71.5 billion) in data centre-related investments since 2021.Thailand, meanwhile, had attracted around $22.6 billion (£17.2 billion) in data centre investment by February 2026. Restrictions that delay equipment deliveries or make it harder to secure customers could undermine expansion plans and affect businesses supplying these facilities.Singapore Seeks Clarity From WashingtonSingapore is among the countries facing the new licensing requirements and has begun discussions with American officials about how the restrictions will be applied.

Its government said it was examining the regulations and assessing their implications for domestic businesses, while seeking arrangements that would allow legitimate companies to maintain access to advanced technology.Officials also stressed that Singapore would not tolerate businesses exploiting their presence in the country to evade foreign export restrictions.

The response reflects the challenge facing regional governments: protecting their growing technology industries while maintaining their relationships with Washington and complying with international trade requirements.

在美国总统唐纳德·特朗普政府对先进人工智能 (AI) 芯片实施更严格的限制后，中国警告称，将采取行动捍卫自己的利益，就在两国准备高层会谈之际，技术准入方面的紧张局势升级。这些措施还可能扰乱东南亚快速扩张的科技产业，该产业正在投资数十亿美元建设由美国制造的处理器驱动的数据中心。11 月 16 日星期一，华盛顿宣布将加强对先进半导体和海外计算设施的控制，这些设施可能使中国企业获得受限制的美国技术据路透社报道。11 月 17 日星期二，中国外交部发言人郭家琨谴责这些限制是经济胁迫，指责华盛顿干涉正常的贸易和技术合作。

他表示，北京将采取必要措施，维护自身正当合法权益。 华盛顿瞄准海外获取英伟达芯片的新规定，旨在切断中国企业在不直接购买硬件的情况下获得强大的美国处理器的途径。

尽管华盛顿已经限制向中国销售最先进的人工智能芯片，但那里的企业可以从配备该技术的海外数据中心租用计算能力。最新的限制要求向新加坡、马来西亚、泰国、印度尼西亚和巴西出口所涵盖的先进半导体需要美国的出口许可证，华盛顿认为这些国家的技术转移风险较高。

该规则包括对运往总部位于美国的公司或最终母公司位于美国的企业的货物进行豁免，前提是满足特定的报告要求。NVIDIA 受到的影响尤为严重，因为其处理器被广泛用于开发和训练先进的人工智能系统。

这些限制可能会使该地区的销售和基础设施合作关系变得复杂，尽管这些规则并不等于全面禁止受影响国家的每一次运输或数据中心运营。 东南亚价值 1000 亿美元的人工智能产业面临不确定性 11 月 17 日星期二，市场反应已经很明显，当时投资者出售了受该地区数据中心扩张影响的公司的股票。

马来西亚的 MN Holdings 和 Critical Holdings 均下跌近 20%，而 NVIDIA 在 AI 基础设施领域的合作伙伴 YTL Power 则下跌近 10%。抛售还蔓延到亚洲各地的半导体供应商和其他技术相关公司，反映出对新许可要求潜在影响的担忧。对于吸引了数字基础设施巨额投资的地区来说，潜在的破坏意义重大。

自 2021 年以来，马来西亚已记录了 3857 亿林吉特（715 亿英镑）的数据中心相关投资。与此同时，到 2026 年 2 月，泰国已吸引了约 226 亿美元（172 亿英镑）的数据中心投资。延迟设备交付或使其更难获得客户的限制可能会破坏扩张计划并影响供应这些设施的企业。新加坡寻求华盛顿的澄清新加坡是面临新形势的国家之一。许可要求，并已开始与美国官员讨论如何实施这些限制。

新加坡政府表示，正在审查这些法规并评估其对国内企业的影响，同时寻求允许合法公司继续获得先进技术的安排。官员们还强调，新加坡不会容忍企业利用其在该国的存在来逃避外国出口限制。

这一回应反映了地方政府面临的挑战：保护其不断发展的科技产业，同时维持与华盛顿的关系并遵守国际贸易要求。

title: Alecto raises $20M seed funding to make UK property law more accessible to consumers with AI
title_en: Alecto raises $20M seed funding to make UK property law more accessible to consumers with AI
author: Kyt Dotson
article_content:
Alecto Conveyancing Ltd., a London-based artificial intelligence-native law firm, today announced it raised $20 million in seed funding led by Insight Partners to make the law more accessible to the general public.

Firstminute Capital, Blue Lion Global, Andrena Ventures, FJ Labs, Antiportfolio Ventures, the Rigby Group and Mischon de Reya LLP also joined in the round. Angel investors participating in the round included Octopus Group Chief Executive and founder Simon Rogerson and SwiftKey founder John Reynolds.

Founded in September 2025 by CEO Will Rice (pictured), a serial entrepreneur who previously built fintech mortgage lender Gen H, Alecto’s first service targets the United Kingdom conveyancing market, the legal work required to buy and sell property. Rice drew on his experience building a mortgage company and decided to focus initially on bringing more people into ownership. With that expertise, Alecto aims to use AI to help give everyday people greater access to the law.

Alecto argues that traditional legal services are starved, with too few qualified attorneys and too few hours a day. Billing is based on hours, not outcomes and the service model doesn’t lean toward customers; this leads to unpredictable costs and a process that leaves customers in the dark.

The law firm said it’s using AI and legal experts to explain opaque legal processes in plain language and help clients make informed decisions. The company intends to target the property conveyancing market, which represents almost $3.3 billion in the U.K. alone, and aims to become the number one leader in property legal services by 2027.

“For too long, the legal industry has expected customers to work on its terms; now, AI presents the opportunity to put the consumer in control,” Rice said. “People don’t want to buy a lawyer’s time; they want results. Alecto exists to make the law accessible to everyone, giving control back to the consumer.”

Consumer legal services in the U.K. value growth pushed revenue over £55 billion, around $72.5 billion, in 2026, according to a report from Research and Markets. Business and commercial practices lead with 51% market value, followed by growth in the injury and conveyancing law markets.

“Property is where we prove the model. We’re building the technology and operations to rapidly break into new countries and new areas of law,” Rice added. “Ultimately, access to exceptional legal support should not depend on how much money you have or how confidently you can navigate the system.”

总部位于伦敦的人工智能本土律师事务所 Alecto Conveyancing Ltd. 今天宣布筹集了由 Insight Partners 牵头的 2000 万美元种子资金，以使公众更容易了解法律。

First 分钟资本、Blue Lion Global、Andrena Ventures、FJ Labs、Antiportfolio Ventures、Rigby Group 和 Mischon de Reya LLP 也参与了本轮融资。参与此轮融资的天使投资人包括 Octopus Group 首席执行官兼创始人 Simon Rogerson 和 SwiftKey 创始人 John Reynolds。

Alecto 由首席执行官 Will Rice（如图）于 2025 年 9 月创立，他是一位连续创业者，曾创立了金融科技抵押贷款公司 Gen H，其首项服务针对的是英国产权转让市场，即买卖房产所需的法律工作。赖斯借鉴了他建立抵押贷款公司的经验，决定首先专注于让更多的人拥有所有权。凭借这些专业知识，Alecto 旨在利用人工智能帮助普通人更好地接触法律。

阿莱克托认为，传统的法律服务匮乏，合格的律师太少，每天的工作时间也太少。计费基于时间，而不是结果，并且服务模式不倾向于客户；这会导致不可预测的成本以及让客户蒙在鼓里的过程。

该律师事务所表示，它正在利用人工智能和法律专家以通俗易懂的语言解释不透明的法律程序，并帮助客户做出明智的决定。该公司打算瞄准房地产转让市场，仅在英国该市场就价值近 33 亿美元，并计划到 2027 年成为房地产法律服务领域的第一大领导者。

“长期以来，法律行业一直期望客户按照其条款行事；现在，人工智能提供了让消费者掌控的机会，”赖斯说。 “人们不想花钱买律师的时间；他们想要的是结果。Alecto 的存在是为了让每个人都能接触到法律，将控制权交还给消费者。”

根据 Research and Markets 的一份报告，到 2026 年，英国消费者法律服务价值的增长将推动收入超过 550 亿英镑（约合 725 亿美元）。商业和商业惯例以 51% 的市场价值领先，其次是伤害和产权转让法律市场的增长。

“财产是我们证明模式的地方。我们正在开发技术和运营，以快速打入新的国家和新的法律领域，”赖斯补充道。 “最终，获得特殊法律支持不应取决于您有多少钱或您对系统的信心程度。”

title: South Korean PE firm MBK Partners agrees to take Japan's Wacom private, in a deal valuing the digital pen tech company at ~$860M, with Samsung participating (Kim Woo-young/CHOSUNBIZ)
title_en: South Korean PE firm MBK Partners agrees to take Japan's Wacom private, in a deal valuing the digital pen tech company at ~$860M, with Samsung participating (Kim Woo-young/CHOSUNBIZ)

inline_images.caption: The headquarters of MBK Partners in Jongno District, Seoul. /Courtesy of News1
inline_images.alt: The headquarters of MBK Partners in Jongno District, Seoul. /Courtesy of News1

author: CHOSUNBIZ
article_content:
Private equity firm MBK Partners will acquire Wacom, a Japanese company that supplies core technology for the Samsung Electronics(005930) Galaxy S Pen, in a deal valued at more than 1 trillion won.

MBK agreed to acquire Wacom and signed a tender offer agreement the previous day, the Nikkei and other outlets reported on the 21st.

The tender offer price is 1,030 yen (about 8,744 won) per share. The offer covers up to approximately 99.88% of the shares. If all are purchased, the total acquisition price will be about 136.6 billion yen (about 1.1597 trillion won). The tender offer is reportedly scheduled to begin in mid-February next year.

Samsung Electronics, which owns a 6.32% stake in Wacom, is also participating in the deal. Its Singapore subsidiary, Samsung Electronics Singapore (SESP), will tender its entire stake and then reinvest in the acquiring company's parent. After the reinvestment, Samsung Electronics is expected to hold a stake of about 6.3%.

Samsung Electronics has maintained a business partnership with Wacom since 2013 and reportedly plans to continue their technology and business cooperation after the deal.

The acquisition is a management buyout (MBO) involving Wacom's current management. An MBO is a transaction in which a company's management acquires the company where they work using outside funding.

Wacom CEO Ide Nobutaka plans to continue leading the company after the acquisition. MBK plans to increase Wacom's corporate value by strengthening its existing digital pen business, developing new technologies and expanding its operations.

Founded in 1983, Wacom specializes in making digital pens for drawing images on tablets and smartphones. It also supplies core technology for the S Pen used in Samsung Electronics' Galaxy series.

据《日经新闻》等媒体 21 日报道，MBK 同意收购 Wacom，并于前一天签署了要约收购协议。

要约收购价格为每股1,030日元（约合8,744韩元）。此次要约涵盖约99.88%的股份。如果全部收购，收购总价约为1366亿日元（约合11597亿韩元）。据报道，要约收购定于明年二月中旬开始。

拥有 Wacom 6.32% 股份的三星电子也参与了此次交易。其新加坡子公司三星电子新加坡（SESP）将出售其全部股权，然后再投资于收购公司的母公司。再投资后，三星电子预计将持股约6.3%。

三星电子自 2013 年以来一直与 Wacom 保持业务合作伙伴关系，据报道，三星电子计划在交易后继续双方的技术和业务合作。

此次收购属于管理层收购 (MBO)，涉及 Wacom 现任管理层。 MBO 是公司管理层利用外部资金收购其所在公司的交易。

Wacom 首席执行官 Ide Nobutaka 计划在收购后继续领导公司。 MBK 计划通过加强现有的数字笔业务、开发新技术和扩大业务来提高 Wacom 的企业价值。

Wacom 成立于 1983 年，专门生产用于在平板电脑和智能手机上绘制图像的数字笔。它还为三星电子 Galaxy 系列中使用的 S Pen 提供核心技术。

【起因与机理】强化数字笔核心业务价值并深挖与三星在Galaxy S Pen等产品线的技术深度绑定
【关键数据与实测】MBK Partners以1030日元/股价格启动MBO，交易总额达1.16万亿日元。
【各方立场与态度】交易预计于明年2月中旬启动要约收购，核心在于巩固S Pen技术壁垒。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] MBK Partners, Wacom, Samsung Electronics (Japanese capital market): Management Buyout (MBO) at 1,030 yen per share
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Strengthen core business value and solidify technical integration for Galaxy S Pen series

[Key Metrics] Samsung Electronics, a key strategic partner, will participate by tendering its current stake and reinvesting in the acquiring entity, retaining a roughly 6.3% stake to ensure ongoing technological collaboration.
[Key Position & Outlook] Tender offer begins mid-February, aimed at securing S Pen technical advantages.

title: BILL to Go Private in $6 Billion Acquisition Deal With TPG and Corpay
title_en: BILL to Go Private in $6 Billion Acquisition Deal With TPG and Corpay

inline_images.caption: BILL to Go Private in $6 Billion Acquisition Deal With TPG and Corpay (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_en: BILL to Go Private in $6 Billion Acquisition Deal With TPG and Corpay (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_zh: BILL to Go Private in $6 Billion Acquisition Deal With TPG and Corpay (摄影：路透社)
inline_images.alt: BILL to Go Private in $6 Billion Acquisition Deal With TPG and Corpay

author: Reuters
article_content:
BILL Holdings BILL has entered into a definitive agreement to be acquired by TPG, Inc. TPG, a global alternative asset management firm, in partnership with Corpay, Inc. CPAY. The all-cash transaction values BILL at approximately $6 billion, with shareholders set to receive $63.25 per share. The offer represents a 31% premium to BILL's 60-day volume-weighted average share price as of Nov. 16, 2026.

Under the agreement, TPG will acquire a majority interest in BILL through TPG Capital, the firm's U.S. and European private equity platform, while Corpay will acquire a minority stake. The partnership brings together TPG's technology investment and business-building experience with Corpay's expertise in payments and spend management. The companies aim to strengthen BILL's financial operations platform and expand its capabilities for small and midsize businesses.

The transaction was unanimously approved by BILL's board and is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals. The deal has no financing conditions attached. Following completion, BILL will become a privately held company and will no longer trade on a public stock exchange.

BILL's recent financial performance provides further context for the acquisition. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, total revenues increased 13% year over year to $353.8 million, while core revenue grew 14% to $316.4 million. The company served 475,300 businesses and processed $102 billion in payment volume, up 14% year over year. Non-GAAP operating income more than doubled to $136.9 million, reflecting improved operating efficiency.

BILL's integrated platform, growing payment volumes and improving profitability provide a solid foundation for future growth. The TPG-Corpay partnership could provide additional resources and expertise to support product innovation, AI development and long-term growth.

Over the past three months, shares of this Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) company have gained 29.8% against the industry's decline of 4%.

article_content_zh:
BILL Holdings BILL 已签订最终协议，将由全球另类资产管理公司 TPG, Inc. 与 Corpay, Inc. CPAY 合作收购。此次全现金交易对 BILL 的估值约为 60 亿美元，股东将获得每股 63.25 美元的收益。该要约较 BILL 截至 2026 年 11 月 16 日的 60 天成交量加权平均股价溢价 31%。

根据协议，TPG将通过该公司在美国和欧洲的私募股权平台TPG Capital收购BILL的多数股权，而Corpay将收购少数股权。此次合作将TPG的技术投资和业务建设经验与Corpay在支付和支出管理方面的专业知识结合起来。两家公司的目标是加强 BILL 的金融运营平台并扩大其针对中小企业的能力。

该交易获得了 BILL 董事会的一致批准，预计将于 2027 年上半年完成，但须获得股东和监管机构的批准。该交易不附加任何融资条件。完成后，BILL 将成为一家私人控股公司，并且将不再在公开证券交易所进行交易。

BILL 最近的财务业绩为此次收购提供了进一步的背景。 2027 财年第一季度，总收入同比增长 13%，达到 3.538 亿美元，核心收入增长 14%，达到 3.164 亿美元。该公司为 475,300 家企业提供服务，处理支付额 1020 亿美元，同比增长 14%。非 GAAP 运营收入增长了一倍多，达到 1.369 亿美元，反映出运营效率的提高。

BILL的集成平台、不断增长的支付量和不断提高的盈利能力为未来的增长奠定了坚实的基础。 TPG 与 Corpay 的合作伙伴关系可以提供额外的资源和专业知识，以支持产品创新、人工智能开发和长期增长。

title: Sources: Jay Clayton, director of national intelligence and AI czar, will also be acting national cyber director pending Kirsten A. Davies' Senate confirmation (Axios)
title_en: Sources: Jay Clayton, director of national intelligence and AI czar, will also be acting national cyber director pending Kirsten A. Davies' Senate confirmation (Axios)

inline_images.caption: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton greets Rep. Vince Fong after a House Homeland Security Committee hearing in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 18. Photo: C
inline_images.alt: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton greets Rep. Vince Fong after a House Homeland Security

author: Axios
article_content:
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton will also serve as acting national cyber director while Kirsten Davies awaits Senate confirmation to lead the office, Axios has learned.

Why it matters: Clayton, the nation's top intelligence official, will now coordinate cybersecurity policy as outages and reported cyberattacks expose vulnerabilities in America's digital infrastructure.

Catch up quick: President Trump announced Thursday he was tapping Davies, the Pentagon's chief information officer, to replace Sean Cairncross as national cyber director.

What they're saying: "I'm excited to work more with Kirsten, who has the experience and capabilities needed to help America navigate our increasingly complex and powerful digital infrastructure as our next National Cyber Director," Clayton said in a statement to Axios.

The big picture: Two critical national security roles will temporarily fall under one official as President Trump shakes up his cybersecurity team amid the growing threat of AI-powered attacks.

Driving the news: Clayton spent Sunday morning on CNN's "State of the Union," ABC's "This Week" and "Fox News Sunday," explaining recent technology disruptions and national security concerns.

Zoom in: Davies oversees the Pentagon's information technology and cybersecurity strategy, including efforts to modernize aging systems and protect military networks.

Behind the scenes: Clayton has already worked closely with the Office of the National Cyber Director, National Security Council, National Security Agency and other agencies through his AI leadership role, according to the White House official.

title: The Brother-Sister Duo Who Want to Keep Anthropic Weird
title_en: The Brother-Sister Duo Who Want to Keep Anthropic Weird

inline_images.caption: The Brother-Sister Duo Who Want to Keep Anthropic Weird (Source: Wall Street Journal)
inline_images.caption_en: The Brother-Sister Duo Who Want to Keep Anthropic Weird (Source: Wall Street Journal)
inline_images.caption_zh: The Brother-Sister Duo Who Want to Keep Anthropic Weird (来源：华尔街日报)
inline_images.alt: The Brother-Sister Duo Who Want to Keep Anthropic Weird

author: Berber Jin and Maxwell Zeff and Keach Hagey
article_content:
Two years before she pulled off the largest public offering of all time, Daniela Amodei gathered everyone at Anthropic in a 16-acre garden on a sweltering fall day near the Santa Cruz mountains.

The AI company now with a market value of roughly $1.18 trillion was at the time still a young startup that Amodei and her big brother, Dario, had co-founded with five friends. It was undergoing a hiring spree and Daniela was worried. So they carted 10-foot-tall bookshelves onto the grass to make reading nooks, played games and made friendship bracelets. As the company’s president, and keeper of its culture, the younger Amodei wanted to deliver a message.

“Keep Anthropic weird,” Daniela told them.

Anthropic embraces being atypical because it believes the artificial intelligence future will be anything but normal. Many co-founders meet in college, or at a first job. This pair met when he was 4 and she was born.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and President Daniela Amodei have defended the artificial intelligence (AI) company's massive infrastructure commitments and reiterated their focus on responsible AI development, saying its record-breaking initial public offering (IPO) will not change its long-term mission.

Speaking to CNBC International ahead of Anthropic's Nasdaq debut, the siblings addressed the company's $900 billion AI commitments, its approach to balancing growth with safety, partnerships with major technology companies and its relationship with the US government.

Daniela Amodei described the IPO as a significant milestone but said the company would remain focused on its original objectives.

Addressing questions around Anthropic's substantial AI infrastructure spending, Dario Amodei defended commitments of around $900 billion, arguing that they should be viewed in the context of the company's cash reserves and growing revenue.

Amodei added that Anthropic tries to "err on the low side" when forecasting its computing requirements.

He also acknowledged the challenge of balancing the pace of AI development with safety considerations, describing it as one of the company's central tensions.

"What we've done with pacing is essentially said, look, we could drive at 200 miles an hour. Maybe let's only drive at 90 miles an hour. Spend time figuring out how to do that safely, and the rest of that surplus we spend building the model in the right way," he said.

On the expectations surrounding Anthropic's public market debut, Amodei said the company was keeping its focus on execution rather than the spotlight.

"We've been calm about it," he said, adding that Anthropic's approach was to "always want to under promise and over deliver".

Daniela Amodei said safety remained central to Anthropic's approach, arguing that the potential benefits of AI must be balanced against the risks associated with the technology.

"The promise is incredible, and the risks are real. And we were really founded on this idea that it is our job to mitigate those risks," she said, adding that the company remained deeply committed to safety.

She also highlighted Anthropic's public benefit structure, saying the company wanted its economic value and broader mission to be embedded in its organisational framework.

On data centre expansion, Daniela said Anthropic would need to listen to local communities and take their concerns into account.

Dario Amodei described Anthropic's relationship with Nvidia as a "long and productive partnership". He also expressed satisfaction with its work with SpaceX amid speculation about whether the company could scale back its use of the Elon Musk-led company's computing capacity.

"We're finding that compute to be high quality. We're enjoying working with SpaceX," he said.

On Anthropic's differences with the US Department of Defense, Daniela Amodei said there were no significant updates but expected the company's relationship with the government to continue.

She said Anthropic had worked closely with the US national security establishment since its founding and remained committed to ensuring that its Claude AI models could help protect the country.

Dario Amodei also said Anthropic hoped to secure an investment-grade credit rating in the future, adding that debt was an instrument the company would like to use at some point.

Anthropic is set for its Nasdaq debut on Thursday after raising more than $81 billion in a record-breaking IPO, surpassing SpaceX's offering in June.

The Claude creator sold 980 million shares at $83 apiece on Wednesday, taking its fully diluted market capitalisation to around $1.5 trillion.

The five-year-old company has seen rapid growth on the back of its Claude AI models and products. According to its prospectus, Anthropic generated $33.24 billion in revenue in the nine months ended September 30, up 1,200% from the same period last year.

Speaking at Nasdaq, Amodei highlighted AI's potential to advance medicine and help cure diseases, while reiterating the importance of responsible development.

"Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so, only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing," he said.

"If we can show it's possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same," he added.

article_content_zh:
两年前，丹妮拉·阿莫代 (Daniela Amodei) 在圣克鲁斯山脉附近一个闷热的秋日，将 Anthropic 的所有人聚集在一个 16 英亩的花园里，完成了有史以来最大规模的公开募股。

这家目前市值约为 1.18 万亿美元的人工智能公司当时还是一家年轻的初创公司，由 Amodei 和她的哥哥 Dario 以及五个朋友共同创立。该公司正在大肆招聘，丹妮拉很担心。于是，他们把 10 英尺高的书架搬到草地上，作为阅读角，玩游戏，制作友谊手链。作为公司总裁和公司文化的守护者，年轻的阿莫代想要传达一个信息。

“让人类保持奇怪，”丹妮拉告诉他们。

Anthropic 拥抱非典型，因为它相信人工智能的未来绝不会是正常的。许多联合创始人是在大学或第一份工作中认识的。这对夫妇在他四岁时相遇，她出生了。

title: The Brother-Sister Duo Who Want to Keep Anthropic Weird
title_en: The Brother-Sister Duo Who Want to Keep Anthropic Weird

inline_images.caption: The Brother-Sister Duo Who Want to Keep Anthropic Weird (Source: Wall Street Journal)
inline_images.caption_en: The Brother-Sister Duo Who Want to Keep Anthropic Weird (Source: Wall Street Journal)
inline_images.caption_zh: The Brother-Sister Duo Who Want to Keep Anthropic Weird (来源：华尔街日报)
inline_images.alt: The Brother-Sister Duo Who Want to Keep Anthropic Weird

author: Berber Jin and Maxwell Zeff and Keach Hagey
article_content:
Two years before she pulled off the largest public offering of all time, Daniela Amodei gathered everyone at Anthropic in a 16-acre garden on a sweltering fall day near the Santa Cruz mountains.

The AI company now with a market value of roughly $1.18 trillion was at the time still a young startup that Amodei and her big brother, Dario, had co-founded with five friends. It was undergoing a hiring spree and Daniela was worried. So they carted 10-foot-tall bookshelves onto the grass to make reading nooks, played games and made friendship bracelets. As the company’s president, and keeper of its culture, the younger Amodei wanted to deliver a message.

“Keep Anthropic weird,” Daniela told them.

Anthropic embraces being atypical because it believes the artificial intelligence future will be anything but normal. Many co-founders meet in college, or at a first job. This pair met when he was 4 and she was born.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and President Daniela Amodei have defended the artificial intelligence (AI) company's massive infrastructure commitments and reiterated their focus on responsible AI development, saying its record-breaking initial public offering (IPO) will not change its long-term mission.

Speaking to CNBC International ahead of Anthropic's Nasdaq debut, the siblings addressed the company's $900 billion AI commitments, its approach to balancing growth with safety, partnerships with major technology companies and its relationship with the US government.

Daniela Amodei described the IPO as a significant milestone but said the company would remain focused on its original objectives.

Addressing questions around Anthropic's substantial AI infrastructure spending, Dario Amodei defended commitments of around $900 billion, arguing that they should be viewed in the context of the company's cash reserves and growing revenue.

Amodei added that Anthropic tries to "err on the low side" when forecasting its computing requirements.

He also acknowledged the challenge of balancing the pace of AI development with safety considerations, describing it as one of the company's central tensions.

"What we've done with pacing is essentially said, look, we could drive at 200 miles an hour. Maybe let's only drive at 90 miles an hour. Spend time figuring out how to do that safely, and the rest of that surplus we spend building the model in the right way," he said.

On the expectations surrounding Anthropic's public market debut, Amodei said the company was keeping its focus on execution rather than the spotlight.

"We've been calm about it," he said, adding that Anthropic's approach was to "always want to under promise and over deliver".

Daniela Amodei said safety remained central to Anthropic's approach, arguing that the potential benefits of AI must be balanced against the risks associated with the technology.

"The promise is incredible, and the risks are real. And we were really founded on this idea that it is our job to mitigate those risks," she said, adding that the company remained deeply committed to safety.

She also highlighted Anthropic's public benefit structure, saying the company wanted its economic value and broader mission to be embedded in its organisational framework.

On data centre expansion, Daniela said Anthropic would need to listen to local communities and take their concerns into account.

Dario Amodei described Anthropic's relationship with Nvidia as a "long and productive partnership". He also expressed satisfaction with its work with SpaceX amid speculation about whether the company could scale back its use of the Elon Musk-led company's computing capacity.

"We're finding that compute to be high quality. We're enjoying working with SpaceX," he said.

On Anthropic's differences with the US Department of Defense, Daniela Amodei said there were no significant updates but expected the company's relationship with the government to continue.

She said Anthropic had worked closely with the US national security establishment since its founding and remained committed to ensuring that its Claude AI models could help protect the country.

Dario Amodei also said Anthropic hoped to secure an investment-grade credit rating in the future, adding that debt was an instrument the company would like to use at some point.

Anthropic is set for its Nasdaq debut on Thursday after raising more than $81 billion in a record-breaking IPO, surpassing SpaceX's offering in June.

The Claude creator sold 980 million shares at $83 apiece on Wednesday, taking its fully diluted market capitalisation to around $1.5 trillion.

The five-year-old company has seen rapid growth on the back of its Claude AI models and products. According to its prospectus, Anthropic generated $33.24 billion in revenue in the nine months ended September 30, up 1,200% from the same period last year.

Speaking at Nasdaq, Amodei highlighted AI's potential to advance medicine and help cure diseases, while reiterating the importance of responsible development.

"Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so, only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing," he said.

"If we can show it's possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same," he added.

title: U.S. Tracked Alice Huang’s Contacts With China Spy Agency During Nvidia Affair
title_en: U.S. Tracked Alice Huang’s Contacts With China Spy Agency During Nvidia Affair

inline_images.caption: Mr. Huang resigned as chief executive of Nvidia this month after reports surfaced involving affairs with two women. (Eric Lee for The New York Times)
inline_images.alt: Mr. Huang resigned as chief executive of Nvidia this month after reports surfaced involving affairs with two women.

inline_images.caption: Mr. Huang with President Trump in Washington in early October. Nvidia’s board has rejected the president’s suggestion that it reinstate Mr. Huang as the head of the company. (Demetrius Freeman for The New York Times)
inline_images.alt: Mr. Huang with President Trump in Washington in early October. Nvidia’s board has rejected the president’s suggestion that it reinstate Mr. Huang as the head of the company.

author: Jonathan Swan, Julian E. Barnes, and Maggie Haberman
article_content:
The Chinese woman at the heart of the Nvidia scandal kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year while she was carrying out a secret affair with Jensen Huang, according to multiple people with knowledge of U.S. intelligence reports that describe the encounters.

The woman, Alice Huang, was in touch with an officer of China’s Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the people with knowledge of the intelligence said. That period overlaps with at least a portion of the time she was in a relationship with Mr. Huang, then the head of the world’s leading maker of advanced artificial intelligence chips.

U.S. intelligence agencies have also gathered evidence that Ms. Huang’s business partner, Kang Wei, who was often introduced as her husband, worked with the same Chinese spy agency, the people said.

The extent and specific timing of Ms. Huang’s contacts with the spy agency — and Mr. Kang’s work for the same intelligence service — have not been previously reported.

Ms. Huang’s contacts with the Chinese spy agency last year and up through recent months help to flesh out how U.S. officials came to believe that Mr. Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive earlier this month, was the target of an intelligence operation.

They correspond not just to the time when he was conducting the affair but also to at least part of the period when Ms. Huang’s company, Megaspeed, was acquiring large amounts of advanced Nvidia chips, some of which went to data centers in Southeast Asia serving Chinese technology companies like Alibaba and some of which are suspected of being smuggled to China.

Allies of the former Nvidia chief, including President Trump, have sought to minimize the scandal and questioned whether Ms. Huang was spying for Chinese intelligence. But the newly revealed information underscores the continuous contacts that she had with the Ministry of State Security, even as she was in a romantic relationship with Mr. Huang.

It also helps to flesh out why some American officials have been worried that Ms. Huang’s role is just one element of a much broader push by China in that technological battle. The Ministry of State Security has prioritized focusing on acquiring high-end chips and advancing China’s A.I. ambitions.

U.S. officials are investigating the role of Ms. Huang and Mr. Kang in a network of Southeast Asian companies, including Megaspeed, that have been linked to the possible smuggling of Nvidia chips to China, to evade U.S. export control laws. U.S. officials are still working to determine the full extent and duration of their work with Chinese intelligence.

The intelligence gathered by the U.S. contains evidence — including shipping records — demonstrating the role of Ms. Huang and Mr. Kang in that network of companies, people with knowledge of the intelligence reports said. The New York Times has previously reported that Ms. Huang and her family have a web of connections to Chinese defense contractors.

Mr. Huang initially described his relationship with Ms. Huang as normal interactions with a business customer. He acknowledged an affair only after The Times revealed last month that Ms. Huang had been identified by the United States as a Chinese intelligence asset and that the Nvidia chief had been picked up on electronic surveillance targeting her.

He stepped down this month after The Times subsequently reported that he had an affair with a subordinate at Nvidia. Administration officials never provided him with a so-called defensive briefing about Ms. Huang, a heads-up that the woman he was in a relationship with had been linked to Chinese intelligence.

A spokesman for Mr. Huang declined to comment. The White House, the State Department, the Chinese Embassy in Washington, Ms. Huang and Mr. Kang did not respond to requests for comment on Sunday.

Before the scandal broke into public view, advisers to Mr. Trump told him on at least two occasions that U.S. intelligence had uncovered Ms. Huang’s links to the Chinese spy agency and that she was in a close relationship with Mr. Huang while he was still running Nvidia, according to U.S. officials with direct knowledge of the briefings.

Both times, including when his national security adviser discussed it with him, the president downplayed the concerns and made clear he did not want to intervene in the matter. The officials said Mr. Trump regarded Mr. Huang as a valuable ally and Nvidia as essential to the health of the American economy and stock market. Mr. Trump has recently suggested that Nvidia should consider bringing Mr. Huang back as chief executive, a possibility the company’s board has rejected.

“We have to protect our brilliant people. Jensen is one of them,” the president said at a White House news conference on Friday. “I think the company if they were smart they’d take that brilliant man, accept an apology and let him go back to work.”

Mr. Trump has claimed that no one in his government told him of any intelligence indicating that Ms. Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset.

“I don’t know that she is a spy,” he said. “Usually, what happens with that is that any woman coming to the country that’s a beautiful woman that comes from China, they say she’s a spy.”

In fact, his administration has been monitoring Ms. Huang’s contacts with the Chinese spy agency for more than a year, a period when the Ministry of State Security has been intensifying its new role in seeking to give China an advantage in artificial intelligence.

“This network of companies working to procure and smuggle Nvidia chips lines up precisely with the M.S.S.’s recently stated core mission of circumventing and undermining U.S. export controls on semiconductors and other key technologies,” said Matt Pottinger, who served as deputy national security adviser during Mr. Trump’s first term, and who is chief executive of the open-source research firm Garnaut Global.

The Ministry of State Security has for decades declared that its mission is to combat espionage and to eliminate political threats to Communist Party rule in China. The minister of state security, Chen Yixin, gave a similar five-point statement as recently as late last year. Then in April, he unveiled a new, sixth mission — overcoming the “blockades” choking China’s access to key technologies like artificial intelligence.

“Deepen the struggle against blockades, and comprehensively advance artificial intelligence innovation, industry development and applications,” Mr. Chen wrote in a party journal. “Focus on tackling the ‘choke holds’ of critical technologies.”

“To assume the M.S.S. wasn’t at the center of this operation would be to assume that they are incompetent,” Mr. Pottinger added. “That’s not an assumption I would make.”

American spy agencies are still working to understand the role played by Mr. Kang, the business partner of Ms. Huang, whom she would introduce to associates as her husband. Multiple people with knowledge of the intelligence said the United States had collected evidence that Mr. Kang worked with the Ministry of State Security.

Ms. Huang also appears to have met with officials of China’s Ministry of Public Security, the nation’s main law enforcement agency, according to multiple people with knowledge of the U.S. intelligence reports.

Ms. Huang, Mr. Kang, Ms. Huang’s sister and companies associated with them have emerged as a significant branch of the Chinese effort to build data centers and acquire access to Nvidia chips to train powerful A.I. models. Ms. Huang’s network has been linked to efforts to supply the powerful chips to Chinese-state owned military contractors doing work for the People’s Liberation Army.

Little of the intelligence about Ms. Huang and her network has been provided to Capitol Hill, but lawmakers from both parties are demanding briefings.

A briefing this month for top lawmakers by John Ratcliffe, the C.I.A. director, and Jay Clayton, the director of national intelligence, was originally scheduled to discuss Iran, but The Times’s reporting on Nvidia led the lawmakers to ask questions about Mr. Huang and Alice Huang. Their answers raised more questions and left some lawmakers puzzled.

Trump administration officials postponed a follow-up briefing for top national security staffers scheduled for last Wednesday, in which senior officials were set to share details of the intelligence collected on Ms. Huang.

The intelligence about Ms. Huang was closely held inside the government until The Times reported the existence of the information in late October. Behind the scenes, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who is also the national security adviser, had written a confidential memo, dated March 30 this year, laying out Ms. Huang’s ties to Chinese intelligence.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 美国情报报告显示，英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋的绯闻对象爱丽丝·黄（Alice Huang）在2025年春季至2024年秋季期间，长期与中国国家安全部人员保持联系。调查指出，爱丽丝·黄及其商业伙伴康伟（Kang Wei）利用其控股的Megaspeed公司，构建了复杂的供应链网络，不仅将先进英伟达芯片分销至东南亚数据中心，更涉及向中国境内非法转移管控级别的高性能计算芯片。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: U.S. intelligence reports reveal that Alice Huang, a central figure in the scandal involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, maintained consistent contact with Chinese Ministry of State Security officers from spring 2025 through autumn 2024. Investigations indicate that she and her business associate, Kang Wei, utilized their company, Megaspeed, to create a supply chain network that diverted advanced Nvidia chips to Southeast Asian data centers and potentially smuggled restricted hardware into China.

elements_zh.who: 爱丽丝·黄（Alice Huang）、康伟（Kang Wei）、黄仁勋（前英伟达CEO）
elements_zh.where: 涉及东南亚数据中心与中美跨境技术供应链
elements_zh.what: 长期与外国情报机构接触，涉嫌绕过出口管制非法转运高性能AI芯片
elements_zh.why: 利用私人情感关系渗透关键半导体行业领导层，以获取中国AI算力战略资源

elements_en.who: Alice Huang, Kang Wei, Jensen Huang (Former Nvidia CEO)
elements_en.where: Southeast Asian data centers and cross-border tech supply chain
elements_en.what: Maintained intelligence contacts and facilitated illicit transfers of restricted high-end AI chips
elements_en.why: Leveraging personal relationships to compromise semiconductor leadership to advance China's AI compute ambitions

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此事件标志着美国对半导体供应链的审查已从单纯的财务合规深入至私人关系与情报层面的穿透性调查。英伟达前CEO的私生活不仅引发企业管治危机，更直接暴露了先进算力出口管制体系中的‘灰色转运’漏洞，预计美国商务部将针对东南亚区域算力节点实施更为严苛的终端用户审查。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This incident signifies a shift in U.S. semiconductor supply chain oversight from financial compliance to deep-tissue intelligence and personnel security investigations. The exposure of these 'gray-market' diversion channels will likely prompt the U.S. Department of Commerce to enforce significantly more stringent end-user verification protocols for AI compute clusters deployed in Southeast Asia.

article_content_zh:
据多位了解美国情报报告的人士透露，这位英伟达丑闻核心的中国女性在与黄仁勋进行秘密恋情期间，与中国最高间谍机构的一名官员保持了一年多的联系。

知情人士称，这名女子名叫 Alice Huang，从 2025 年春季到今年秋季一直与中国国家安全部的一名官员保持联系。那段时期至少有一部分时间与她与时任全球领先先进人工智能芯片制造商负责人的黄先生交往的时间重叠。

知情人士称，美国情报机构还收集了黄女士的商业伙伴康伟（经常被介绍为黄女士的丈夫）与同一家中国间谍机构合作的证据。

黄女士与该间谍机构接触的程度和具体时间以及康先生为同一情报机构工作的情况此前并未报道过。

黄女士去年和最近几个月与中国间谍机构的接触有助于充实美国官员如何相信本月早些时候辞去英伟达首席执行官职务的黄先生是情报行动的目标。

它们不仅与他进行这起事件的时间相符，而且至少与黄女士的公司 Megaspeed 收购大量先进的英伟达芯片的时期相符，其中一些芯片被运往东南亚的数据中心，为阿里巴巴等中国科技公司提供服务，其中一些芯片涉嫌走私到中国。

包括特朗普总统在内的英伟达前首席执行官的盟友一直试图将丑闻最小化，并质疑黄女士是否在为中国情报部门进行间谍活动。但新披露的信息突显了她与国家安全部的持续接触，尽管她与黄先生处于恋爱关系。

这也有助于解释为什么一些美国官员一直担心黄女士的角色只是中国在这场技术战中更广泛推动的一个因素。国家安全部优先关注高端芯片和推进中国人工智能发展。野心。

美国官员正在调查黄女士和康先生在包括 Megaspeed 在内的东南亚公司网络中所扮演的角色，这些公司可能与将英伟达芯片走私到中国有关，以逃避美国出口管制法。美国官员仍在努力确定他们与中国情报部门合作的全部范围和持续时间。

了解情报的人士称，美国收集的情报包含的证据（包括运输记录）证明了黄女士和康先生在该公司网络中的作用。 《纽约时报》此前曾报道称，黄女士及其家人与中国国防承包商有着广泛的关系网。

黄先生最初将他与黄女士的关系描述为与商业客户的正常互动。上个月，《泰晤士报》披露黄女士已被美国认定为中国情报人员，并且英伟达首席执行官因针对她的电子监控而被捕后，他才承认了这一事件。

在《泰晤士报》随后报道他与英伟达的一名下属有染后，他于本月辞职。政府官员从未向他提供过有关黄女士的所谓防御性简报，即与他有关系的那位女士与中国情报部门有联系。

黄先生的发言人拒绝置评。白宫、国务院、中国驻华盛顿大使馆、黄女士和康先生周日没有回应置评请求。

据直接了解简报的美国官员透露，在丑闻进入公众视野之前，特朗普的顾问至少两次告诉他，美国情报部门已经发现了黄女士与中国间谍机构的联系，并且在黄先生仍在管理英伟达期间，她与黄先生关系密切。

title: Inside an AI prophet’s secretive visions for humanity’s future
title_en: Inside an AI prophet’s secretive visions for humanity’s future

inline_images.alt: Inside an AI prophet’s secretive visions for humanity’s future

author: Nitasha Tiku
article_content:
SAN FRANCISCO — As Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei regaled investors last month with his artificial intelligence company’s plans for future products, a very different meeting unfolded elsewhere in the company’s headquarters.

Anthropic had invited more than a dozen academics, think tank fellows and media figures for briefings from senior staff on how society should navigate the rise of powerful AI. Guests were asked to first read an essay by Amodei that argued that AI was advancing dangerously fast, and the 23,000-word “constitution” that guides his company’s chatbot with statements like “Claude should not even tell white lies.”

In a 10th floor conference room down the hall from a built-in barista bar, attendees recalled, Anthropic staff described how AI was increasingly able to improve itself and that teaching machines morals might stop them from becoming harmful. “They feel it’s going to be a transformative event for humanity and society needs to be prepared,” said New York University economist Arpit Gupta, who joined the two-day program. “I got the sense that they’re not happy with the public discourse” about AI, he said, and want to change it.
