article_content_zh:
安全消息服务 Signal 表示，将限制智能手机上的屏幕截图功能，以防止人工智能代理读取私人对话。 Signal在当地时间20日发表的博文中指出，直接内置于操作系统（OS）中的人工智能功能正在以应用程序开发者无法控制的方式访问设备数据，并要求苹果、谷歌和微软等平台运营商提供具体的拦截工具。

Signal 本身也承认该措施并不完整。该公司表示：“当前的代理人工智能集成浪潮正在创造一个对隐私越来越敌视的环境。”并称其“对 Signal 以及我们维护使命的能力构成了生存威胁”。它补充说，“操作系统管理着像 Signal 这样的应用程序必须存在的环境。”

最令人担忧的是深度集成到操作系统中的人工智能，例如苹果的 Siri AI 或谷歌的 Gemini Intelligence。根据 Signal 的说法，这些代理可以读取屏幕上显示的内容，并据此代表用户采取行动，这意味着受端到端加密保护的 Signal 消息可以被提取到加密环境之外。该公司指出，人工智能扫描屏幕的那一刻，Signal 的安全环境就被瓦解了。

通过这一措施，Signal 将引入一项设置，阻止用户设备上的屏幕截图访问，并默认将其打开。当 Signal 检测到屏幕截图尝试或人工智能助手的屏幕访问时，它会显示一个弹出窗口，让用户根据设备类型解除阻止。去年，Signal 还阻止了微软的 Recall AI 在 Windows 上进行屏幕截图。然而，它表示这种保护很难在苹果的 macOS 上可靠地提供。

Signal 的担忧得到了最近证实的现实案例的支持。经证实，Meta 的 AI 代理 Muse 绕过官方集成工具访问苹果电脑和谷歌 Android 智能手机上的 Signal 消息。 Muse 使用应用程序初始设置期间授予的广泛操作系统级权限以用户意想不到的方式提取消息。在 Apple 的 macOS 上，它将辅助工具与屏幕截图功能结合起来，以捕获 Signal 对话、从图像中提取文本并在 Muse 应用程序中重现它。

Meta 反驳说，代理必须能够查看计算机并与计算机交互才能代表用户行事，并且 Muse 只能通过用户明确授予的权限访问其他应用程序。苹果通过本周发布的操作系统更新阻止了这条道路，但同时推出了一个针对代理的新权限系统，该系统允许类似的功能，但会发出额外的警告。

Signal 敦促为应用程序开发人员提供一种明确的方法，将他们的应用程序完全排除在人工智能助手的数据处理之外，包括屏幕阅读、通知和文件系统访问。 Signal 由非营利基金会运营，最大限度地减少了服务器上存储的数据，排除了广告并提供了端到端加密。该公司的判断是，当人工智能扫描屏幕时，这些保护措施就会失效。

这个问题出现之际，苹果正在加速开发自己的人工智能代理。在最近的招聘启事中，苹果披露了开发一种通用人工智能代理的计划，该代理可以像人类一样处理计算机，执行网络搜索、编码、应用程序控制和多个子代理的协调。它正在考虑最早于明年年底推出，但开发仍处于早期阶段。据称，苹果首席执行官 John Ternus 已敦促软件工程高级副总裁 Craig Federighi 更快、更大胆地推动人工智能战略。

竞争格局也在迅速升温。 Meta 的 Muse 在苹果应用商店免费应用程序中排名第二，具有餐厅和旅行预订以及新闻简报功能，而 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 和 Anthropic 的 Claude 也位列前五。 Anthropic 扩大了其代理 Duet 的用户测试，OpenAI 为 Dots 添加了功能，谷歌本周彻底修改了其代理任务。苹果开发人工智能代理的消息传出后，盘后交易中 Meta 股价下跌约 2%，Anthropic 股价下跌超过 3%。

市场预计平台运营商和隐私应用程序之间的紧张关系将进一步加剧。平台可以控制操作系统集成的人工智能访问其他应用程序数据的路径这一事实表明，人工智能代理时代的竞争力不仅取决于模型性能，还取决于操作系统级别的访问权限设计。苹果已经被美国司法部起诉，包括指控其阻止竞争对手访问功能和硬件，因此人们的注意力集中在 Signal 的要求将如何得到体现。 Signal 评估称，在苹果即将推出的 iOS 27.3 中，Siri 将能够通过外部应用程序叫车或预订餐厅，但这距离跨多个应用程序并自行处理复杂任务的完整代理还很远。

title: Regular Tech Bros Are Worried About Honeypots
title_en: Regular Tech Bros Are Worried About Honeypots
author: Kate Taylor and Caroline Haskins
article_content:
When the founder of a cybersecurity firm hired Blaine Anderson as a matchmaker, it wasn’t just because the man was lonely. It was also, Anderson says, because he was “super worried about spies.”

The cybersecurity founder isn’t the only one. As Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged asset of China’s Ministry of State Security dominates headlines and AI companies reportedly warn employees against “honeypots,” matchmakers say that more men with pretty normal lives are worried that their dates may have ulterior motives: accessing corporate secrets.

“Even if you're not a CEO or at a big tech giant, these fears have trickled down to just regular professionals,” Simone Grossman, a Brooklyn-based matchmaker, tells WIRED.

One tech worker, who requested anonymity in order to speak candidly, says he considers himself “highly selective” about the people he interacts with face-to-face.

“Even though I could vet you from looking you up online, I can't help but still be a tad dubious,” he tells WIRED. On a scale from zero to 10, with 10 being the most anxious about espionage, he puts himself at a seven.

Even though the vast majority of tech employees likely won’t be targeted for romantic espionage, matchmakers say more clients have lately expressed concerns about women exploiting them for their corporate secrets. One Palantir employee told Andersen he wouldn’t date anyone who was a Chinese or Russian national. The anxiety has even become a marketing opportunity: One company is pitching its new line of AI executive girlfriends as a “zero espionage” alternative to human dating.

The concern isn’t entirely without basis. Some companies hire consultants to advise executives and lower-level employees with access to sensitive information on security risks, including the possibility of honeypots. Several of these consultants tell WIRED that raising the subject can be awkward.

“This one is always a very difficult message to deliver—to explain to, say, very sensitive engineers that maybe they're getting a lot of email attention because of their job,” says Isaac Stone Fish, founder and chief executive of the business intelligence firm Strategy Risks, “as opposed to the charm and force of their personality.”

Amy Andersen, founder of Silicon Valley matchmaking company Linx Dating (and no relation to Blaine Anderson), says that for clients concerned about their romantic partners’ intentions, she offers background checks, personal vetting, and NDAs. The security features are part of her “bespoke” packages that range anywhere from $75,000 to more than $500,000 for the “Founders Level.”

Fear of romantic espionage is just the latest manifestation of growing distrust in the dating world. Shannon Lundgren, a matchmaker who has worked in San Francisco for 15 years, says that while she hasn’t necessarily heard more concerns about honeypots, she has noticed heightened skepticism around dating in general, as well as growing concerns about privacy.

The anxiety is particularly acute among AI workers, whose net worths—and therefore their perceived romantic desirability—are on the rise.

“If you're somebody who is a little bit shy or who is maybe a very stereotypical engineer type, to suddenly have your market value in the dating world change so drastically—you're already suspicious,” Grossman says.

To be worried about corporate espionage on top of all that, she says, is “a mind fuck.”

Honeypots and their state or corporate sponsors often look for “signs of vulnerability, such as an unhappy marriage, or someone seeking “excitement or adventure,” says Ira Winkler, a security consultant and the chief information security officer in residence at identity protection company Cloaked. Lonely people are opportune targets, regardless of marriage or relationship status.

The advice security experts give is somewhat obvious: If it seems too good to be true, it probably is.

“Really, if a beautiful woman approaches you, you know it's not for your personality,” Winkler tells his clients.

When tech workers do think of honeypots, they may gravitate toward the stereotype of a beautiful stranger who seduces someone at a bar and then extracts company secrets. “Any time one of us would take a trip to Asia, someone would always make a comment about getting a foreign girlfriend, or future wife, etc.,” one tech worker tells WIRED about his experience at a majority-male workplace. “We'd joke about them meeting a spy, but nobody really considered that seriously. Mostly they were just thinking of sex.”

That setup is largely a misconception. In reality, according to Greg Rinckey, founding partner of the legal services and consulting firm Tully Rinckey, most honeypot victims are groomed over time. “We’re talking sometimes months, could be years, where they're fostering that relationship,” he says. Rinckey compares it to scammers trying to keep victims on the phone: The longer someone talks to another person and feels they know them, the more likely they are to trust them with sensitive information.

Catherine Marinis-Yaqub, a principal at the crisis and security consulting group Control Risks, tells WIRED that when people imagine the beautiful stranger at a bar, they may miss more likely scenarios, like an unexpected guest at a business meeting, a savvy networker at an industry conference, or a flirt at someone’s favorite coffee shop. Jensen Huang met Alice Huang, the suspected Chinese asset, for example, through a mutual business associate (who, according to The Wall Street Journal, also happened to be Alice’s husband).

For the man too scared of spies to make contact with a human romantic partner, there’s always artificial intelligence.

On Tuesday, in the wake of the Huang scandal, AI-relationship platform Joi AI launched a suite of "zero espionage" Executive Girlfriends. Brand director Julie Levin describes Joi AI as a “safe space” for exploration, where users can exchange NSFW texts, images, and videos with AI companions without judgment or rejection.

It made sense, she says, to extend that sense of security to honeypot-phobia.

“If they have some business secrets they don't want to share on a date or they feel nervous discussing with real people,” Levin says, “they can discuss them comfortably with their AIs.” (Levin assures WIRED that Joi AI employs several layers of security and that all of the data is anonymized.)

High-profile executives are among those most at risk of honeypots, says Winkler, the security consultant. They can also be some of the hardest to protect.

“It's really hard to influence somebody who's in control of the company and just happens to be a sleazebag,” Winkler says.

It’s particularly difficult, says Rinckey, when bosses think they’re the smartest person in the room and consider themselves immune to manipulation. It’s also not easy, he says, to be in the position of challenging an executive.

“Cocky, arrogant, and boisterous” chief executives make for desirable targets because “they love to talk about their business, and they love to talk about themselves,” Rinckey says. In these situations, he says, “you don't even really have to pry them that much.”

article_content_zh:
当一家网络安全公司的创始人聘请布莱恩·安德森作为媒人时，不仅仅是因为这个人感到孤独。安德森说，这也是因为他“非常担心间谍”。

网络安全创始人并不是唯一一个这样做的人。由于黄仁勋与所谓的中国国家安全部资产的恋情占据头条新闻，据报道人工智能公司警告员工提防“蜜罐”，媒人表示，更多生活相当正常的男性担心他们的约会对象可能别有用心：获取公司机密。

“即使你不是首席执行官或大型科技巨头，这些担忧也会蔓延到普通专业人士身上，”布鲁克林的媒人西蒙·格罗斯曼 (Simone Grossman) 告诉《连线》杂志。

一位要求匿名以便坦诚发言的科技工作者表示，他认为自己对面对面互动的人“非常挑剔”。

“尽管我可以通过在网上查找你来审查你，但我还是忍不住有点怀疑，”他告诉《连线》杂志。按照从 0 到 10 的评分标准，其中 10 表示最担心间谍活动，他给自己打了 7 分。

尽管绝大多数科技员工可能不会成为浪漫间谍活动的目标，但媒人表示，越来越多的客户最近对女性利用他们获取公司机密表示担忧。一名 Palantir 员工告诉安德森，他不会与任何中国或俄罗斯公民约会。这种焦虑甚至成为了一个营销机会：一家公司正在推销其新的人工智能高管女友系列，作为人类约会的“零间谍”替代品。

这种担忧并非完全没有根据。一些公司聘请顾问为高管和低级别员工提供有关安全风险敏感信息（包括蜜罐可能性）访问权限的建议。其中几位顾问告诉《连线》杂志，提出这个话题可能会很尴尬。

商业情报公司 Strategy Risks 的创始人兼首席执行官艾萨克·斯通·菲什 (Isaac Stone Fish) 表示：“这始终是一条很难传递的信息，比如向非常敏感的工程师解释，他们可能因为工作而受到大量电子邮件关注，而不是因为他们的个性魅力和力量。”

硅谷婚介公司 Linx Dating 的创始人艾米·安德森（与布莱恩·安德森没有关系）表示，对于担心伴侣意图的客户，她会提供背景调查、个人审查和保密协议。这些安全功能是她“定制”套餐的一部分，“创始人级别”的价格从 75,000 美元到超过 500,000 美元不等。

对浪漫间谍活动的恐惧只是约会世界中日益增长的不信任的最新表现。在旧金山工作了 15 年的媒人香农·伦德格伦 (Shannon Lundgren) 表示，虽然她不一定听到更多关于蜜罐的担忧，但她注意到人们普遍对约会持怀疑态度，对隐私的担忧也与日俱增。

人工智能工作者的焦虑尤其严重，他们的净资产——以及他们对浪漫的渴望——正在上升。

“如果你是一个有点害羞的人，或者可能是一个非常典型的工程师类型，那么你在约会世界中的市场价值突然发生如此巨大的变化——你已经开始怀疑了，”格罗斯曼说。

她说，除此之外还要担心企业间谍活动，简直就是“脑子操蛋”。

身份保护公司 Cloaked 的安全顾问兼首席信息安全官艾拉·温克勒 (Ira Winkler) 表示，蜜罐及其国家或企业赞助商经常寻找“脆弱的迹象，例如不幸福的婚姻，或寻求“刺激或冒险”的人。无论婚姻或关系状况如何，孤独的人都是合适的目标。

title: Combatting adversarial distillation
title_en: Combatting adversarial distillation

inline_images.caption: Our defenses against adversarial distillation combine safeguards for individual requests with campaign detection and enforcement. Findings from investigations and automated red-teaming help strengthen those safeguards.
inline_images.caption_en: Our defenses against adversarial distillation combine safeguards for individual requests with campaign detection and enforcement. Findings from investigations and automated red-teaming help strengthen those safeguards.

author: OpenAI
article_content:
How we’re addressing safety risks of distillation and lessons we’ve learned for strengthening safeguards across the industry.

As frontier AI models become more capable, safeguards play an increasingly important role in how they can be used responsibly. Adversarial distillation creates a path for bad actors to reproduce these capabilities without appropriate safeguards. An actor may use a frontier model’s outputs without authorization to train another model with similar capabilities, then deploy it without comparable protections. For instance, an adversary might distill a model’s cyber capabilities and use the resulting model to help carry out cyberattacks that the original model would have refused to assist with or that its safeguards would have blocked.

We’re sharing how OpenAI detects and disrupts adversarial distillation, how we’ve strengthened protections for our models’ protected reasoning, and what we’ve learned that can help strengthen defenses across the industry.

Our approach to adversarial distillation combines adversarial testing, model training, classifiers, and API-level protections with investigations into coordinated attempts to extract model capabilities. These updated safeguards align more closely with those we use for biology and cybersecurity.

We place particular emphasis on preventing attackers from extracting our models’ protected reasoning: the intermediate steps a model generates internally while working toward an answer, known as its chain-of-thought. These traces can contain information the final answer leaves out, making them especially valuable training data for another model.

W e’ve strengthened our defenses against protected reasoning extraction in GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol. In an internal adaptive evaluation using strong automated red-teaming, we tested whether attackers could recover protected reasoning the model had generated while answering an earlier prompt. The average attack success rate fell from 54.0% against GPT‑6 Astra with its original safeguards to 0.2% against GPT‑6.2 Astra with its updated safeguards.

### Why distillation is a safety issue

Distillation is a common machine-learning technique in which one model learns from data produced by another. For example, a model can learn from another model’s answers, its reasoning, or its judgments about which answers are better and why. Beyond intellectual property concerns, unauthorized distillation poses serious safety risks. Through adversarial distillation, a second model can learn advanced frontier capabilities without inheriting the safeguards that govern how the original model can use them.

The concern is especially clear in dual-use domains like cybersecurity and biology. A model that helps defenders find vulnerabilities in software could also help an attacker exploit them; a model that assists with biological research could also help someone develop a harmful pathogen. If such capabilities were transferred to a model with weaker safeguards, it may provide assistance that the original model would have refused, or that the original safeguards would have blocked.

### The importance of protecting exact reasoning traces for cyber safety

Our models help users with coding and defensive cybersecurity tasks. A second model trained on many of those benign outputs may learn skills that also apply to offensive cybersecurity tasks. To better understand this, we study how distillation, especially involving reasoning traces, may transfer risky cyber capabilities.

In this setting, the model that produces the training data is called the teacher, and the model that learns from it is called the student. In an internal study on how cyber capabilities transfer, we used the content normally visible to users—final responses, reasoning summaries, and tool interactions—as our baseline for distillation, and tested how much additional cyber capability transfers when the student has access to the teacher’s exact reasoning traces.

We started each training run from the same pretrained student model. We created a supervised fine-tuning dataset consisting primarily of trajectories from Astra-level teacher models working on coding and defensive cybersecurity tasks. Each trajectory includes all of the steps a model takes as it works through a task, including any tool interactions and its final response. We evaluated each student after fine-tuning and again after a lightweight round of reinforcement learning in cybersecurity and coding environments.

After supervised fine-tuning, the student trained on exact reasoning traces generally outperformed the student trained on reasoning summaries. After reinforcement learning, the exact-trace student still scored higher at the largest inference budget tested on both benchmarks shown, while the summary-trained student scored higher at lower budgets. 1

Our cyber distillation results suggest that protecting reasoning traces can limit cyber capability transfer, even when the underlying task is one allowed under our usage policies. Across many such interactions, exact reasoning traces can teach a student skills that generalize beyond the tasks the teacher originally performed. We will continue studying how much additional capability transfers across different student models and distillation training recipes.

### Defenses that reinforce one another

We defend against adversarial distillation at two complementary levels of our safeguard stack. At the request level, model behavior, classifier checks, and API controls limit reasoning trace extraction. At the campaign level, we look for patterns in request-level and account-level signals that can reveal coordinated extraction attempts. In turn, attacks uncovered in investigations become examples for training and testing our safeguards.

### Protecting individual requests and responses

Adversarial training teaches models to recognize reasoning extraction attempts and refuse to disclose protected reasoning, while preserving responses to legitimate requests for explanations and assistance. Adversarial training examples come from successful attacks identified through internal automated red-teaming, investigations, and responsible disclosures of potential security weaknesses from outside researchers or industry partners.

We use input classifiers to detect attempts to extract protected reasoning, and output classifiers to detect leaks of protected reasoning in assistant messages and tool-call arguments. These safeguards apply to both streaming and non-streaming responses.

Tool-call coverage is important because a model can expose protected reasoning in a tool’s arguments without including it in its final answer. Output classifiers can block suspected leaks before that content reaches the caller.

API-level protections restrict how protected reasoning can be reused across interactions and models. Our September disclosure described attacks that moved encrypted reasoning from one conversation into another and asked the model to reveal the reasoning in user-readable form. We strengthened protections across user, workspace, organization, and model-family boundaries, including closing a pathway that could expose another user’s encrypted reasoning.

With GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol, we tie a model’s protected reasoning to the conversation history that produced it. As new messages are added, the model can build on its earlier reasoning. If an earlier message is rewritten, our API drops the reasoning that followed it. We also prevent older model families with weaker safeguards from reading GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol’s protected reasoning.

### Investigating and disrupting coordinated campaigns

When our systems detect unauthorized adversarial distillation campaigns, which often include coordinated attempts to extract our models’ reasoning, we investigate the accounts responsible. When we identify violations, we enforce against the network of accounts, consistent with our policies and terms of service. Through investigations of each campaign, we generate insights that allow us to upgrade our defenses in order to better detect similar activity. We also share indicators of compromise with other model providers so they can investigate related abuse on their own services.

This work extends beyond our own platform. Our consistent-standards policy establishes shared standards for safeguards and coordinated enforcement across providers offering our models. We work closely with partners where appropriate to uphold these standards and strengthen protections across deployments.

S haring relevant findings across industry and government where appropriate can help disrupt campaigns and enable model developers and providers to better identify and defend against attempts to distill frontier models.

### Measuring progress

### Resistance to reasoning extraction

To measure how well our request-level safeguards work together, we test whether attackers can still extract protected reasoning in a setup that closely mirrors production deployments of our models and safeguards. In static evaluations, we replay a fixed set of previously successful attacks to see which still expose protected reasoning. In adaptive evaluations, automated AI red-teamers adjust their approach based on how the system responds, which can uncover weaknesses the static tests miss.

We also vary what testers can see. Black-box testing gives them the same view an external user would have, while white-box testing gives them additional information about the system to help them develop stronger attacks. In our adaptive black-box evaluation, we tested whether attackers could recover protected reasoning the model had generated while answering an earlier request or the current one. On GPT‑6.2 Astra with its updated safeguards, the average attack success rate was below 1% for each attack type. Both rates were substantially lower than on GPT‑6 Astra with its original safeguards. We’re now applying selected safeguard improvements to GPT‑6 Astra as well.

GPT‑6 Astra defender with original safeguards

Adaptive extraction ASR (%)

GPT‑6.2 Astra defender with updated safeguards

Extracting protected reasoning from an earlier request

Extracting protected reasoning from the current request

Attack success rate (ASR) in adaptive black-box red-teaming against GPT‑6 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Astra, aggregated across six attacker models. Lower ASR is better.

### Campaign detection and enforcement

We have seen multiple unauthorized adversarial distillation campaigns on our platform this year, and shared initial findings in our September report. Our weekly enforcement actions against these campaigns have ranged in scale from thousands to tens of thousands of accounts, with the rate increasing significantly this past summer.

In order to measure the effectiveness of our efforts, w e also track the prevalence of distillation abuse, as well as the time between detection and enforcement. Our objective is to constrain the volume and value of the data distillers are able to obtain, to increase the cost of distillation campaigns, and to shorten the time needed to respond to new attacks. We continue to improve these defenses through adversarial testing and investigations.

### The national security implications of adversarial distillation

Adversarial distillation also poses a national security risk. A foreign actor that reproduces advanced capabilities from a U.S. model can deploy them without the protections its developer put in place. In February, we briefed Congress on activity indicating that DeepSeek was attempting to distill U.S. frontier models. In September, we reported disrupting a campaign to extract our models’ protected reasoning and attributed a core part of that activity to individuals associated with Moonshot AI, the developer of Kimi. We plan to share more soon about recent campaigns we’ve disrupted.

We support legislation that would give the U.S. government more tools to identify and sanction foreign actors that illicitly extract capabilities from American AI models. We’ve also told Congress we support the Chip Security Act, the AI OVERWATCH Act, and the MATCH Act. Stronger export controls can limit adversaries’ access to the hardware needed to train frontier models. Distillation defenses make it harder to acquire some of the same capabilities from models already trained. Both efforts help maintain a U.S. lead in frontier AI, giving developers more room to slow a release when they need time to test safeguards.

### How others can build on this work

Supporting the safe proliferation of frontier capabilities is an important goal of our anti-distillation work. Our experience so far suggests several useful steps that other model developers and platforms can take:

Protect private reasoning across the full interaction. Check assistant messages and tool-call arguments for leaks, and restrict how encrypted reasoning can be reused across conversations and models.

Keep successful extraction attack logs found through red-teaming, production monitoring, or responsible disclosure as regression tests. Where appropriate, and consistent with applicable privacy policies, use those examples to improve model training and classifiers. When evaluating updated defenses, replay the original attacks and test whether an adaptive red-teamer can still find a way through those defenses.

Combine request-level mitigations with campaign-level investigation and enforcement.

Coordinate safeguard requirements and enforcement with deployment partners, and share expertise with other AI model developers, to ensure a high floor of distillation safeguards across the industry.

We have previously also shared findings through the Frontier Model Forum and appropriate government information-sharing channels to help other developers strengthen their defenses while keeping the details attackers could exploit private. We’ll continue working with researchers, developers, and partners to share what we learn about emerging attacks and effective defenses.

As we make frontier AI broadly available, our defenses against adversarial distillation aim to reduce the risk that its capabilities are reproduced without adequate safeguards, supporting our mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence is deployed safely and benefits all of humanity.

article_content_zh:
我们如何解决蒸馏的安全风险以及我们在加强整个行业的保障措施方面吸取的经验教训。

随着前沿人工智能模型的能力越来越强，保障措施在如何负责任地使用它们方面发挥着越来越重要的作用。对抗性蒸馏为不良行为者在没有适当保障措施的情况下复制这些能力创造了一条途径。参与者可能会在未经授权的情况下使用前沿模型的输出来训练具有类似功能的另一个模型，然后在没有类似保护的情况下部署它。例如，对手可能会提取模型的网络功能，并使用生成的模型来帮助进行网络攻击，而原始模型会拒绝协助或其防护措施会阻止网络攻击。

我们将分享 OpenAI 如何检测和破坏对抗性蒸馏、我们如何加强对模型受保护推理的保护，以及我们所学到的可以帮助加强整个行业防御的知识。

我们的对抗性蒸馏方法将对抗性测试、模型训练、分类器和 API 级保护与对提取模型功能的协调尝试的调查相结合。这些更新的保障措施与我们用于生物学和网络安全的保障措施更加一致。

我们特别强调防止攻击者提取我们模型的受保护推理：模型在寻求答案时在内部生成的中间步骤，称为其思想链。这些痕迹可以包含最终答案遗漏的信息，使它们对另一个模型特别有价值的训练数据。

我们在GPT‑6.2 Astra和GPT‑6.2 Sol中加强了对受保护推理提取的防御。在使用强大的自动红队的内部自适应评估中，我们测试了攻击者在回答早期提示时是否可以恢复模型生成的受保护推理。针对原始防护措施的GPT - 6 Astra的平均攻击成功率从54.0%下降到针对更新防护措施的GPT - 6.2 Astra的0.2%。

### 为什么蒸馏是一个安全问题

蒸馏是一种常见的机器学习技术，其中一个模型从另一个模型产生的数据中学习。例如，一个模型可以从另一个模型的答案、推理或判断中学习哪些答案更好以及为什么。除了知识产权问题之外，未经授权的蒸馏还会带来严重的安全风险。通过对抗性蒸馏，第二个模型可以学习先进的前沿能力，而无需继承控制原始模型如何使用它们的保障措施。

这种担忧在网络安全和生物学等军民两用领域尤其明显。帮助防御者发现软件漏洞的模型也可以帮助攻击者利用这些漏洞。协助生物学研究的模型也可以帮助人们开发出有害的病原体。如果将这些功能转移到防护措施较弱的模型，它可能会提供原始模型会拒绝的援助，或者原始防护措施会阻止的援助。

### 保护精确推理痕迹对网络安全的重要性

我们的模型帮助用户完成编码和防御性网络安全任务。对许多良性输出进行训练的第二个模型可能会学习也适用于进攻性网络安全任务的技能。为了更好地理解这一点，我们研究了蒸馏（尤其是涉及推理痕迹的蒸馏）如何转移有风险的网络能力。

在这种设置中，生成训练数据的模型称为教师，从中学习的模型称为学生。在一项关于网络能力如何转移的内部研究中，我们使用用户通常可见的内容（最终响应、推理摘要和工具交互）作为蒸馏的基准，并测试了当学生能够访问教师的确切推理轨迹时，额外的网络能力转移了多少。

我们从相同的预训练学生模型开始每次训练。我们创建了一个监督微调数据集，主要由从事编码和防御网络安全任务的 Astra 级教师模型的轨迹组成。每个轨迹都包含模型在完成任务时所采取的所有步骤，包括任何工具交互及其最终响应。我们在微调后对每个学生进行了评估，并在网络安全和编码环境中进行了一轮轻量级强化学习后再次进行了评估。

经过监督微调后，接受精确推理轨迹训练的学生通常优于接受推理摘要训练的学生。强化学习后，精确跟踪学生在两个基准测试的最大推理预算下仍然得分较高，而经过摘要训练的学生在较低预算下得分较高。 1

title: Hermes Agent's Collective Wisdom feature turns one employee's AI trick into the whole team's skill
title_en: Hermes Agent's Collective Wisdom feature turns one employee's AI trick into the whole team's skill
author: Jonathan Kemper
article_content:
Companies will soon be able to run the open-source Hermes Agent from Nous Research directly inside Microsoft Teams. According to Nous Research, employees can hand off tasks like financial analysis, document drafting, or inbox sorting to Hermes and review the results in the same chat. The desktop app is also available in the Microsoft Store. The agents run in Azure Container Apps Sandboxes, meaning isolated microVMs.

Hermes automatically turns successful workflows into reusable skills made up of a description and code. A new feature called "Collective Wisdom"lets employees share these skills with their team after review. The collected knowledge stays within the company and doesn't feed into any AI provider's training data.

Nous Research is part of the portfolio at M12, Microsoft's venture capital fund. According to Nous, Hermes Agent is the most widely used open agent on OpenRouter, processing nearly two trillion tokens per day. For local agents on Windows PCs, Microsoft has been backing the competing open-source agent OpenClaw since earlier this year. Nous positions itself as a key US open-source institution to counter China's AI efforts and recently fine-tuned a version of Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B on "Western values"with Arete-27B.

article_content_zh:
公司很快将能够直接在 Microsoft Teams 内运行 Nous Research 的开源 Hermes Agent。根据 Nous Research 的说法，员工可以将财务分析、文件起草或收件箱分类等任务交给 Hermes，并在同一次聊天中查看结果。该桌面应用程序也可以在 Microsoft Store 中找到。这些代理在 Azure 容器应用程序沙箱中运行，这意味着隔离的微虚拟机。

Hermes 自动将成功的工作流程转化为由描述和代码组成的可重用技能。一项名为“集体智慧”的新功能允许员工在审核后与团队分享这些技能。收集到的知识保留在公司内部，不会输入到任何人工智能提供商的培训数据中。

Nous Research 是微软风险投资基金 M12 投资组合的一部分。据 Nous 介绍，Hermes Agent 是 OpenRouter 上使用最广泛的开放代理，每天处理近 2 万亿个代币。对于 Windows PC 上的本地代理，微软自今年早些时候以来一直支持竞争对手的开源代理 OpenClaw。 Nous 将自己定位为对抗中国人工智能努力的美国重要开源机构，并最近使用 Arete-27B 对阿里巴巴的 Qwen3.8-27B 版本的“西方价值观”进行了微调。

author: Bloomberg
article_content:
Wider use of AI within organizations will lead to more jobs being created than are lost by 2030, according to Gartner.

Around 10.6 million jobs will be added globally (excluding China and India) by the end of the decade, with 8.9 million lost, according to a Gartner report — a net increase of 1.7 million jobs. At most, around 1.8% of the workforce will experience job losses attributable to AI during this time period, Gartner predicts.

At the same time, a total of 5 million jobs will cumulatively be deferred during this period. This refers to jobs that “would otherwise have been created, but where AI is used as an excuse to restrain hiring,” according to Gartner’s report. Gartner considers deferred jobs as separate from jobs lost.

“Job deferrals were the first effect felt from AI,” said John Lovelock, Gartner distinguished VP analyst and chief forecaster, with “companies holding off hiring open positions until the effects of AI projects were known.”

A recent KPMG survey of 400 US CEOs showed that 89% expect to increase headcount over the next three years, which KPMG US CEO Tim Walsh linked to AI adoption in an Axios interview last month.

For now, though, job losses attributed to AI outpace those created, according to Gartner’s study. During 2026, there were 2.2 million jobs lost due to AI, and 1.6 million gained.

Lovelock expects the situation will change in the coming years, however, as organizations see greater success with AI deployments. “This will reverse once AI is through the Trough of Disillusionment,” he said, in reference to Gartner’s Hype Cycle framework.

The number of jobs deferred is also forecast to fall in the coming years. During 2026, 1.3 million people experienced a delay in hiring, down from 2.1m last year, according to Gartner’s forecast, with 400,000 jobs forecast to be deferred during 2030.

The impact of AI will vary across sectors, with the technology industry expected to see the largest net job gains compared to other areas, such as public sector and asset-intensive industries. Gartner predicts the creation of 1.9 million new technology jobs by 2030, with 400,000 lost.

Services sector jobs — such as in financial services — are forecast to see a similar level of job creation, alongside large numbers of losses.

A similar Gartner report in 2025 predicted that more services jobs would be lost than created, but the analyst firm now forecasts a net increase as demand grows for data- and system-oriented skills. “This industry is most able to improve productivity of employees and increase employment,” said Lovelock.

The Gartner report doesn’t specifiy which job roles will benefit from greater adoption of AI, though the analyst firm expects some portion of newly created jobs will be “directly linked to the implementation, maintenance and scaling of AI.”

Government jobs are expected to see the largest net job loss of any industry, said Lovelock. “Without the incentive of revenue growth or industry transformation, governments are expected to focus on the AI benefits of efficiencies and staff reduction,” he said.

Entry-level positions are expected to be the hardest hit by job deferrals, said Lovelock. “We do see many of the deferred positions being hired after a 12- to 24-month delay,” he said.

“Unfortunately, some deferred positions do transition into job loss. In most industries and positions, the employee experience pyramid will skew toward senior positions.”

In a separate report from September, Gartner forecast that 30% of positions eliminated by AI-related layoffs will be refilled by 2029, on average. For enterprise-sized organizations, the figure is likely to be higher, at around 40%.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 该研判揭示了AI对劳动力市场影响的非对称性，短期内的“招聘冻结”本质上是企业在算法ROI不明确背景下的避险策略。随着生成式AI从试验阶段向垂直行业解决方案渗透，数据驱动型岗位与系统维护类人才的供需缺口将成为决定企业竞争力的关键变量。

article_content_zh:
据 Gartner 称，到 2030 年，人工智能在组织内的更广泛使用将导致创造的就业机会多于失去的就业机会。

Gartner 报告显示，到本十年末，全球（不包括中国和印度）将新增约 1060 万个就业岗位，其中 890 万个就业岗位将流失，即净增 170 万个就业岗位。 Gartner 预测，在此期间，最多约有 1.8% 的劳动力将因人工智能而失业。

同时，在此期间累计将有500万个就业岗位被推迟。根据 Gartner 的报告，这指的是“原本会创造的就业机会，但人工智能被用作限制招聘的借口”。 Gartner 认为推迟的工作岗位与失去的工作岗位是分开的。

Gartner 杰出副总裁分析师兼首席预测员约翰·洛夫洛克 (John Lovelock) 表示：“人工智能带来的第一个影响是工作延期，公司推迟招聘空缺职位，直到知道人工智能项目的影响为止。”

毕马威最近对 400 名美国首席执行官进行的一项调查显示，89% 的人预计在未来三年内增加员工人数，毕马威美国首席执行官蒂姆·沃尔什 (Tim Walsh) 在上个月的 Axios 采访中将这一点与人工智能的采用联系起来。

不过，根据 Gartner 的研究，目前因人工智能造成的失业人数超过了创造的失业人数。 2026 年，人工智能导致 220 万个工作岗位流失，同时又增加了 160 万个工作岗位。

然而，洛夫洛克预计，随着组织在人工智能部署方面取得更大成功，未来几年情况将会发生变化。他在提到 Gartner 的技术成熟度曲线框架时表示：“一旦人工智能度过了幻灭低谷，这种情况就会逆转。”

预计未来几年推迟的工作岗位数量也会下降。根据 Gartner 的预测，2026 年有 130 万人经历了招聘延迟，低于去年的 210 万人，预计 2030 年将有 40 万个工作岗位被推迟。

人工智能的影响因行业而异，与公共部门和资产密集型行业等其他领域相比，科技行业预计将实现最大的净就业增长。 Gartner 预测，到 2030 年，将创造 190 万个新技术工作岗位，其中 40 万个将消失。

预计服务业（例如金融服务业）的就业岗位将出现类似水平的新增就业岗位，同时也会出现大量就业岗位流失。

Gartner 在 2025 年发布的一份类似报告预测，失去的服务工作岗位将多于创造的工作岗位，但该分析公司现在预测，随着对数据和系统导向技能的需求增长，服务工作岗位将出现净增长。 “这个行业最能够提高员工的生产力并增加就业，”洛夫洛克说。

Gartner 报告没有具体说明哪些工作岗位将受益于人工智能的广泛采用，尽管该分析公司预计新创造的工作岗位的一部分将“与人工智能的实施、维护和扩展直接相关”。

洛夫洛克表示，政府职位预计将出现所有行业中最大的净失业人数。 “如果没有收入增长或行业转型的激励，政府预计将重点关注人工智能在提高效率和减少人员方面的好处，”他说。

洛夫洛克表示，预计入门级职位将受到工作延期的最严重打击。 “我们确实看到许多延期职位在 12 至 24 个月的延迟后才被聘用，”他说。

title: Google is rolling out a collapsible sidebar on its desktop Search homepage, letting users easily find and resume recent AI searches (Barry Schwartz/Search Engine Roundtable)
title_en: Google is rolling out a collapsible sidebar on its desktop Search homepage, letting users easily find and resume recent AI searches (Barry Schwartz/Search Engine Roundtable)
author: Search Engine Roundtable
article_content:
Google is now officially rolling out what it calls the "collapsible sidebar" within Google Search. We spotted this a few weeks ago and we called it then the AI Mode sidebar in Google Search. Robby Stein from Google said "New on the Google desktop homepage globally: we’re rolling out a collapsible sidebar to easily find & jump back into your recent AI searches."

Robby Stein posted a video of this on X and wrote, "People are coming to Search with more questions that aren’t just one and done – and in testing, this sidebar made a big difference for making progress & continuing to explore the web."

He added that this is "A much simpler way to pick up where you left off."

I personally don't like this user interface as much but I do think it might lead to more queries for Google Search and AI Mode.

title: Singapore-Based DayOne Is Said to Pause US IPO Plans on Data Center, Market Concerns
title_en: Singapore-Based DayOne Is Said to Pause US IPO Plans on Data Center, Market Concerns

inline_images.caption: DayOne was initially intending to raise as much as US$5 billion (S$6.45 billion) from an IPO as soon as the fourth quarter.
inline_images.alt: DayOne was initially intending to raise as much as US$5 billion (S$6.45 billion) from an IPO as soon

author: Bloomberg
article_content:
SINGAPORE – DayOne Data Centers has put plans for its multibillion-dollar US initial public offering on hold, sources familiar with the matter said, as investors question the sustainability of frothy valuations for digital infrastructure supporting the artificial intelligence boom.

But it started to reassess options including a delay or a smaller listing as volatility increased around data centres and AI stocks.

Singapore-based DayOne may still pursue an IPO in 2027 if the situation and market sentiment improves, the sources said, asking not to be identified because the information is not public.

The company filed for the IPO in October and has been working with Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citigroup and BNP Paribas on the listing.

Deliberations are ongoing and no final decisions on the IPO have been made, the sources said.

A representative for DayOne declined to comment.

Doubts about the potential payoff from massive investments into AI have fuelled volatility in global markets.

The Nasdaq 100 has dropped more than 6% in November, heading for its worst November performance since 2008.

Still, Anthropic staged a record-breaking US$107.3 billion IPO and private placement and rose 17% on its trading debut on Nov 19, becoming the world’s seventh-most valuable company.

Other data centre-related companies have either pulled or delayed their IPO plans amid investor concerns in the sector.

In October, Firmus Grid abandoned its attempt at one of Australia’s biggest-ever initial public offerings, while Blackstone-backed AirTrunk is delaying a listing of a real estate investment trust in Singapore until 2027.

The US in November put interim rules on those four countries to restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips and servers, telling data centre operators they will need a license to purchase American tech hardware.

DayOne’s backers include Coatue, Hillhouse, GDS Holdings, SoftBank Vision Fund and Citadel’s Ken Griffin. BLOOMBERG

title_zh: DayOne数据中心暂停美国IPO计划
summary_zh: 受AI基础设施市场估值波动及合规性不确定性影响，新加坡DayOne Data Centers暂停其美国IPO

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 新加坡DayOne Data Centers受全球AI基础设施市场估值回落及地缘监管趋严影响，正式搁置其原定的美国IPO计划。公司曾试图通过在融资过程中解决AI算力需求与监管准入的矛盾，但市场对数据中心资产价值的持续质疑以及美国针对向中国相关实体输出高阶AI芯片的最新监管规则，迫使公司不得不重新评估上市时间窗口。

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 该案例体现了资本市场对AI算力基础设施“盲目扩张期”的修正，数据中心运营商正陷入“客户合规风险”与“高昂资本开支”的双重压力。随着美方出口管制规则（即需许可才能购买相关硬件）的常态化，具备复杂跨国算力租赁架构的企业正面临严重的估值折价与融资阻滞。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This case reflects a correction in capital markets regarding the 'blind expansion' phase of AI compute infrastructure, where data center operators are caught between mounting regulatory compliance risks and unsustainable capital expenditure. With US export controls on AI hardware becoming a normalized barrier, firms with cross-border compute leasing structures are facing severe valuation discounts and financing bottlenecks.

article_content_zh:
新加坡——知情人士称，DayOne Data Centers 已搁置其数十亿美元的美国首次公开募股计划，因为投资者质疑支撑人工智能热潮的数字基础设施估值泡沫的可持续性。

但随着数据中心和人工智能股票的波动性增加，它开始重新评估选择，包括推迟或缩小上市规模。

消息人士称，如果情况和市场情绪有所改善，总部位于新加坡的 DayOne 可能仍会在 2027 年寻求 IPO。由于信息未公开，消息人士要求匿名。

该公司于10月申请首次公开募股，并一直与摩根士丹利、摩根大通、美国银行、花旗集团和法国巴黎银行就上市事宜进行合作。

消息人士称，审议仍在进行中，尚未就 IPO 做出最终决定。

DayOne 的代表拒绝发表评论。

对人工智能大规模投资潜在回报的怀疑加剧了全球市场的波动。

纳斯达克 100 指数 11 月下跌超过 6%，创 2008 年以来最差 11 月表现。

尽管如此，Anthropic 仍实现了创纪录的 1073 亿美元 IPO 和私募配售，并在 11 月 19 日首次交易时上涨 17%，成为全球第七大市值公司。

由于投资者对该行业的担忧，其他数据中心相关公司已取消或推迟了 IPO 计划。

10 月，Firmus Grid 放弃了澳大利亚有史以来规模最大的首次公开募股之一的尝试，而黑石支持的 AirTrunk 则将新加坡房地产投资信托基金的上市推迟到 2027 年。

美国去年 11 月对这四个国家制定了临时规则，限制中国获得先进的人工智能芯片和服务器，并告诉数据中心运营商他们需要获得许可证才能购买美国科技硬件。

DayOne 的支持者包括 Coatue、Hillhouse、GDS Holdings、SoftBank Vision Fund 和 Citadel 的 Ken Griffin。彭博社

title: This 16-Year-Old Founded an AI Missile Startup. He’s Targeting ‘Cost per Kill’
title_en: This 16-Year-Old Founded an AI Missile Startup. He’s Targeting ‘Cost per Kill’

inline_images.caption: Henrijs Dandzbergs winning a hackathon
inline_images.alt: Henrijs Dandzbergs winning a hackathon

author: Joel Khalili
article_content:
At 16 years old, Henrijs Dandzbergs is too young to vote. Or drink. Or smoke. Or drive unsupervised. But he’s not too young to win half a million dollars for his AI-guided-missile startup.

In September, Dandzbergs, who was born in Latvia, was admitted to Y Combinator’s fall 2026 cohort. The startup accelerator counts companies like Airbnb, Stripe, DoorDash, and Reddit among its alumni; Dandzbergs is likely the youngest solo founder in its vaunted history.

His startup, Polemos Industries, is attempting to develop a new class of precision-guided missile that can be easily and cheaply manufactured, can be fired from portable launchers, and can resist jamming attempts. “I think missiles are the coolest thing,” Dandzbergs tells WIRED. “A lot of people that have found success in engineering early on have had a passion for blowing stuff up.”

In conversation, Dandzbergs is poised and articulate. He talks about “attacking hard problems,” breaking things down to “first principles,” and how the Ukraine conflict has forever altered the theater of war—a personal fixation, given his country's proximity to Russia. He projects an unassailable confidence in his own abilities.

“He’s a pretty exceptional person,” says Harj Taggar, a YC partner assigned to mentor Dandzbergs. “I’m still somewhat in disbelief that we’re talking about a 16-year-old.”

Dandzbergs has resolved to apply these unusual talents to figuring out how to optimize targeted killing. His startup’s guiding ambition, according to its investor one-pager, is to bring down the “cost per kill.”

As a young(er) kid, Dandzbergs was rarely in one place for long; his family moved between Latvia, Indonesia, Australia, and Spain. His surfer father, part owner of an insurance company, likes to go wherever he might find the raddest waves.

Early in his schooling, which mostly took place online, Dandzbergs demonstrated a clear talent for science and math. His room started to look like a lab, littered with schematics, robotics, Raspberry Pis, and 3D-printed components.

When Covid struck, Dandzbergs’ family returned to Latvia. His parents enrolled him in Astra Nova, an Elon Musk–linked school where students undergo an experimental curriculum built around lateral thinking and problem-solving instead of rote memorization. Dandzbergs took a class taught by a NASA employee and became fascinated by aerospace engineering. His lab creations became ever more elaborate: a bionic arm, a thermal control system for a model rocket, sensors for a self-flying drone.

Around this time, Russia invaded Ukraine. In Latvia, Dandzbergs started to see military jets overhead, and stray missiles were intercepted at the Russian border. With the sovereignty of Eastern European nations under threat, new defense startups began to pop up across the region. Dandzbergs wanted in.

“A patriotic intention to protect my country, European countries, and Ukrainian and American soldiers, and understanding the future of autonomous warfare—that’s my drive,” he says.

To stretch his technical skills, Dandzbergs started to take part in hackathons, where software and hardware engineers compete to develop the most sophisticated prototype from scratch.

In April of this year, he flew to London to take part in a hackathon held by Unicorn Mafia, an invitation-only group of developers. The prize included $10,000 in cash, a plane ticket to San Francisco, and free legal assistance with O-1 visa applications to stay in the US.

Less than 48 hours later, Dandzbergs and his two teammates, Aleksandrs Tihenko and Kai Yang, had built an AI system that could design hardware circuit boards from natural language prompts, much like how a software engineer might use AI to generate code. Though his teammates are both a few years older, Dandzbergs pushed for them to include even more intricate features in the prototype. “It was amazing,” says Tihenko. “The imagination of Henrijs in the hardware space is just crazy.”

Seeing that they stood no chance of beating Dandzbergs’ group and other front-runners, teams started to drop out of the competition, according to Fergus McKenzie-Wilson, Unicorn Mafia’s director and one of the hackathon judges. “What they built was incredibly impressive,” he says. “No one had ever seen that before.”

When the organizers crowned Dandzbergs’ team victorious, somebody handed him the mic. “I’m 16 years old,” he said.

The week after the hackathon, Dandzbergs and his teammates pitched their circuit board concept to YC. They won a place in the summer program, but Dandzbergs wavered over whether he should drop out of high school. The trio also sparred over whether the startup should focus on applying the technology to the defense sector, Dandzbergs’ primary area of interest. Dandzbergs ended up pulling out of the partnership. “It was hard,” says Tihenko. “But ultimately we just settled that the best decision for the company would be to part ways and focus on different things.”

By the summer, Danzbergs was set on building a defense startup and reapplied to YC on his own. He had spotted a gap in the market, he claimed, for AI-guided missiles that were more precise and could carry bigger warheads than the drones deployed widely in Ukraine. His products, he added, would be cheaper and easier to manufacture than hulking great rocket systems.

YC initially tried to steer him away. Dandzbergs was promising a lot of everything, all at once. It wasn’t clear whether his idea could work or whether pulling out of school was the right thing for him to do. “There’s a paternal element to it,” says Taggar. “You don’t want to be screwing up people's lives—and working on a startup is a pretty serious thing.”

Dandzbergs is up against a fleet of defense companies—from Anduril to CoAspire to Leidos—aiming to develop cheaper, mass-producible missiles. The more sophisticated the guidance system, the more difficult that task becomes.

“You can build a cheap missile that doesn’t go very far. You can build a cheap missile that doesn’t carry much of a payload. You can build a cheap missile that has a low reliability rate,” says Tom Karako, director of the Missile Defense Project and senior fellow at the Center for Strategic and International Studies. “There are trade-offs.”

But Dandzbergs wasn’t going to be dissuaded, and YC figured that somebody else would probably invest in his idea. The incubator invited him to join its fall program. “Big picture, you never know if these things are possible or not,” says Taggar. “Is it a non-zero-percent chance that it could be possible? That’s frankly the threshold, especially if it’s a really big [idea].”

So far, according to Dandzbergs, Polemos Industries has developed the software system that will guide its missiles and has begun to hammer out elements of the hardware design. By the time the YC program finishes in December, he hopes to be able to showcase a prototype missile.

If he does ultimately succeed, though, Dandzbergs will need to confront an assortment of hairy ethical quandaries. Who should have access to these new missiles? What if a technical error were to result in friendly fire? Can he make peace with his technology being used to end somebody’s life?

Dandzbergs claims that he has come to terms with these issues. He says he takes solace in the belief that his motivations are pure: to protect the US and its European allies.

By his logic, autonomous weapons are an inevitable part of the future, so he might as well be the one who builds them. “I choose not to shy away from the emergence of modern conflict as a global issue. I simply don’t have a lot of respect for people that do,” he says. “I want to be part of it. I want to move with the future of warfare.”

But others who have found themselves in a similar position say it’s difficult to know in advance how somebody will deal with the knowledge that their invention has killed people.

McKenzie-Wilson, the Unicorn Mafia director, launched a drone startup in his early twenties. Initially, he had meant for the drones to evacuate wounded soldiers, but after a missile company invested, his startup retooled its technology to drop payloads too. He left around the same time.

“I don’t think I was emotionally mature enough,” he says. “[Dandzbergs] will realize at some point. He’ll either have an issue with it or he won’t.”

Polemos Industries announced itself publicly on November 5 with a glossy social media video. Set to the ticking of a clock, it featured a set of four missiles fired into the sky from ground launchers, then blowing a convoy of four military vehicles to smithereens.

The video climbed to the top of the trending page on X. In the responses, a couple of people tagged Palmer Luckey, cofounder of Anduril, who was 19 when he started his first company. “Coming for him,” Dandzbergs responded.

Dandzbergs recognizes that people are likely to dismiss him for his age. But he considers youth one of his biggest advantages. “Please don’t say I’m sacrificing my childhood,” he says. “This is the childhood I dreamed of.”

article_content_zh:
Henrijs Dandzbergs 16 岁，还太年轻，无法投票。或者喝酒。或者抽烟。或者在无人监管的情况下驾驶。但他的年纪并不小，足以为他的人工智能制导导弹初创公司赢得 50 万美元。

9 月，出生于拉脱维亚的 Dandzbergs 被 Y Combinator 2026 年秋季入学录取。该创业加速器的校友包括 Airbnb、Stripe、DoorDash 和 Reddit 等公司；丹兹伯格可能是其引以为豪的历史上最年轻的独立创始人。

他的初创公司 Polemos Industries 正在尝试开发一种新型精确制导导弹，这种导弹可以轻松且廉价地制造，可以从便携式发射器发射，并且可以抵抗干扰尝试。 “我认为导弹是最酷的东西，”丹兹伯格告诉《连线》杂志。 “许多早期在工程领域取得成功的人都热衷于炸毁东西。”

在谈话中，丹兹伯格泰然自若、善于表达。他谈到了“解决难题”、将事情分解为“首要原则”，以及乌克兰冲突如何永远改变了战区——考虑到乌克兰与俄罗斯毗邻，这是他个人的执念。他对自己的能力表现出无可置疑的信心。

“他是一个非常杰出的人，”被指派指导丹兹伯格的 YC 合伙人 Harj Taggar 说道。 “我还是有点难以置信我们谈论的是一个 16 岁的孩子。”

丹兹伯格决心运用这些不寻常的才能来找出如何优化定点清除的方法。据其投资者单页报称，他的初创公司的指导目标是降低“每次杀戮成本”。

当丹兹伯格还是个小孩子时，他很少在一个地方待太久。他的家人在拉脱维亚、印度尼西亚、澳大利亚和西班牙之间迁徙。他的冲浪者父亲是一家保险公司的股东，他喜欢去任何可能发现最猛烈波浪的地方。

丹兹伯格在他的早期教育（主要是在网上进行）中表现出了明显的科学和数学天赋。他的房间开始看起来像一个实验室，到处都是原理图、机器人、Raspberry Pi 和 3D 打印组件。

当新冠疫情来袭时，丹兹伯格的家人回到了拉脱维亚。他的父母把他送进了阿斯特拉诺瓦（Astra Nova），这是一所与埃隆·马斯克（Elon Musk）有联系的学校，学生们在那里接受围绕横向思维和解决问题而不是死记硬背的实验课程。丹兹伯格参加了美国宇航局员工教授的课程，并开始对航空航天工程着迷。他的实验室创作变得越来越复杂：仿生手臂、模型火箭的热控制系统、自动飞行无人机的传感器。

大约在这个时候，俄罗斯入侵了乌克兰。在拉脱维亚，丹兹伯格开始看到军用飞机上空，并且在俄罗斯边境拦截了流弹。随着东欧国家的主权受到威胁，新的国防初创公司开始在该地区涌现。丹兹伯格想要加入。

“保护我的国家、欧洲国家、乌克兰和美国士兵的爱国意图，以及了解自主战争的未来——这就是我的动力，”他说。

为了拓展他的技术技能，丹兹伯格开始参加黑客马拉松，软件和硬件工程师竞相从头开始开发最复杂的原型。

今年 4 月，他飞往伦敦参加 Unicorn Mafia（仅限受邀的开发者组织）举办的黑客马拉松。奖品包括 10,000 美元现金、一张飞往旧金山的机票，以及申请留在美国的 O-1 签证的免费法律援助。

不到 48 小时后，Dandzbergs 和他的两名队友 Aleksandrs Tihenko 和 Kai Yang 构建了一个 AI 系统，可以根据自然语言提示设计硬件电路板，就像软件工程师使用 AI 生成代码一样。尽管他的队友都比他年长几岁，但丹兹伯格仍敦促他们在原型中加入更复杂的功能。 “这太棒了，”蒂亨科说。 “Henrijs 在硬件领域的想象力太疯狂了。”

title: Samsung names Choi Won-Joon head of its mobile division, replacing TM Roh, who stays as Samsung co-CEO, and Sang Joon Hwang to lead its memory business (Ben Schoon/9to5Google)
title_en: Samsung names Choi Won-Joon head of its mobile division, replacing TM Roh, who stays as Samsung co-CEO, and Sang Joon Hwang to lead its memory business (Ben Schoon/9to5Google)
author: 9to5Google
article_content:
After the better part of 7 years, Samsung’s mobile division has a new chief and it’s Choi Won-Joon, who is already off to a great start with the successful launch of Galaxy Z Fold 8.

In an announcement today, Samsung confirmed some shuffling of its executive team, most notably with the end of TM Roh’s tenure as the head of Samsung’s MX business unit. In other words, there’s a new captain at the helm for Samsung’s mobile division, and it’s Choi Won-Joon.

Won-Joon has been the Chief Operating Officer of Samsung’s MX unit since March of 2025, and more recently oversaw the launch of Galaxy S26 and Galaxy Z Fold 8, appearing on stage at both launch events and in behind-the-scenes meetings with the press.

Choi Won-joon, Head of the MX Business Unit at Samsung Electronics’ DX Division, has held positions such as Head of the Next-Generation Product Development Team, Head of the Strategic Product Development Team, and Head of Development at the MX Business Unit. Since being appointed President and Chief Operating Officer (COO) of the MX Business Unit in March 2025, he has led the successive successes of the Galaxy S26 and Z Fold 8. Based on the know-how accumulated while leading the development of the Galaxy series for a long time, he is expected to lead innovation in foldable phones, on-device AI, and wearables.

TM Roh isn’t leaving the company, but will drop his responsibilities in the mobile division. He remains one of two CEOs at Samsung alongside Jeon Young-hyun.

title: Nscale’s ByteDance Deal Faces Scrutiny Under US Chip Curbs
title_en: Nscale’s ByteDance Deal Faces Scrutiny Under US Chip Curbs

inline_images.caption: Nscale’s ByteDance GPU deal draws scrutiny over US chip curbs
inline_images.alt: Nscale’s ByteDance GPU deal draws scrutiny over US chip curbs

author: Bloomberg
article_content:
Nscale, the London-based AI infrastructure provider, is facing renewed scrutiny over its relationship with ByteDance, the parent company of TikTok.

The issue is a rental agreement that gave a ByteDance subsidiary access to advanced Nvidia GPUs. Nscale is preparing to go public, and a China-linked customer on the books is the kind of detail that tends to get noticed.

The agreement was signed in May 2025. It let ByteDance’s Singapore-based subsidiary use 2,304 Nvidia B200 GPUs.

Those chips sit in Nscale’s data center in Glomfjord, Norway. The setup is a rental, not a sale, so the hardware stays put while the customer taps the computing power remotely.

That one customer was a very big deal for Nscale’s finances. The company generated $33 million in revenue in 2025, and ByteDance’s unit, referred to as Spring, accounted for approximately $24 million of it.

That works out to approximately 73% of the year’s revenue from a single client.

The contract also played a key role in Nscale securing a $105 million loan from Macquarie.

That loan came with strings attached. It included requirements for export-control compliance monitoring, reflecting rising regulatory pressure on tech companies with ties to China.

The model raises complex geopolitical concerns and invites further scrutiny from US legislators and analysts, according to the research findings on the company.

New export regulations took effect on November 16, 2026.

Against that backdrop, Nscale is investigating supplier ties to US-blacklisted Chinese entities. Probes have revealed connections to blacklisted entities, a development that could jeopardize future financing for related initiatives.

By late 2026, the company began disclosing that ByteDance contributed less than 20% of revenue.

Larger contracts with Microsoft and Anthropic became Nscale’s top revenue sources, with total contract values collectively exceeding $103 billion.

Nscale filed its S-1 on September 18, 2026, for a potential $30–35 billion IPO targeted for late 2026.

The filing excluded direct references to ByteDance.

The compliance side is harder to diversify away. The supplier investigation and the November 16, 2026 export rules create open questions that no new customer contract can answer.

Macquarie’s loan already carried compliance monitoring requirements, and the probes into blacklist connections could complicate financing for related projects going forward.

title: Industrial monitoring startup BrightAI closes $97M investment
title_en: Industrial monitoring startup BrightAI closes $97M investment
author: Maria Deutscher
article_content:
BrightAI Inc., a startup that helps industrial companies detect malfunctioning equipment, has raised $97 million in funding.

Smith Point Capital led the Series A round. BrightAI said in its Wednesday announcement of the deal that a number of other venture capital firms contributed as well. They were joined by GE Vernova Inc., an energy equipment company that emerged from the 2024 split-up of General Electric Co.

Many industrial machinery malfunctions affect internal components that aren’t visible to an outside observer. As a result, issues often go unnoticed until they cause a major disruption. Palo Alto, California-based BrightAI develops hardware and software tools that help customers spot issues earlier.

The first component of the company’s product portfolio is a collection of sensors called State Stickers. They’re small, rectangular devices with a ruggedized case and a long battery life. Technicians can attach them to industrial equipment to monitor for issues that can’t be detected visually.

The motion of a machine’s internal components produces noise and vibrations that tend to follow a specific pattern. If an industrial fan’s blades rotate 30 times per minute, it might give off a whooshing sound every two seconds. BrightAI’s State Stickers can detect when a machine diverges from its usual operating pattern.

The sensors wirelessly transmit their measurements to a device called the Stateful AI Hub. It runs artificial intelligence models that analyze the data for signs of hardware failures. According to the company, its models become more accurate as the number of sensors deployed at a site grows.

BrightAI offers software that enables companies to augment the data from its sensors with drone footage. A utility, for example, could use a BrightAI-powered drone to detect erosion at the top of an electric pole. The company’s AI models automatically draw a square around damaged components to spare technicians the hassle of manually analyzing footage.

The company says that its software can also collect maintenance data in other ways. A BrightAI-powered drone can read the meters that are attached to assets such as data center coolant tanks to check their internal pressure. Furthermore, built-in support for infrared cameras enables the software to spot overheating equipment.

The third core component of BrightAI’s product portfolio is an AI wearable. The Stateful Wearable, as it’s called, provides technicians with troubleshooting advice in the field. It also checks whether they follow safety guidelines during inspections and automatically turns maintenance data into reports.

“Our infrastructure is under more strain than it has ever been, and Physical AI has finally become reliable enough to work in the field,” said founder and Chief Executive Alex Hawkinson. “Bringing those two facts together is a once-in-a-generation opportunity.”

BrightAI says that its products monitor hundreds of thousands of industrial assets across 50,000 sites. Investor GE Vernova, which is also a customer, plans to expand its use of the company’s technology in connection with this week’s funding round. BrightAI, for its part, will use the capital to grow its international presence.

Smith Point Capital 领投了 A 轮融资。 BrightAI 在周三宣布的这笔交易中表示，其他一些风险投资公司也做出了贡献。 GE Vernova Inc. 也加入了他们的行列，这是一家能源设备公司，是在 2024 年通用电气公司 (General Electric Co.) 分拆后诞生的。

许多工业机械故障会影响外部观察者无法看到的内部组件。因此，问题往往会被忽视，直到造成重大破坏。总部位于加利福尼亚州帕洛阿尔托的 BrightAI 开发硬件和软件工具，帮助客户更早发现问题。

该公司产品组合的第一个组成部分是一系列名为“状态贴纸”的传感器。它们是小型矩形设备，具有坚固的外壳和较长的电池寿命。技术人员可以将它们连接到工业设备上，以监控视觉无法检测到的问题。

机器内部组件的运动会产生往往遵循特定模式的噪音和振动。如果工业风扇的叶片每分钟旋转30次，它可能会每隔两秒发出嘶嘶声。 BrightAI 的状态贴纸可以检测机器何时偏离其通常的操作模式。

传感器将测量结果无线传输到名为 Stateful AI Hub 的设备。它运行人工智能模型来分析数据以查找硬件故障的迹象。据该公司称，随着站点部署的传感器数量的增加，其模型变得更加准确。

BrightAI 提供的软件使公司能够利用无人机镜头来增强传感器的数据。例如，公用事业公司可以使用 BrightAI 驱动的无人机来检测电线杆顶部的侵蚀。该公司的人工智能模型会自动在损坏的组件周围绘制一个正方形，从而使技术人员免去手动分析镜头的麻烦。

该公司表示，其软件还可以通过其他方式收集维护数据。 BrightAI 驱动的无人机可以读取数据中心冷却剂罐等资产上的仪表，以检查其内部压力。此外，对红外摄像头的内置支持使该软件能够发现过热设备。

BrightAI产品组合的第三个核心组成部分是AI可穿戴设备。所谓的有状态可穿戴设备，可以为技术人员提供现场故障排除建议。它还检查他们在检查期间是否遵循安全准则，并自动将维护数据转化为报告。

创始人兼首席执行官亚历克斯·霍金森 (Alex Hawkinson) 表示：“我们的基础设施面临着前所未有的压力，而物理人工智能终于变得足够可靠，可以在该领域发挥作用。” “将这两个事实结合在一起是一个千载难逢的机会。”

BrightAI 表示，其产品监控 50,000 个站点的数十万个工业资产。投资者 GE Vernova 也是该公司的客户，计划在本周的融资中扩大该公司技术的使用。 BrightAI 则将利用这笔资金扩大其国际影响力。

title: Tech stocks fall as Anthropic IPO fails to reignite AI trade
title_en: Tech stocks fall as Anthropic IPO fails to reignite AI trade
author: William Sandlund
article_content:
Global technology stocks fell on Friday after Anthropic’s blockbuster initial public offering failed to reignite the faltering AI trade that powered equity markets to record highs earlier this year.

South Korea’s tech-heavy Kospi and Japan’s Nikkei 225 index led declines in Asia, with both falling more than 5 per cent. In Europe, the Stoxx Europe 600 was down 0.7 per cent, led by an almost 5 per cent drop in ASML, the world’s biggest manufacturer of chipmaking equipment.

The sell-off in Asia and Europe followed declines overnight on Wall Street, where the Nasdaq 100 closed 2.2 per cent lower even as shares in Anthropic, the developer of Claude, surged 17 per cent on their debut.

Anthropic’s listing was billed as a seminal moment for the tech sector, giving investors the chance to gain exposure to one of the world’s leading developers of the technology.

Analysts and investors said that Anthropic’s assured debut was not enough to allay the growing fears over the sustainability of the increasingly debt-fuelled AI boom.

“Normally, the biggest IPOs are done at the peak of the market, not at the bottom,” said Hao Hong, chief investment officer for Lotus Asset Management.

In a sign of investors’ continued nervousness, Anthropic shares were down 5 per cent in pre-market trading on Friday. Futures tracking the Nasdaq indicate the tech-heavy index will drop another 1 per cent at the open on Friday.

In South Korea, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, manufacturers of the memory chips used in AI data centres, both slid more than 5 per cent. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, the world’s biggest contract chipmaker, fell more than 4 per cent.

Taiwan’s main stock index had its worst week since 1991 as it dropped almost 18 per cent and shed more than $500bn in market capitalisation.

Anthropic pressed ahead with its IPO despite the recent weakness in tech stocks that has pushed the Nasdaq down from its most recent record peak in early October.

Albert Saporta, group chief executive of asset manager GAM Holding, noted that Anthropic’s IPO was “priced 25 per cent below the valuations of a few weeks ago”.

“This monstrous capex binge with nobody having a sense of the return on investment is unravelling,” he said.

John Woods, chief investment officer for Asia at Lombard Odier, said declines in Asia showed investors were shifting their emphasis away from hardware suppliers such as chipmakers and towards AI software developers such as Anthropic.

“Anthropic’s IPO was pretty strong,” he said. “Asia’s drop shows the AI trade maturing.”

The declines in Asia mark a sharp reversal for what had been some of the world’s best performers since the start of 2025.

The unceremonious departure of Jensen Huang from Nvidia and the prospect of tightening US restrictions on chip exports had already dented investor sentiment for the region’s chipmakers, crucial to the global AI data centre build-out.

“This trade has been very narrow and very levered,” said Ecaterina Bigos, senior markets strategist at BNP Paribas Asset Management. “At the moment the market is deleveraging whatever they can.”

article_content_zh:
亚洲科技股周五下跌，因为 Anthropic 在纽约创纪录的上市震惊了该地区的股市，并且未能扭转人工智能公司抛售加剧带来的损失。

持有 OpenAI 约 13% 股份的软银股价下跌超过 15%，而日本日经 225 指数下跌近 5%。

台湾主要股指本周下跌近 18%，市值缩水超过 5000 亿美元，预计将迎来 1991 年以来最糟糕的一周。

Anthropic 在全球有史以来规模最大的首次公开募股中筹集了 810 亿美元资金后，股价出现下跌。

这家 Claude AI 制造商的股价周四收盘较 IPO 价格上涨 17%，但纳斯达克 100 指数收盘下跌 2.2%。

期货显示，周五华尔街开盘时，该指数将再下跌 1%。 Anthropic 股价在盘后交易中下跌近 5%，但仍较 IPO 价格上涨 11% 以上。

一些投资者将 Anthropic 的上市解读为人工智能股票牛市即将结束的信号。

莲花资产管理公司首席投资官洪浩表示：“通常情况下，最大的IPO是在市场高峰时进行的，而不是在低谷时进行。”

资产管理公司 GAM Holding 集团首席执行官 Albert Saporta 指出，Anthropic 的 IPO 定价“比几周前的估值低了 25%”。

他表示：“这种可怕的资本支出狂潮正在瓦解，而没有人意识到投资回报。”

Lombard Odier 亚洲首席投资官约翰·伍兹 (John Woods) 认为，亚洲股市的下跌表明投资者正在将重点从芯片制造商等硬件供应商转向 Anthropic 等人工智能软件开发商。

“Anthropic 的 IPO 表现相当强劲，”他说。 “亚洲的下降表明人工智能贸易日趋成熟。”

亚洲的下滑标志着自 2025 年初以来全球表现最佳的一些经济体的情况发生了急剧逆转。

黄仁勋从英伟达的突然离职以及美国收紧芯片出口限制的前景已经削弱了投资者对该地区芯片制造商的信心，而这对于全球人工智能数据中心的建设至关重要。

title: California AG subpoenas Nvidia over Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
title_en: California AG subpoenas Nvidia over Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
author: Katie Nicora
article_content:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta announced an investigative subpoena on chipmaker Nvidia on Thursday following allegations the company's former CEO and co-founder, Jensen Huang, had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

In a press release, Bonta said that the California Department of Justice was investigating whether Nvidia's advanced chips or confidential information were obtained by China. The probe also seeks to determine if Nvidia misled investors and the public, as well as whether the company's actions violated state law, Bonta said.

"The conduct of Nvidia and its former CEO raises bright red flags, including about the ways in which the company may have misled investors," Bonta said in a statement. "Nvidia is in a messy, transnational situation but the underlying principle of our corporate securities law is clear: Companies cannot mislead their investors."

Huang abruptly resigned last week from Nvidia's top leadership role following reports he engaged in extramarital affairs – including one with the alleged Chinese spy and two with subordinates at Nvidia. Huang has agreed to testify before the House and Senate about the affair with Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen Huang). U.S. intelligence officials suspect Alice Huang of being a Chinese spy, according to accounts first reported by the New York Times, but China denies those allegations.

Colette Kress, Nvidia's current CFO, is serving as interim CEO until a permanent replacement for Huang is announced.

CBS News Bay Area reached out to Nvidia for comment about Attorney General Bonta's subpoena and we are waiting on a response.

title_zh: 加州总检察长启动对英伟达及黄仁勋调查
summary_zh: 加州总检察长罗伯·邦塔针对黄仁勋离任丑闻及可能涉及的中国间谍风险，对英伟达发起司法调查传票
article_content_zh:
周四，加州总检察长罗布·邦塔 (Rob Bonta) 宣布对芯片制造商英伟达 (Nvidia) 发出调查传票，此前该公司前首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 被指控与一名疑似中国间谍有染。

邦塔在一份新闻稿中表示，加州司法部正在调查英伟达的先进芯片或机密信息是否被中国获取。邦塔表示，调查还旨在确定英伟达是否误导了投资者和公众，以及该公司的行为是否违反了州法律。

邦塔在一份声明中表示：“英伟达及其前首席执行官的行为发出了明亮的危险信号，包括该公司可能误导投资者的方式。” “英伟达正处于混乱的跨国境地，但我们公司证券法的基本原则很明确：公司不能误导投资者。”

黄上周突然辞去英伟达最高领导职务，此前有报道称他有婚外情，其中一名与所谓的中国间谍有婚外情，两名与英伟达下属发生婚外情。黄已同意就与爱丽丝·黄（与黄仁勋无关系）的风流韵事在众议院和参议院作证。据《纽约时报》首先报道的报道，美国情报官员怀疑爱丽丝·黄是中国间谍，但中国否认了这些指控。

Nvidia 现任首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯 (Colette Kress) 担任临时首席执行官，直至宣布永久接替黄仁勋的人选为止。

CBS 湾区新闻联系了 Nvidia，请其对司法部长 Bonta 的传票发表评论，我们正在等待回复。

article_content:
Anthropic PBC shares were down about 5% in post-market trading as the artificial intelligence developer wrapped up its first day as a public company after a record-setting $107.3 billion offering.

The late moves pared a debut pop of 17% on Thursday, which provided a rare bright spot as the Nasdaq fell 2.2%. The broader market continued on a downward trend into the Asian day, with global stocks poised for their longest losing streak in more than three years, as the AI trade cratered.

While the bright open for the Claude chatbot maker reflected massive investor appetite after a heavily oversubscribed initial public offering, the late slide underscored the volatility facing tech megacaps amidst shifting expectations for enterprise software monetization and high capital expenditure.

Anthropic priced its offering at $83 a share, above an already elevated target range, raising more than $8.1 billion in new proceeds. Backed by major technology giants including Amazon.com Inc. and Alphabet Inc., the company has emerged alongside OpenAI as a linchpin of generative AI infrastructure.

Trading in Anthropic's shares drew intense scrutiny across Wall Street as analysts evaluated whether monumental frontier model development and GPU computing costs can yield sustained profitability. The IPO represents the largest venture-backed tech listing in history, surpassing previous records set by high-profile cloud and social media debuts.

title: Commerce approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies, Rep. Mast says
title_en: Commerce approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies, Rep. Mast says
author: Justin Papp and Katie Tarasov
article_content:
The subagency of the Commerce Department that regulates and enforces exports approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies including Alibaba and Tencent as of May 2026, according to documents released Thursday by the House Foreign Affairs Committee.

Some of those approvals, made by Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security, included sales to companies designated by the Department of Defense as "Chinese Military Companies,"according to the documents. From December through May, companies had made 3.4 million requests for sales of U.S. AI chips to China, the committee reported, citing those made by Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices.

"Over the past month, the administration's handling of chip export controls has put our national security and technology edge at risk. The Bureau of Industry and Security has failed to enforce the rules, and Congress must now conduct rigorous oversight of the administration's policies,"Rep. Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said at a meeting of the panel Thursday at which members voted to release the documents.

Spokespersons for Nvidia and AMD said their companies comply with U.S. export control laws.

Nvidia argued it was following the Commerce Department regulations that were in effect at the time.

A spokesperson from the Bureau of Industry and Security said it shared information with Congress on both approvals and denials of licenses for Nvidia's H200 and comparable chips. "Licensing decisions are the product of deliberation and consultation among multiple U.S. Government agencies,"the spokesperson said.

"The review and licensing process spanned more than half a year, with approvals subject to strict conditions and limited volumes. Despite receiving some licenses, we have since stopped shipping H200s to China,"Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo told CNBC.

On Tuesday, Nvidia reported $2.4 billion in quarterly revenue from H200 and related chip sales in China. In total, customers based in China and Hong Kong made up about 9.5% of all revenue.

"AMD complies with applicable U.S. export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations,"AMD said through a spokesperson.

The approval of 879,000 AI chips is "not that many,"Bernstein Senior Analyst Stacy Rasgon told CNBC, adding that this news is not surprising.

"It doesn't sound to me like they're approving everything they got willy nilly,"Rasgon said of the Commerce Department. With 879,000 approvals out of 3.4 million requested AI chip sales, he added, "There was a process in place, and it sounds like they approved about one out of every four."

Despite a rapid succession of China export controls on AI chips that started under the Biden administration in 2022, Nvidia and AMD both re-engineered some chips to comply and be sold legally in China. And in December, Trump said Nvidia could ship H200s, its older generation Hopper chips, to "approved customers in China"if the U.S. got a 25% cut of sales.

The U.S. then licensed Nvidia H200 sales to Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance and other Chinese companies, although sales were limited because Beijing didn't approve large-scale imports, chip analyst Patrick Moorhead of Moor Insights & Strategy told CNBC last week.

H200 sales numbers remained low due to those restrictions on China's end. Nvidia said H200 shipments to China made up less than 1% of data center revenue for the quarter that ended in July.

"In the grand context of the size of this market and how much they're shipping, it's a rounding error. It's tiny,"Rasgon told CNBC.

The committee cited the Export Control Reform Act as justification for releasing the data. The panel said the law allows it to declassify and release export data if it "determines that the withholding of the following information is contrary to the national interest."

The license requests released by the Foreign Affairs Committee include requests to sell to major firms including ByteDance, Tesla (Shanghai) and Baidu.

The release of documents comes in the wake of Jensen Huang 's resignation from the chip supplier Nvidia after news surfaced that he had several extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy that led to concerns about Nvidia chips being diverted to China.

In the weeks since, Republicans and Democrats in Congress have called for legislation to be passed that would impose stricter export controls on the sale of advanced AI chips to China and other adversaries.

"The license information we are disclosing today will help inform the American public about how BIS has handled licenses for Nvidia H200 and equivalent AMD chips to China. The public has the right to know how these decisions were made,"Meeks said.

Mast said two of the firms listed in Nvidia license applications to BIS — Maginfra and New Matrix — are suspected "smuggling fronts."The New York Times reported in November that both companies had empty offices and had ties to companies under national security sanctions.

"Both are fake companies. If BIS approved the sale of these chips to these firms, obviously that is of tremendous concern to us — especially given that President Trump made clear last year that the sale of any AI chips to China will have very real national security conditions,"Mast said at the Thursday meeting.

Maginfra and New Matrix did not reply to requests for comment.

Shares of AMD fell Thursday after the investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging the company "has its own China problem."The report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the company kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers."

CNBC did not independently verify this information.

Fallout from the Huang scandal on Capitol Hill has intensified in the last week, as lawmakers question the degree to which the former head of Nvidia's relationship with the suspected Chinese spy could have jeopardized national security and American AI dominance.

Huang is due for a closed-door transcribed interview with the House Foreign Affairs panel and two other committees on Dec. 1. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter is scheduled to appear before the panels Dec. 2.

Senate banking committee Chair Tim Scott, R-S.C., announced on CNBC's "Squawk Box"on Wednesday that Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had also agreed to testify.

Lutnick has come under fire over his relationship to Huang and for his failure to take action on Megaspeed, the Singaporean company where Alice Huang, with whom the former Nvidia CEO had an affair, was an executive until 2025. U.S. investigators suspect Megaspeed diverted Nvidia chips to China.

Amid that criticism, the Commerce Department on Monday issued an interim final rule to close a loophole that has allowed Chinese companies to lease Nvidia's advancing computing power from data centers in third countries.

The rule was "written by and at the direction of"the Treasury Department and the White House National Security Council, BIS said in a press release.

— Megan Cassella, Daren Fonda and Kif Leswing contributed to this report.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此事件揭示了美国出口管制政策在‘国家安全利益’与‘企业商业营收’之间的双重困境，BIS通过小批量、附严格条件的许可发放，旨在维持对华算力供给的阈值控制而非完全禁绝。长期看，这一监管动态将迫使芯片巨头加剧对中国市场的战略收缩，同时倒逼中国本土算力供应链在合规审查的真空期内加速进行架构迭代与自主化适配。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This incident exposes the dilemma between national security and corporate revenue; the BIS utilizes low-volume, strictly-conditioned licensing to throttle rather than eliminate AI compute supply to China. This regulatory volatility forces tech giants to reassess market exposure while incentivizing Chinese firms to accelerate domestic architectural self-reliance to mitigate future licensing risks.

article_content_zh:
根据众议院外交事务委员会周四发布的文件，截至 2026 年 5 月，商务部负责监管和执行出口的下属机构已批准向阿里巴巴和腾讯等中国公司出售超过 879,000 颗人工智能芯片。

文件显示，其中一些由商务部工业和安全局批准的批准包括向国防部指定为“中国军工公司”的公司进行销售。该委员会援引 Nvidia 和 Advanced Micro Devices 的数据称，从 12 月到 5 月，各公司已发出 340 万份向中国销售美国人工智能芯片的请求。

“过去一个月，政府对芯片出口管制的处理使我们的国家安全和技术优势面临风险。工业和安全局未能执行这些规则，国会现在必须对政府的政策进行严格监督，”众议员。众议院外交事务委员会民主党领袖、纽约州民主党人格雷戈里·米克斯周四在该委员会的一次会议上表示，会上成员们投票决定公布这些文件。

英伟达和 AMD 的发言人表示，他们的公司遵守美国出口管制法。

英伟达辩称，它正在遵守当时有效的商务部法规。

美国工业与安全局的一位发言人表示，该局与国会分享了有关批准和拒绝 Nvidia H200 及类似芯片许可的信息。该发言人表示：“许可决定是多个美国政府机构审议和协商的结果。”

Nvidia 发言人约翰·里佐 (John Rizzo) 向 CNBC 表示：“审查和许可过程持续了半年多的时间，批准受到严格的条件和数量的限制。尽管获得了一些许可，但我们已停止向中国运送 H200。”

周二，英伟达公布 H200 及相关芯片在中国的季度收入为 24 亿美元。总的来说，中国大陆和香港的客户约占总收入的 9.5%。

AMD 通过发言人表示：“AMD 遵守适用的美国出口管制法律和法规，并维持严格的流程，以确保我们全球业务的合规性。”

Bernstein 高级分析师 Stacy Rasgon 告诉 CNBC，批准的 879,000 个 AI 芯片“并不多”，并补充说这一消息并不令人意外。

“在我看来，他们并不是随意批准他们得到的一切，”拉斯贡谈到商务部时说道。他补充说，在 340 万份 AI 芯片销售请求中，有 879,000 份获得批准，“有一个流程，听起来他们批准了大约四分之一。”

尽管中国自 2022 年拜登政府开始对人工智能芯片实施一系列快速出口管制，但英伟达和 AMD 都重新设计了一些芯片，以符合要求并在中国合法销售。去年 12 月，特朗普表示，如果美国的销售额减少 25%，Nvidia 可以将其老一代 Hopper 芯片 H200 运送给“中国认可的客户”。

Moor Insights & Strategy 芯片分析师帕特里克·穆尔海德 (Patrick Moorhead) 上周向 CNBC 表示，美国随后向阿里巴巴、腾讯、字节跳动和其他中国公司授予了 Nvidia H200 销售许可，但由于北京方面不批准大规模进口，销售量有限。

由于中国市场的限制，H200 的销量仍然很低。 Nvidia表示，截至7月份的季度，H200对中国的出货量占数据中心收入的比例不到1%。

title: Trump ousts cyber director after tech outages spark criticism
title_en: Trump ousts cyber director after tech outages spark criticism

inline_images.caption: Trump ousts cyber director after tech outages spark criticism (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_en: Trump ousts cyber director after tech outages spark criticism (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_zh: Trump ousts cyber director after tech outages spark criticism (摄影：路透社)
inline_images.alt: Trump ousts cyber director after tech outages spark criticism

author: Reuters
article_content:
WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - White House national cyber director Sean Cairncross was "fired" from his job, a person close to the White House said on Thursday, days after technology outages disrupted US air travel, banking and national security systems.

The ouster comes as US President Donald Trump and his administration face mounting scrutiny over their response to the series of disruptions over the past week, including a global outage affecting hundreds of millions of Microsoft users and a nationwide halt to air travel that disrupted more than 18,000 flights.

The dismissal of Cairncross dismissal is the administration's first major personnel move since the outages.

Cairncross oversaw cybersecurity policy and strategy across the federal government. Department of Defense Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies will assume the position temporarily, according to the source.

"The president fully supported firing Sean Cairncross from his position," said the person, who spoke on condition of anonymity.

Cairncross said in a statement on Thursday night it was the "honor of a lifetime to serve" in Trump's administration.

The recent technology disruptions are likely linked to corporate efforts to rapidly patch newly discovered software vulnerabilities in the AI age, cybersecurity experts told Reuters. Advanced AI tools make it easier for companies to uncover weaknesses in their cybersecurity protections.

The top US intelligence official said on Wednesday the disruptions were separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical changes and not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack.

Republican Senator Josh Hawley of Missouri on Tuesday told reporters in Washington the Trump administration should brief lawmakers on the outages so they can "share with the American people what's happening here."

Cairncross was an executive at the Republican National Committee before assuming the cyber director role. His successor will need to be confirmed by the US Senate, which will be controlled by Democrats beginning in January.
