title: Gemini on Mac can now use your computer
title_en: Gemini on Mac can now use your computer
author: Jay Peters
article_content:
Google’s Gemini app for macOS now has computer use, meaning it can help you “get multi-step tasks done across your local files, desktop apps, and the web,” the company says. Google suggests the feature might be useful for things like speeding up workflows, filling in forms, making presentations, and listing items for sale.

Users will be able to decide which of your apps Gemini can access, and be able to follow along as Gemini works because it has its own background window that shows a live preview in your chat, Google says. The feature is rolling out now in English for users in the US.

Gemini is introducing the new feature ahead of Apple launching new restrictions for apps wanting “full disk access” on Mac due to potential risks from AI agents with computer use. A preview of the settings rolled out with this week’s macOS 27.3 beta.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 从对话式AI向代理式AI（Agentic AI）进阶，系统级权限获取是关键技术博弈点。苹果近期针对“全盘访问权限”收紧监管，旨在防御恶意AI入侵，这预示着未来AI Agent生态的竞争将演变为‘算力算法能力’与‘操作系统底层访问策略’的深度制衡。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Transitioning from conversational to agentic AI requires system-level permissions, which is the current critical technical battleground. Apple’s tightening of "Full Disk Access" security against malicious agents indicates that future AI ecosystem dominance will hinge on the trade-off between AI capability and OS-level security access policies.

ai_analysis.digest_en: Google has introduced the "Computer Use" feature to its Gemini app for macOS, enabling the AI to execute multi-step tasks across local files, desktop applications, and the web. article_content_zh:
谷歌的 macOS Gemini 应用程序现在可以在计算机上使用，这意味着它可以帮助你“跨本地文件、桌面应用程序和网络完成多步骤任务”，该公司表示。谷歌表示，该功能可能对加快工作流程、填写表格、进行演示和列出待售商品等有用。

谷歌表示，用户将能够决定 Gemini 可以访问哪些应用程序，并且能够跟随 Gemini 的工作，因为它有自己的背景窗口，可以在聊天中显示实时预览。该功能现已以英语向美国用户推出。

title: Ubisoft Logs Strong Bookings as Players Welcome Assassin’s Creed Remake
title_en: Ubisoft Logs Strong Bookings as Players Welcome Assassin’s Creed Remake
author: Wall Street Journal
article_content:
It's been almost four months now since Ubisoft released their first Assassin's Creed remake in the form of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, a single-player Edward Kenway-focused remake of 2013's Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag.

Black Flag Resynced wound up becoming one of Ubisoft's most successful games in recent years, having sold over 3.5 million copies by its second week alone, and to help keep fans interested in the remake, Ubisoft Singapore recently added New Game+ as well as Nightmare difficulty to the pirate game.

A day after that update launched, AC franchise Head of Content Jean Guesdon released a Fall 2026 Update article detailing the future for the series, with one of the more disappointing revelations being that Ubisoft currently has no other AC remake in development, suggesting that a remake of Assassin's Creed 1 won't be launching alongside its 20th anniversary next year.

Guesdon started the Fall 2026 Update article detailing the AC franchise's new leadership and plans to better connect with the fan community by hosting several closed-door workshops throughout the remainder of the year with "dedicated community members and content creators."

Guesdon additionally announced that the New Game+ update won't be the last players see of new content for Black Flag Resynced as Ubisoft Singapore will be releasing several quality-of-life updates to the game over the next few months.

However, there are no plans to add any more major content for Black Flag Resynced, much to the disappointment of fans hoping to see the Adewale-led Freedom Cry DLC be added to the remake or even feature a brand-new DLC storyline following Edward Kenway as an Assassin in England.

Guesdon went on to detail official new info about the upcoming PvP AC multiplayer game, Codename Invictus, with insiders reportedly responding very positive to the game's prototype parkour, cooperative play, ability to play as multiple famous AC characters, and map design.

Invictus is still a long way away from release, however, and won't likely launch until after the next mainline AC game, Assassin's Creed: Codename Hexe, debuts, with Guesdon reporting that Ubisoft is making steady progress on Hexe and will share more concrete details about the game in 2027.

With 2027 being the 20th anniversary year of the Assassin's Creed franchise, Ubisoft is prepping next year to be chock-full of reveals, updates, rewards, and community events for fans, but one thing fans shouldn't expect to see next year is a remake of Assassin's Creed 1.

In the Fall 2026 Update article, Guesdon acknowledged fan excitement about the potential of other AC remakes following Black Flag Resynced's success but reported that Ubisoft currently has no other AC remakes in active development.

Instead, all AC developer teams are hard at work on "the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles" which includes games that haven't been publicly revealed yet, set in new settings and stories.

While the hint at more brand-new AC games is exciting, the news that no other AC remakes are in active development comes as a disappointment to many fans, as many expected Assassin's Creed 1 to be remade for the franchise's 20th anniversary in November 2027.

Despite starting the franchise, AC1 has been the most neglected game in the series as it hasn't been remastered or rereleased on any gaming platform beyond the seventh console generation.

With the game being nearly 20 years old, Assassin's Creed 1 is the AC game most in need of a proper remake as, while the game's story, gameplay, and visuals were great for 2007, not everything has aged perfectly well.

Most notably, AC1's gameplay feels sluggish and clunky compared to modern AC titles, and it would be nice to see developers like Ubisoft Bordeaux tackle a remake of AC1 given that Assassin's Creed Mirage was meant to harken back AC1's more stealth-focused style of gameplay.

It's unlikely that Ubisoft would be able to start and finish development of an AC1 remake in 2027, but that shouldn't stop them from starting to work on an AC1 remake that could potentially debut in 2028 or 2029.

A remake of AC1 could not only make it easier for younger AC fans to witness Altair and Desmond Miles' stories, but help expand both characters' history with the remake potentially including story elements from Assassin's Creed: Bloodlines, Assassin's Creed: Revelations, and even events only hinted at in games and books such as the backstory of Altair's parents.

Remaking AC1 would also be a good starting point toward the goal of eventually remaking the Ezio trilogy, as those games feature some of the most popular stories of the AC franchise and Ubisoft is sure to want to profit from fans longing to relive the life of Ezio Auditore in a new way.

title_zh: 育碧黑旗重制版销售强劲，暂无后续重制计划
summary_zh: 育碧重制版《刺客信条：黑旗》两周内销量突破350万份，官方明确目前无其他重制项目
article_content_zh:
自育碧以《刺客信条黑旗重新同步》的形式发布第一款《刺客信条》重制版以来，已经过去近四个月了，这是一款以爱德华·肯维为主的 2013 年《刺客信条 IV：黑旗》的单人重制版。

《Black Flag Resynced》最终成为育碧近年来最成功的游戏之一，仅第二周就售出超过 350 万份，为了帮助粉丝保持对重制版的兴趣，育碧新加坡最近在这款盗版游戏中添加了 New Game+ 和 Nightmare 难度。

更新推出一天后，AC 系列内容主管 Jean Guesdon 发布了一篇 2026 年秋季更新文章，详细介绍了该系列的未来，其中一个更令人失望的消息是，育碧目前没有其他 AC 重制版正在开发中，这表明《刺客信条 1》的重制版不会在明年的 20 周年纪念日推出。

Guesdon 在 2026 年秋季更新文章中详细介绍了 AC 系列的新领导层，并计划通过在今年剩余时间内与“专门的社区成员和内容创作者”举办多个闭门研讨会，更好地与粉丝社区建立联系。

Guesdon 还宣布，New Game+ 更新不会是玩家最后一次看到《Black Flag Resynced》新内容，育碧新加坡公司将在未来几个月内发布该游戏的多项生活质量更新。

然而，目前还没有计划为 Black Flag Resynced 添加更多主要内容，这让那些希望看到 Adewale 主导的 Freedom Cry DLC 被添加到重制版中，甚至以爱德华·肯威 (Edward Kenway) 在英格兰扮演刺客的全新 DLC 故事情节的粉丝们感到非常失望。

Guesdon 接下来详细介绍了即将推出的 PvP AC 多人游戏《代号 Invictus》的官方新信息，据报道，内部人士对该游戏的原型跑酷、合作游戏、扮演多个著名 AC 角色的能力以及地图设计反应非常积极。

然而，《成事在人》距离发布还有很长的路要走，直到下一款主线 AC 游戏《刺客信条：代号 Hexe》首次亮相后，它才可能推出。Guesdon 报道称，育碧正在 Hexe 上取得稳步进展，并将在 2027 年分享有关该游戏的更多具体细节。

2027 年是《刺客信条》系列的 20 周年，育碧正在为明年为粉丝们准备大量的揭秘、更新、奖励和社区活动，但粉丝们不应该期望明年看到的一件事是《刺客信条 1》的重制版。

在 2026 年秋季更新文章中，Guesdon 承认继《Black Flag Resynced》取得成功之后，粉丝们对其他 AC 重制版的潜力感到兴奋，但他报告称，育碧目前没有其他正在积极开发的 AC 重制版。

相反，所有 AC 开发团队都在努力开发“刺客信条游戏的下一章”，其中包括尚未公开发布的游戏，以新的背景和故事为背景。

虽然更多全新 AC 游戏的暗示令人兴奋，但没有其他 AC 重制版正在积极开发的消息让许多粉丝感到失望，因为许多人预计《刺客信条 1》将在 2027 年 11 月庆祝该系列 20 周年纪念日进行重制。

尽管推出了该系列，但《AC1》一直是该系列中最被忽视的游戏，因为除了第七代游戏机之外，它还没有在任何游戏平台上进行过重新制作或重新发布。

《刺客信条 1》已经有近 20 年的历史，是最需要适当重制的 AC 游戏，虽然游戏的故事、游戏玩法和视觉效果在 2007 年都很棒，但并非所有内容都已经过时了。

Google parent Alphabet has set initial price guidance for its inaugural bond sales in Hong Kong and Singapore dollars, according to a term sheet seen by Reuters on Thursday.

• Initial price guidance for the Hong Kong dollar portion was set at 4.60% for the 2028 notes, 5.00% for the 2031 notes, and 5.50% for the 2036 notes.

• The starting rates for the Singapore dollar tranche were set at 2.75% for the 2028 notes, 3.25% for the 2031 notes, 3.65% for the 2036 notes, and 4.00% for the 2056 notes.

• Reuters earlier reported that Alphabet was looking to launch its first bond sales in Hong Kong and Singapore dollars, citing two people with knowledge of the matter.

• One of the people said the sales would likely raise at least $2.2 billion, with Alphabet considering minimum sizes of HK$8 billion ($1.02 billion) for the Hong Kong dollar portion and S$1.5 billion ($1.17 billion) for the Singapore dollar portion.

• HSBC and JPMorgan are the joint global coordinators for both the Hong Kong dollar and Singapore dollar sales.

• For the Hong Kong dollar bonds, Bank of China (Hong Kong), ICBC, and Standard Chartered are arranging the sale. DBS, OCBC, and United Overseas Bank will arrange the Singapore dollar bond sale.

• The bonds are expected to be rated "Aa2" by Moody's and "AA+" by S&P, with settlement scheduled for November 19. content_snippet: Alphabet Inc. is returning to the Canadian market with a five-part bond sale, just six months after issuing its first notes in the currency.
summary_en: Alphabet Inc. is planning to raise at least CA$5 billion through a five-part bond sale in the Canadian market, marking its return just six months after its inaugural CA$8.5 billion offering in May. The move is designed to leverage regional liquidity to optimize the company's global treasury and capital structure.

title: London-based Boltz raises $110M Series A
title_en: London-based Boltz raises $110M Series A
author: John Reynolds
article_content:
London-based AI drug discovery startup Boltz has raised a $110m Series A funding round, less than a year after emerging out of stealth.

Boltz is an AI research startup that develops AI models to speed up drug discovery. It was spun out of MIT in the US but is now located in London, employing 40 AI researchers in the capital's King's Cross district.

Bessemer Venture Partners led the round, with existing investors including Andreessen Horowitz, Amplify Partners, Zetta Venture Partners and Obvious Ventures participating.

New investors include Greycroft, F-Prime Capital, Hummingbird and Benchling, joining Nvidia, which also announced an investment earlier this year during Jensen Huang’s visit to the UK. It follows Boltz raising a $28m seed round at the start of the year.

The startup builds software which helps pharmaceutical and biotech researchers design potential drugs and decide which candidates to test in labs.

Its AI models can predict what protein and drug candidates look like when bound together, estimate how strongly they bind, and propose new molecules designed to bind to a target. It develops open-source AI models and other models through its own platform and API.

At MIT, the co-founders released open-source AI models that matched the performance of closed-source models like DeepMind’s AlphaFold3. These models are now part of the default setting for early-stage drug discovery.

Boltz has announced collaborations with Pfizer, GSK, Takeda and Bristol Myers Squibb. Revenue is generated through partnerships and providing access to its platform and models.

It says it will use the funding to invest in compute and data, and expand its team.

Boltz said: ‘We believe we are still just at the beginning of an exponential trajectory in model capabilities. Our upcoming models are already showing substantial improvements in the quality of the molecules they generate. Our long-term goal remains a world where a scientist can go from a therapeutic hypothesis to a human-ready molecule without leaving their computer. Reaching that goal will require further advances in the models and substantial investment in compute and data.’

article_content_zh:
伦敦人工智能药物研发初创公司 Boltz 正式宣布完成 1.1 亿美元的 A 轮融资，距离其走出隐形模式不足一年。

Boltz 是一家专注于开发加速药物发现 AI 模型的前沿研究机构。该公司最初由麻省理工学院（MIT）孵化，现总部设立于英国伦敦国王十字科技核心区，拥有 40 位顶尖人工智能研究员。

本轮融资由 Bessemer Venture Partners 领投，现有投资方 Andreessen Horowitz（a16z）、Amplify Partners、Zetta Venture Partners 与 Obvious Ventures 悉数跟投。

新加入的战略投资机构包括 Greycroft、F-Prime Capital、Hummingbird 与 Benchling；英伟达（Nvidia）亦在今年早些时候黄仁勋访英期间宣布了对该公司的战略投资。此前 Boltz 曾于今年初完成 2800 万美元种子轮融资。

该初创公司构建的软件平台能够协助制药巨头与生物科技科研人员精准设计候选药物，并科学筛选最具潜力的分子进入实验室实测。

其底层 AI 模型能够高精度预测蛋白质与候选药物分子结合时的三维结构形态，准确评估结合亲和力，并主动生成专门针对特定靶点的新型活性分子。公司通过开源模型及其商业化企业平台和 API 两种模式提供能力。

在麻省理工学院期间，联合创始人团队发布了与 DeepMind 旗下 AlphaFold3 性能匹敌的开源前沿模型，这些模型现已成为全球早期药物发现的行业默认基准。

Boltz 已宣布与辉瑞（Pfizer）、葛兰素史克（GSK）、武田制药（Takeda）以及百时美施贵宝（Bristol Myers Squibb）等跨国药企建立深度研发合作。商业化收入主要来自于战略科研合作授权以及企业级平台与模型 API 访问订阅。

Boltz 表示，本轮筹集的资金将重点用于扩大算力基础设施集群、采购前沿生物数据集，并进一步扩充顶尖研究团队。

Boltz 联合创始人表示：“我们坚信模型能力的指数级跃升才刚刚拉开序幕。即将发布的新一代模型在生成分子的成药性质量上已展现出实质性突破。我们的长期愿景是让科学家无需离开电脑，即可从治疗假设直接跃迁到可用于人体临床的候选分子。实现这一愿景需要模型算法的深度演进以及对算力和数据的持续大规模投入。”

title: Chinese tech firms face a double hit as chip shipments stop and overseas cloud access disappears
title_en: Chinese tech firms face a double hit as chip shipments stop and overseas cloud access disappears
author: Maximilian Schreiner
article_content:
The first multimillion-dollar AI data center deals across Asia are already collapsing as tighter US export controls push chipmakers to freeze deliveries. New reporting reveals how Chinese corporations used earlier loopholes for military-adjacent research.

Days after the US Commerce Department closed the cloud loophole for AI chips in the wake of the scandal around former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, the fallout in Asia's tech industry is immediate. Chinese firms had been skirting US sanctions by renting compute capacity in third countries such as Singapore, Malaysia, and Indonesia. Those data centers now need a license from the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), the Commerce Department agency that regulates sensitive technologies and enforces US export controls. Existing operators have a 90-day transition period and must rigorously screen their customers for ties to China.

According to the law firm Sidley Austin, the licensing requirement kicks in at an extremely low threshold equivalent to roughly 300 modern AI chips, while Chinese labs typically need several thousand processors. The Information reports that Beijing-based startup Moonshot AI canceled a $150 million contract with a Southeast Asian cloud provider in Indonesia in response and paused talks on additional deals.

Moonshot had planned to rent a large cluster of Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 chips there starting next year to train its next language model, Kimi K4. Because of the heavy compute demand, the company had agreed to prepay about 50 percent instead of the industry-standard 15 percent. Access to Blackwell chips abroad was already critical for its predecessor model K3, which matched top US models in July and triggered a BIS investigation, The Information also reported.

Bernstein analysts led by Qingyuan Lin are warning of rising training costs, and banks are pulling back too. According to Bloomberg, five lenders are considering dropping out of a $480 million loan for Singapore-based cloud provider Aolani, which was supposed to supply Nvidia chips in Malaysia for TikTok parent ByteDance.

### TSMC and Samsung halt chip shipments to China

Beyond cloud restrictions, the new US rules are also starting to cut physical supply chains. The Financial Times reports that contract manufacturers TSMC and Samsung stopped certain processor shipments to Chinese customers in recent days while they apply for Commerce Department licenses. The move hits Chinese tech firms at a time when they are already struggling with historically high memory chip prices and capacity bottlenecks at domestic foundries such as SMIC. Huawei recently told its customers to source their own memory for its new AI chip.

The new BIS rules block a workaround through independent packaging and testing firms that Chinese chip designers had used to order high-performance processors without getting direct US approval. Samsung's affected customers include ByteDance and Baidu's AI data center unit Kunlun. Exemptions for non-AI chips have also been eliminated, so TSMC and Samsung now need licenses even for advanced smartphone processors from manufacturers including Xiaomi, Oppo, and Vivo. Industry insiders say that is likely to cause significant production delays.

### Alibaba's covert network reached China's military research

A New York Times investigation into the background of the espionage scandal involving Jensen Huang's former mistress Alice Huang shows why Washington tightened controls so aggressively. According to the Times, Alibaba acted as the secret primary customer and financier behind Alice Huang's Singapore-based firm Megaspeed, which bought more than $4 billion worth of Nvidia chips. Nvidia's sales team introduced Alibaba to Alice Huang in 2022.

Through its subsidiary Speedmatrix, Megaspeed operated cutting-edge Nvidia chips on behalf of Alibaba in a data center in Johor built by Malaysian conglomerate YTL, in an analysis by security firm Infrawatch that is said to show this. Megaspeed reportedly sourced the servers from Aivres, a US subsidiary of state-linked Chinese firm Inspur, had them maintained by technicians from Shanghai, and routed data to China through fiber-optic and undersea cables via Singapore. Some chips were reportedly also smuggled physically.

A contingency contract gives Alibaba direct access to all servers, chips, and intellectual property if Megaspeed breaches their agreement. YTL's stock price fell 20 percent amid the investigations.

Alibaba also has a direct connection to Zhejiang Lab in Hangzhou, co-founded in 2017, which links civilian and military research. The lab is run by former Alibaba CTO Wang Jian, a longtime friend of Jensen Huang who also advises the People's Liberation Army's National Defense University, an institution on the US sanctions list.

Researchers at the lab use Nvidia hardware to work on, among other things, AI-driven cyberattacks and automated vulnerability discovery, according to the New York Times. They also work with a Chinese air force academy on war-game simulations against foreign carrier strike groups. Through the state-owned firm Zhejiang Computility and suppliers tied to the business network of Alice Huang and her husband Kang Wei, Alibaba built data centers with export-controlled Nvidia processors for the lab, even though the company officially denies any military use of its services.

title_zh: 美国出口管制收紧，中国AI企业海外算力受阻
summary_zh: 美国商务部实施云端算力出口新规，迫使台积电、三星对华暂停部分先进芯片供应，中国AI企业面临海外算力接入与硬件采购的双重压力
article_content_zh:
由于美国收紧出口管制迫使芯片制造商冻结交货，亚洲首个数百万美元的人工智能数据中心交易已经破裂。新的报告揭示了中国企业如何利用早期的漏洞进行军事相关研究。

因英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋的丑闻，美国商务部关闭了人工智能芯片的云漏洞几天后，亚洲科技行业的影响立竿见影。中国企业一直在通过租用新加坡、马来西亚和印度尼西亚等第三国的计算能力来规避美国的制裁。这些数据中心现在需要获得工业与安全局 (BIS) 的许可，该局是商务部负责监管敏感技术并执行美国出口管制的机构。现有运营商有 90 天的过渡期，并且必须严格筛选其客户是否与中国有联系。

据盛德律师事务所称，许可要求的门槛极低，相当于大约 300 个现代人工智能芯片，而中国实验室通常需要数千个处理器。据 The Information 报道，作为回应，总部位于北京的初创公司 Moonshot AI 取消了与印度尼西亚一家东南亚云提供商价值 1.5 亿美元的合同，并暂停了更多交易的谈判。

Moonshot 计划从明年开始在那里租用大量 Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 芯片来训练其下一个语言模型 Kimi K4。由于计算需求量大，该公司同意预付约 50%，而不是行业标准的 15%。据 The Information 报道，在国外获得 Blackwell 芯片对于其前身型号 K3 来说已经至关重要，该型号于 7 月份与美国顶级型号相匹配，并引发了 BIS 调查。

以林清源为首的伯恩斯坦分析师警告说，培训成本不断上升，银行也在缩减培训成本。据彭博社报道，五家贷款机构正在考虑放弃向新加坡云提供商 Aolani 提供的 4.8 亿美元贷款，该公司本应在马来西亚为 TikTok 母公司字节跳动供应 Nvidia 芯片。

### 台积电和三星停止向中国出口芯片

除了云限制之外，美国新规定也开始削减实体供应链。英国《金融时报》报道称，合同制造商台积电和三星最近几天在申请商务部许可证时停止了向中国客户供应某些处理器。此举对中国科技公司造成了打击，而此时它们已经在努力应对历史高位的存储芯片价格和中芯国际等国内代工厂的产能瓶颈。华为最近告诉其客户为其新的人工智能芯片采购自己的内存。

BIS 新规定阻止了通过独立封装和测试公司的解决办法，中国芯片设计者曾利用这些公司在未获得美国直接批准的情况下订购高性能处理器。三星受影响的客户包括字节跳动和百度的人工智能数据中心部门昆仑万维。非人工智能芯片的豁免也被取消，因此台积电和三星现在甚至需要获得小米、Oppo 和 Vivo 等制造商的先进智能手机处理器的许可。业内人士表示，这可能会导致生产严重延误。

### 阿里巴巴的秘密网络触及中国军事研究

《纽约时报》对黄仁勋前情妇黄爱丽丝间谍丑闻背景的调查揭示了华盛顿为何如此积极收紧控制。据《泰晤士报》报道，阿里巴巴是 Alice Huang 的新加坡公司 Megaspeed 背后的秘密主要客户和金融家，该公司购买了价值超过 40 亿美元的 Nvidia 芯片。 2022 年，英伟达销售团队向 Alice Huang 介绍了阿里巴巴。

安全公司 Infrawatch 的分析据称显示了这一点，Megaspeed 通过其子公司 Speedmatrix 代表阿里巴巴在马来西亚企业集团 YTL 建造的柔佛数据中心运行尖端的 Nvidia 芯片。据报道，Megaspeed 从 Aivres 采购服务器，Aivres 是中国浪潮公司的美国子公司，由上海的技术人员维护，并通过新加坡通过光纤和海底电缆将数据传输到中国。据报道，一些芯片也被实际走私。

如果 Megaspeed 违反协议，阿里巴巴将通过应急合同直接获得所有服务器、芯片和知识产权。调查期间，杨忠礼机构股价下跌 20%。

阿里巴巴还与 2017 年共同创立的杭州之江实验室有直接联系，该实验室将民用和军事研究联系起来。该实验室由阿里巴巴前首席技术官王健负责管理，他是黄仁勋的老朋友，也是中国人民解放军国防大学的顾问，该大学是美国制裁名单上的一个机构。

据《纽约时报》报道，该实验室的研究人员使用 Nvidia 硬件来研究人工智能驱动的网络攻击和自动漏洞发现等。他们还与中国空军学院合作，针对外国航母战斗群进行兵棋模拟。通过国有企业浙江省计算公司以及与爱丽丝黄和她的丈夫康伟的商业网络相关的供应商，阿里巴巴为实验室建造了配备出口管制英伟达处理器的数据中心，尽管该公司官方否认其服务有任何军事用途。

title: Google Built a Giant ‘Mirror Dimension’ Internet to Test Its Chrome AI Agents
title_en: Google Built a Giant ‘Mirror Dimension’ Internet to Test Its Chrome AI Agents
author: Lily Hay Newman
article_content:
As the Google Chrome team has worked to develop AI browsing features using the company's Gemini models, they realized they need to go the extra mile to keep things from going haywire. So they did the only thing they could think to do—they built an expansive alternate-universe internet that they completely control.

“Web-use” agents need to be familiar with the open internet, how to navigate real websites and platforms, and how to be hardened against web attacks. So training them in limited test environments is only so effective. Plus, models can develop what's known as “eval awareness” where they behave differently because they have determined that they are in a test or simulation. On the other hand, setting unrefined agents loose on the open internet is a bad idea. That’s where the alternate-universe internet comes in.

The “Mirror Dimension,” which Google is detailing in a blog post today for the first time, is a sweeping and diverse but isolated web ecosystem that the Chrome team entirely controls. It includes a vast array of websites and platforms—including social media sites, shopping, and bank dashboards—that are built with all the components and attributes of real websites. Browsing assistant agents must interact with the sites and complete tasks in Chrome the way they would on the real internet. And they face resilience tests as they go, like hidden prompt-injection attacks, to test their defenses.

“Agents are not programmed so you can’t predict every possible thing an agent might see, the exploration space that we have to address is huge and the web is hostile,” says Charles Qian, a software engineer on the Chrome AI security team. “Any user can ask any prompt on any website, so we really need to explore that space as thoroughly as we can. And we’ve seen the agent start to develop a mature sense of judgement when it comes to knowing what information is actually needed for a task and when to punt back to the user for a confirmation.”

Building out and populating the Mirror Dimension was a challenge in itself, because it needed to be vast and varied enough to represent the scale of the real web while being developed quickly. To construct it, the Chrome team gathered armies of website and web app development agents guided by a purpose-built AI harness to quickly create realistic web services and data flows—down to details like entering promo codes on a shopping site or populating social media pages.

Even though the entire environment is controlled by Google, Chrome is built with so many user protections and validity checks that in order to allow the agents to use real Chrome (which is crucial for accurate training), the researchers essentially had to hack the browser and take elaborate steps like making forged web certificates for validity checks so the agents could have a normal experience. The team emphasizes, though, that none of these attacks would be possible against regular Chrome users on the open internet. They were all facilitated by the god-mode type access and privilege the team inherently has because they control the entire environment and network.

The researchers say that while the browsing assistant agents they have been testing are benign and do not have cyber capabilities, their goal is to make the Mirror Dimension available to teams across Google so more researchers have access to the safe and controlled environment for testing.

“We’re sharing this approach so other teams both internally and externally think about doing it this way,” says Doug Turner, Google’s director of engineering. “This is the first step, there’s going to be continued investment in this approach to train models. And I would imagine as they become more sophisticated we’ll have to continue working on this environment to make it more and more realistic.”

title_zh: Google构建“镜像维度”环境测试AI智能体
summary_zh: Google Chrome团队构建名为“镜像维度”的封闭互联网仿真系统，用于在完全受控环境中测试与加固Chrome AI浏览智能体
article_content_zh:
当 Google Chrome 团队致力于使用该公司的 Gemini 模型开发人工智能浏览功能时，他们意识到需要付出更多努力来防止事情变得混乱。因此，他们做了他们唯一能想到做的事情——建立了一个完全由他们控制的广阔的平行宇宙互联网。

“网络使用”代理需要熟悉开放的互联网、如何浏览真实的网站和平台，以及如何防御网络攻击。因此，在有限的测试环境中对他们进行培训只是如此有效。另外，模型可以发展所谓的“评估意识”，因为它们已经确定自己处于测试或模拟中，因此它们的行为有所不同。另一方面，在开放的互联网上放置未经改进的代理是一个坏主意。这就是平行宇宙互联网发挥作用的地方。

谷歌今天在博客文章中首次详细介绍了“镜像维度”，这是一个广泛、多样化但孤立的网络生态系统，由 Chrome 团队完全控制。它包括大量的网站和平台，包括社交媒体网站、购物和银行仪表板，这些网站和平台是使用真实网站的所有组件和属性构建的。浏览助理代理必须与网站交互并在 Chrome 中完成任务，就像在真实互联网上一样。他们在前进过程中面临弹性测试，例如隐藏的即时注入攻击，以测试他们的防御能力。

“代理没有经过编程，因此你无法预测代理可能看到的所有可能的事情，我们必须解决的探索空间巨大，而且网络充满敌意，”Chrome AI 安全团队的软件工程师 Charles Qi 说。 “任何用户都可以在任何网站上提出任何提示，因此我们确实需要尽可能彻底地探索这个空间。我们已经看到，在了解任务实际需要哪些信息以及何时返回给用户进行确认时，代理开始形成成熟的判断力。”

构建和填充镜像维度本身就是一个挑战，因为它需要足够庞大和多样化，才能在快速开发的同时代表真实网络的规模。为了构建它，Chrome 团队聚集了大批网站和网络应用程序开发代理，在专门构建的人工智能工具的指导下，快速创建现实的网络服务和数据流——具体到细节，例如在购物网站上输入促销代码或填充社交媒体页面。

尽管整个环境都由 Google 控制，但 Chrome 内置了如此多的用户保护和有效性检查，为了让代理能够使用真正的 Chrome（这对于准确的训练至关重要），研究人员基本上必须破解浏览器并采取复杂的步骤，例如制作伪造的网络证书进行有效性检查，以便代理能够获得正常的体验。不过，该团队强调，这些攻击都不可能针对开放互联网上的普通 Chrome 用户。他们都受到团队固有的上帝模式类型的访问和特权的促进，因为他们控制了整个环境和网络。

研究人员表示，虽然他们测试的浏览助理代理是良性的并且不具备网络功能，但他们的目标是让 Mirror Dimension 可供 Google 的团队使用，以便更多的研究人员能够访问安全且受控的环境进行测试。

谷歌工程总监道格·特纳 (Doug Turner) 表示：“我们正在分享这种方法，以便内部和外部的其他团队考虑这样做。” “这是第一步，我们将继续投资这种训练模型的方法。我想，随着模型变得越来越复杂，我们将不得不继续致力于这个环境，使其变得越来越现实。”

title: Anthropic's historic debut to put AI's promise and peril to Wall St test
title_en: Anthropic's historic debut to put AI's promise and peril to Wall St test

author: Niket Nishant, Manya Saini and Echo Wang
article_content:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Anthropic's record $81 billion IPO brings to Wall Street an avatar of a sector that proponents herald as an economic panacea, while detractors warn it has stoked a market bubble and could ultimately threaten humanity itself.

More immediately, the Claude chatbot maker's debut after securing a $1.5 trillion valuation in the IPO, together with Tuesday's earnings report by AI poster child Nvidia, signals the industry has nominally passed the two big tests facing it this week.

The strong demand for Anthropic shares amid a broader tech selloff offers hope to the sector, even as a rocky market reception for Nvidia results which looked strong at first blush, signals the euphoria around the sector has cooled.

"I've looked at this whole week as a referendum on AI. Nvidia gave us a read on the buildout, and Anthropic is about to give us a read on investor appetite for the next generation of AI companies," Jake Behan, head of capital markets at Direxion, said before the Anthropic debut.

AI technology has boosted economic growth, sparked doomsday warnings and arguably helped usher in a data-center-skeptic Democratic tsunami in the US midterm elections.

Investors who once embraced the boom have turned skeptical in recent weeks over concerns that the enormous spending needed to build out the sector and the incipient crushing debt loads may not be justified by the eventual returns.

An extramarital-affair scandal involving Nvidia's CEO and a spike in Treasury yields have further unnerved investors.

As the first frontier AI company to go public, Anthropic is poised to become the sector's benchmark, with its arch-rival OpenAI reportedly eyeing a 2027 listing.

The company sold 980 million shares at $83 each, pricing the IPO above its initial range of $70 to $78 set when it launched the roadshow. The additional $26 billion raised through a private placement takes the total haul to over $107 billion.

"Some of the demand may simply reflect investors not wanting to miss out on the rare opportunity to gain exposure to a leading AI company, even if its long-term profitability remains uncertain," IPOX associate Lukas Muehlbauer said.

London-based index rebalance analytics firm Intropic estimates passive demand from index-tracking funds will account for about 28% of Anthropic's shares offered, or roughly $19 billion.

When it debuts on the Nasdaq later on Thursday, Anthropic will join the world's trillion-dollar club, alongside technology giants such as Microsoft, Apple and Nvidia.

The listing will also give retail investors a chance to pile into one of the AI industry's hottest names, potentially amplifying swings in the stock as trading begins.

The buzz has already spilled onto prediction markets, where traders are placing bets on everything from its opening pop to where the stock will close on its first day.

Debate has intensified across global markets in recent months over whether the AI boom is veering into bubble territory, with economists, some of the world's biggest CEOs, and political leaders split over its sustainability.

Much of the scrutiny has focused on circular financing arrangements. A complicated web of deals between AI companies, chipmakers, cloud providers and investors has raised questions over how much of the industry's growth is being fueled by money circulating within the same ecosystem.

Anthropic's breakneck growth has so far defied these concerns, but some investors have said they may wait for the initial euphoria to subside before buying.

"It doesn't have to be a bad company for it to be a bad investment at the IPO price," said Nic Puckrin, cross-asset analyst and founder of Coin Bureau.

Anthropic has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Alphabet's Google, underscoring how its rapid growth hinges on securing vast amounts of future computing capacity, some of which relies on financing beyond the company's control.

Investors will be watching Anthropic's debut and subsequent trading closely, with analysts expecting the stock to emerge as a proxy for the broader AI trade as questions over valuations, spending and returns weigh on sentiment.

The company will also need to balance growth with calls to slow the development of advanced AI models over concerns that they pose cybersecurity threats and could be exploited by bad actors to target critical government and private infrastructure.

Anthropic warned in its IPO prospectus that AI could behave unpredictably and advance faster than oversight mechanisms, posing potentially "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity."

article_content_zh:
11 月 19 日（路透社）——Anthropic 创纪录的 810 亿美元 IPO 给华尔街带来了一个被支持者誉为经济灵丹妙药的行业的化身，而批评者则警告称，它煽动了市场泡沫，并最终可能威胁人类本身。

更直接的是，这家 Claude 聊天机器人制造商在 IPO 中获得 1.5 万亿美元估值后首次亮相，再加上周二人工智能典范英伟达的收益报告，表明该行业名义上已经通过了本周面临的两大考验。

在更广泛的科技股抛售中，对 Anthropic 股票的强劲需求给该行业带来了希望，尽管市场对英伟达业绩的反应乍一看很强劲，这表明该行业的乐观情绪已经降温。

Direxion 资本市场主管杰克·贝汉 (Jake Behan) 在 Anthropic 首次亮相前表示：“我将这一整周视为对人工智能的公投。Nvidia 向我们介绍了其扩建情况，而 Anthropic 则将向我们介绍投资者对下一代人工智能公司的兴趣。”

人工智能技术促进了经济增长，引发了世界末日警告，并可以说在美国中期选举中引发了对数据中心持怀疑态度的民主党海啸。

曾经拥抱繁荣的投资者最近几周变得持怀疑态度，因为他们担心建设该行业所需的巨额支出以及初期的沉重债务负担可能无法通过最终回报来证明是合理的。

涉及英伟达首席执行官的婚外情丑闻和美国国债收益率的飙升进一步让投资者感到不安。

作为第一家上市的前沿人工智能公司，Anthropic 有望成为该行业的标杆，据报道其主要竞争对手 OpenAI 也计划于 2027 年上市。

该公司以每股 83 美元的价格出售了 9.8 亿股股票，IPO 定价高于路演时设定的 70 至 78 美元的初始区间。通过私募额外筹集的 260 亿美元使总募资额超过 1,070 亿美元。

IPOX 合伙人卢卡斯·穆尔鲍尔 (Lukas Muehlbauer) 表示：“部分需求可能只是反映出投资者不想错过接触领先人工智能公司的难得机会，即使该公司的长期盈利能力仍不确定。”

总部位于伦敦的指数再平衡分析公司 Intropic 估计，来自指数跟踪基金的被动需求将占 Anthropic 所发行股票的约 28%，即约 190 亿美元。

当周四晚些时候在纳斯达克上市时，Anthropic 将与微软、苹果和英伟达等科技巨头一起加入全球万亿美元俱乐部。

此次上市还将让散户投资者有机会买入人工智能行业最热门的股票之一，这可能会在交易开始时放大该股的波动。

这种热潮已经蔓延到预测市场，交易员对从开盘价到首日收盘价等各个方面进行押注。

title: Anthropic starts trading on Wall Street
title_en: Anthropic starts trading on Wall Street
author: Emma Roth
article_content:
Anthropic has officially gone public. It began trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol “ANT” at $111.50 per share, up from its initial $83 per share price that put company’s value at around $1.5 trillion.

The listing comes nearly a month after Anthropic revealed its plans to go public. In its lengthy S-1 filing, the AI company reported recording an $80.7 billion net loss in the first half of this year, most of which comes from an accounting charge that doesn’t reflect its business, along with $16.3 billion in revenue. The filing outlines plans that Anthropic says will help it develop AI for the benefit of humanity, which includes a governance structure that keeps control of the company in the hands of the founders, rather than the shareholders.

While speaking ahead of Anthropic’s debut at the Nasdaq, CEO Dario Amodei highlighted his stance on AI safety. “To state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control,” Amodei said, according to Reuters. “We will not bend to either business nor political pressure.”

Anthropic’s S-1 filing also listed possible “catastrophic” risks associated with its AI models, including “self-preserving behaviors” like resisting attempts to shut them down. It also warns potential shareholders that its AI models “may behave in unintended, misaligned, or autonomous ways” that can harm Anthropic.

Anthropic recently revealed that, like rival OpenAI, it has experienced incidents of AI agents escaping their testing environment and hacking third-party organizations. In September, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei proposed a plan to slow down the training and development of AI in response to the wave of rogue AI cyberattacks. As part of that plan, it gave safety evaluators at METR “employee-like access” to its internal systems, who found that the company is using AI to accelerate its research and development.

在 Anthropic 在纳斯达克上市之前发表讲话时，首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪强调了他对人工智能安全的立场。据路透社报道，阿莫迪表示：“明确地说，我们将加快人工智能系统的训练和部署步伐，只要有必要，我们就会相信它们是安全的，并将继续处于人类控制之下。” “我们不会屈服于商业或政治压力。”

AMD plunged 9% after Hunterbrook, short the stock, alleged blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT kept shipping BIOS updates carrying newer AMD firmware.

Intel climbed 3% on its first external 18A customer, while NVIDIA edged up 1% as Trump floated future Blackwell sales to China.

Bulls cite AMD's 97% Data Center growth and Lisa Su's record quarter, but bears say unanswered compliance questions invite regulatory scrutiny.

A short seller's export-control allegations turned an early chip rally into a sharp reversal for Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD). AMD stock is trading at $487.80 as of 11:00 a.m. ET on Thursday, down 8% from Wednesday's close. The slide erased an early 3% gain that came as AMD shares rose with the rest of the chip group.

Hunterbrook says it's short AMD. The firm reported that IEIT Systems, a Chinese server maker the U.S. blacklisted in March 2025, kept posting Basic Input/Output System (BIOS) updates containing newer AMD firmware after the blacklisting. The firm said AMD didn't answer its questions and that its findings don't establish an export-law violation. AMD hadn't publicly responded to the report as of this writing.

The broader tech market is rebounding around the Nasdaq debut of Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT), which makes AMD's reversal stand out. Anthropic is one of the lead customers running workloads on AMD's Helios rack-scale systems.

China's access to U.S. AI and server chips was already the market's hottest topic before Hunterbrook published its findings on November 19. President Donald Trump suggested the U.S. could allow sales of NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) Blackwell chips to China in the future, Bloomberg reported. NVIDIA's guidance for Q4 FY2027 already assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China.

Any hint that AMD technology reached a blacklisted firm raises regulatory risk for a company now leaning heavily on server and AI demand. AMD's Data Center segment revenue rose 97% year over year (YoY) to $8.55 billion in Q3 2026. The company has previously cited government export regulations, tariffs and licensing requirements as risks. Executives on the company's November 3 earnings call didn't address China, export controls or restricted entities, leaving the market to consider Hunterbrook's claims without a direct response.

Despite the volatility of AMD stock, Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) stock is still up 5% to $57.38. The company signed its first external customer for its advanced 18A chip process, news that's still lifting the shares. Intel's position as the rival x86 server processor maker adds context while Hunterbrook's allegations weigh on AMD.

NVIDIA stock is at $153.40, up 1.6%, so it's also holding steady despite the big swings of AMD stock today. Measured year to date (YTD), NVDA stock is down 18%.

AMD designs its chips and outsources manufacturing to third-party foundries and contract manufacturers, so its processors move through a wide network of server builders. Under this approach, AMD competes in server central processing units (CPUs) through EPYC and in AI accelerators through Instinct, which it packages together in Helios systems. Reliance on partners can also leave AMD with less direct control over where its technology ends up.

Intel takes the opposite approach, building chips in its own factories. Intel held its October 29 earnings call. On the call, CEO Lip-Bu Tan stated, "We are one of just three advanced-node semiconductor foundries in the world, and the only one domiciled in the United States." The U.S. government holds a significant equity interest in Intel.

NVIDIA, by contrast, is the dominant AI accelerator maker and competes most directly with AMD's Instinct line. Tan has targeted AMD in server processors too, saying Intel's next-generation product "will be ahead of AMD."

AMD's Q4 2026 revenue guidance of approximately $17 billion, plus or minus 3% offers bulls evidence that demand for its Instinct and EPYC chips remains strong. Speaking at the company's November 3 earnings release, CEO Lisa Su declared, "We delivered a record quarter with revenue exceeding the high end of our guidance as Data Center segment sales nearly doubled year-over-year." Hunterbrook's own statement that its findings don't establish an export-law violation gives AMD supporters another argument.

The bears counter that even unresolved questions about blacklisted buyers can invite scrutiny from regulators and customers, and AMD stock already carries high expectations after its run this year. The same AI data-center expansion driving EPYC and Instinct demand also runs through the power, cooling, and networking suppliers we profiled in a free report on seven AI infrastructure names that aren't chipmakers. AMD's next test is whether the company publicly addresses Hunterbrook's findings on IEIT Systems. A cautious approach could make sense for traders considering AMD stock until the export-compliance question around the company resolves.

author: Lisa Fickenscher
article_content:
Amazon customers in New York City will be charged up to $5 more per order if the local government passes a controversial bill aimed at cracking down on employment practices for “last-mile” delivery drivers, the e-tail giant is warning.

Amazon is appealing directly to its Big Apple customers in its fight against the legislation, The Post has learned.

Starting Thursday, they will see messages on Amazon’s website and app warning of higher costs if the bill passes.

Amazon is also urging customers to contact their City Council members, providing a form and link to send direct messages saying they don’t want “slower and more expensive” service.

“As the City Council continues to review this bill, we want to be transparent with our customers about what it would cost them if it passes as written – which is why we’re doing this,” Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel said in a statement.

The appeal marks an escalation from Amazon’s efforts to date, which include months of TV ads about the bill’s potential impact.

The legislation aims to end Amazon’s reliance on subcontractors by requiring the e-commerce giant to get licenses for its 15 last-mile facilities in the city and hire delivery workers as full-timers. Other companies including FedEx would also be subject to the new rules.

The bill would affect over 5,000 delivery workers currently employed by about 40 third-party contractors, according to Amazon.

A supermajority of Council members — and far-left Mayor Zohran Mamdani — support the bill, which comes from Councilwoman Tiffany Cabán (D-Queens).

Proponents claim it would improve worker pay and safety by holding Amazon to a higher standard and making it liable for accidents involving its delivery operations.

Opponents say the legislation could cost thousands of jobs, with a group called New York Delivers threatening legal action earlier this week.

Council Speaker Julie Menin (D-Manhattan) is in active negotiations with Amazon, the Teamsters union – which is advocating for the bill – and the city’s legal counsel, she told The Post last week.

“It’s time for Amazon to adhere to a licensing framework that ensures fair pay, strong worker protections, and more responsible delivery practices,” the lawmaker said.

Amazon has threatened to move its distribution centers outside the city to avoid the direct-hire mandate — saying it would have to fire some 2,000 warehouse workers who staff them — if the bill becomes law.

“We’re hopeful that this bill doesn’t pass as written, but so far, key City Council members seem uninterested in learning about our delivery operations and they haven’t taken us up on our offer to visit our sites and talk with the small businesses that work out of them every day,” Nantel said.

Some co-sponsors have begun to express concerns about the potential for job losses. Councilman Phil Wong (D-Queens) withdrew his support for the bill over that issue, as The Post previously reported.

动因背景：端到端低延迟全双工语音架构打破传统级联瓶颈，以极低边际成本加速多模态实时交互在各端侧应用场景的规模化普及。
key_points_en: Key Development: Amazon warns NYC customers they face price hikes up to $5 for every order if delivery bill is passed

article_content_zh:
电子零售巨头警告说，如果当地政府通过一项旨在打击“最后一英里”送货司机雇佣行为的有争议的法案，纽约市的亚马逊客户每笔订单将被收取最多 5 美元的费用。

据《华盛顿邮报》获悉，亚马逊正在直接向其纽约客户发出呼吁，反对这项立法。

从周四开始，他们将在亚马逊网站和应用程序上看到消息，警告如果该法案通过，成本将更高。

亚马逊还敦促顾客联系他们的市议会成员，提供表格和链接来发送直接消息，表示他们不想要“更慢、更昂贵”的服务。

亚马逊发言人凯利·南特尔（Kelly Nantel）在一份声明中表示：“随着市议会继续审查这项法案，我们希望对客户保持透明，让他们知道如果该法案按规定通过，他们将付出什么代价——这就是我们这样做的原因。”

此次上诉标志着亚马逊迄今为止所做努力的升级，其中包括数月来宣传该法案潜在影响的电视广告。

该立法旨在结束亚马逊对分包商的依赖，要求这家电子商务巨头为其在该市的 15 个最后一英里设施获得许可证，并雇用全职送货员。包括联邦快递在内的其他公司也将受到新规则的约束。

据亚马逊称，该法案将影响目前约 40 家第三方承包商雇用的 5,000 多名送货工人。

绝大多数议员——以及极左翼市长佐兰·马姆达尼（Zohran Mamdani）——支持该法案，该法案由女议员蒂芙尼·卡班（D-Queens）提出。

支持者声称，通过让亚马逊遵守更高的标准并让其对涉及其送货业务的事故承担责任，可以提高工人的工资和安全。

反对者表示，这项立法可能会导致数千人失业，一个名为“纽约交付”的组织本周早些时候威胁采取法律行动。

议会议长朱莉·梅宁（曼哈顿民主党）上周告诉《华盛顿邮报》，她正在与亚马逊、倡导该法案的卡车司机工会以及该市的法律顾问进行积极谈判。

这位立法者表示：“亚马逊是时候遵守许可框架了，以确保公平的薪酬、强有力的工人保护和更负责任的交付实践。”

亚马逊威胁称，如果该法案成为法律，它将把其配送中心迁往城外，以避免直接雇用的规定，并表示将不得不解雇约 2000 名为其配备的仓库工人。

title: Binance Secures $6.5 Billion Freezing Order From Abu Dhabi Court
title_en: Binance Secures $6.5 Billion Freezing Order From Abu Dhabi Court

inline_images.caption: Binance SAFU
inline_images.alt: Binance SAFU

author: Bloomberg
article_content:
Binance announced the court action on November 18, saying its legal representatives had identified approximately 26,000 cryptocurrency wallet addresses associated with stolen assets. The exchange plans to maintain an updated list as investigators trace funds moving between wallets and blockchains.

The injunction follows an attack that Binance valued at approximately $6.34 billion. The company previously reported that about $2.85 billion had been frozen or intercepted, leaving substantial assets outside its immediate control.

The ADGM Courts granted a worldwide freezing injunction against unidentified defendants accused of carrying out the theft, alongside separate proprietary injunctions and delivery-up orders intended to support asset recovery.

The $6.5 billion represents the amount covered by the legal order, not the value of cryptocurrency already secured. A freezing injunction restricts dealings with covered assets, while delivery-up orders provide a mechanism for requiring identified assets to be returned.

Some orders involve named parties that previously froze assets linked to the attack. Binance has not alleged wrongdoing by those parties, which include entities cooperating with recovery efforts.

The exchange said certain stablecoin issuers, cryptocurrency exchanges and other intermediaries require judicial authorization before transferring frozen assets to a claimant. The new orders are intended to provide that legal basis where applicable.

Gibson Dunn, the law firm representing Binance, said the orders can be served through blockchain transactions. Its lawyers also described the approximately 26,000 identified wallet addresses as a continuously updated list designed to help intermediaries recognize and restrict stolen funds.

However, identifying an address does not automatically establish that its current balance is recoverable. Effective enforcement depends on the relevant jurisdiction, the assets involved and whether an intermediary can prevent further transfers.

The $6.5 billion figure measures the injunction’s legal scope rather than Binance’s recovered assets. The financial benefit will depend on how much previously frozen cryptocurrency can actually be returned and whether additional stolen funds can be intercepted.

Binance’s earlier incident report placed the total value of affected cryptocurrency at approximately $6.34 billion, with around $2.85 billion frozen or intercepted as of November 3.

The US Department of Justice subsequently announced on November 12 that coordinated government and private-sector efforts had frozen more than $2.7 billion, including more than $1.2 billion covered by US court authorization to seize or restrain assets.

Those figures should not be added together. The American enforcement actions concern assets within the broader pool of stolen cryptocurrency, and the announcements do not establish how much of the funds is independently covered by the different legal proceedings.

As FinanceFeeds previously examined, frozen assets are not equivalent to returned funds. Ownership, custody arrangements and judicial procedures can delay recovery even when issuers or exchanges have successfully restricted transfers.

The challenge is particularly pronounced for bitcoin and ether, which lack the centralized issuer controls available for freezing certain stablecoins. Funds held in self-custodied wallets generally cannot be immobilized merely by obtaining a court order.

Separately, Binance announced on November 12 that it had completed coverage of assets affected by the breach, using its corporate treasury, part of its Secure Asset Fund for Users and surplus futures insurance-fund resources.

The exchange also published a new proof-of-reserves snapshot covering 198 tokens. Replenishing customer-facing reserves is nevertheless distinct from recovering the original stolen cryptocurrency.

Successful asset recovery could eventually offset part of the resources Binance deployed to cover the breach. But the exchange does not publish comprehensive audited financial statements, limiting investors’ ability to assess the incident’s ultimate effect on its liquidity, capital and profitability.

The October attack involved unauthorized access to Binance’s internal wallet-signing infrastructure. The exchange’s investigation identified a multistage intrusion involving compromised employee systems, malicious software and unauthorized transaction approvals.

FinanceFeeds previously reported on the compromised development infrastructure and the technical weaknesses that allowed attackers to initiate unauthorized transfers.

The US Justice Department attributed the theft to North Korean military-linked actors known as TraderTraitor. Investigators said the stolen assets were being moved through bridges, mixers and cryptocurrency exchanges, complicating efforts to identify and restrain them.

The evolving wallet-address list could help exchanges and stablecoin issuers identify suspicious deposits before the funds are transferred again. However, tracing cryptocurrency across multiple networks does not establish that investigators retain control over the assets.

Binance’s legal action also comes as the exchange attempts to restore normal operations and continue its international expansion. In a separate development, FinanceFeeds reported that Binance is preparing to enter five additional Asian markets in 2027 while maintaining that it does not need fresh capital following the breach.

For institutional customers, the outstanding considerations extend beyond the size of the injunction. They include the effectiveness of Binance’s revised custody controls, the timing of remaining withdrawal-service restorations and the extent to which the company can recover funds without disrupting its operating reserves.

The ADGM orders strengthen Binance’s legal recovery options but cannot prevent every transfer of stolen cryptocurrency. The most useful indicators of progress will be independently verifiable asset returns, updated recovery balances and evidence that the exchange’s security and liquidity measures remain effective.

key_points_en: Key Development: Binance Secures $6.5 Billion Freezing Order From Abu Dhabi Court

article_content_zh:
币安于 11 月 18 日宣布向法院提起诉讼，称其法律代表已识别出约 26,000 个与被盗资产相关的加密货币钱包地址。该交易所计划在调查人员追踪钱包和区块链之间流动的资金时维护一份更新的清单。

该禁令是在币安遭受一次价值约 63.4 亿美元的攻击之后发布的。该公司此前报道称，约 28.5 亿美元已被冻结或截获，导致大量资产处于其直接控制范围之外。

阿布扎比国际金融中心法院对被指控实施盗窃行为的身份不明的被告颁布了全球冻结令，同时还颁布了单独的专有禁令和交付令，旨在支持资产追回。

65 亿美元代表法律命令涵盖的金额，而不是已获得保护的加密货币的价值。冻结令限制了受保护资产的交易，而交割令则提供了要求返还已识别资产的机制。

一些命令涉及先前冻结与攻击有关的资产的指定方。币安并未指控这些当事方有不当行为，其中包括配合恢复工作的实体。

该交易所表示，某些稳定币发行人、加密货币交易所和其他中介机构在将冻结资产转移给索赔人之前需要获得司法授权。新命令旨在提供适用的法律依据。

币安的代表律师事务所 Gibson Dunn 表示，这些订单可以通过区块链交易来交付。其律师还将大约 26,000 个已识别的钱包地址描述为一个不断更新的列表，旨在帮助中介机构识别和限制被盗资金。

然而，识别地址并不会自动确定其当前余额是可恢复的。有效执行取决于相关司法管辖区、所涉及的资产以及中介机构是否可以阻止进一步转移。

65 亿美元的数字衡量的是禁令的法律范围，而不是币安追回的资产。经济利益将取决于之前冻结的加密货币实际上可以返还多少，以及是否可以拦截额外的被盗资金。

币安早些时候的事件报告显示，截至 11 月 3 日，受影响的加密货币总价值约为 63.4 亿美元，其中约 28.5 亿美元被冻结或截获。

美国司法部随后于 11 月 12 日宣布，通过政府和私营部门的协调努力，已冻结了超过 27 亿美元，其中包括美国法院授权扣押或限制资产的超过 12 亿美元。

这些数字不应该加在一起。美国的执法行动涉及更广泛的被盗加密货币中的资产，公告并未确定不同法律程序独立涵盖了多少资金。

正如 FinanceFeeds 之前所研究的那样，冻结的资产并不等于返还的资金。即使发行人或交易所成功限制了转让，所有权、托管安排和司法程序也可能会延迟恢复。

对于比特币和以太币来说，这一挑战尤其明显，因为它们缺乏可用于冻结某些稳定币的集中发行人控制。自我托管钱包中的资金通常不能仅仅通过获得法院命令来冻结。

title: ChatGPT can transcribe as you speak now with Live Dictation
title_en: ChatGPT can transcribe as you speak now with Live Dictation
author: Stevie Bonifield
article_content:
ChatGPT can receive audio prompts from your microphone faster now with a Live Dictation feature that transcribes as you speak, rather than waiting until you finish recording. It’s rolling out now globally on all ChatGPT plans on the web, desktop app, and iOS and Android apps. While using dictation in ChatGPT, you can tap or click the audio waveform to show the live text transcript the AI is generating, then edit it in the prompt box when you’re done.

Along with faster transcription, OpenAI also announced it’s removing the 10-minute recording limit on voice dictation in ChatGPT, and it says the feature is getting “more reliable.” The update follows an overhaul for ChatGPT’s two-way conversational voice mode earlier this year. Last year, OpenAI also announced a “record mode” for transcribing voice notes and meetings. That feature is still in beta and limited to Plus, Enterprise, Edu, Business, and Pro workspaces, but you can also use ChatGPT’s prompt box dictation feature to ask it to transcribe voice messages or turn them into bullet points.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI在其ChatGPT全平台（Web、桌面端、iOS及Android应用）正式上线“实时听写（Live Dictation）”功能，支持边说话边生成实时转录文本。同时，OpenAI取消了语音录入原有的10分钟时长限制，旨在提升长音频处理的可靠性与人机交互效率。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI has officially launched the 'Live Dictation' feature across all ChatGPT platforms (Web, Desktop, iOS, and Android), enabling real-time text transcription as users speak. Additionally, OpenAI has removed the previous 10-minute recording limit for voice dictation to enhance reliability and efficiency in handling long-form audio input.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 语音交互是AI从“聊天机器人”向“生产力助手”转型的核心路径，实时转录能力的深化显著降低了多模态交互延迟。此举意在通过降低输入摩擦力，进一步粘合专业领域用户，并为后续的实时多模态深度集成奠定用户习惯。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Voice interaction is the core bridge for AI to evolve from a chatbot to a productivity assistant, with real-time transcription significantly reducing multimodal latency. This move aims to minimize input friction, improve retention for professional users, and build user behavior for future deep-integrated multimodal interactions.

article_content_zh:
ChatGPT 现在可以通过实时听写功能更快地从麦克风接收音频提示，该功能可以在您说话时进行转录，而不是等到您完成录音。它现已在全球所有 ChatGPT 计划的网络、桌面应用程序以及 iOS 和 Android 应用程序中推出。在 ChatGPT 中使用听写时，您可以点击或单击音频波形来显示 AI 生成的实时文本记录，然后在完成后在提示框中进行编辑。

除了更快的转录之外，OpenAI 还宣布取消 ChatGPT 中语音听写的 10 分钟录音限制，并表示该功能正在变得“更加可靠”。此次更新是在今年早些时候对 ChatGPT 的双向对话语音模式进行彻底修改之后进行的。去年，OpenAI 还宣布了一种用于转录语音笔记和会议的“录音模式”。该功能仍处于测试阶段，仅限于 Plus、Enterprise、Edu、Business 和 Pro 工作区，但您也可以使用 ChatGPT 的提示框听写功能要求其转录语音消息或将其转换为要点。

【各方立场与态度】针对长会议与笔记场景优化，提升交互可靠性。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] Lowering input friction, optimizing transcription experience, and improving long-form interaction efficiency
[Key Fact Detail] Live dictation deployed across all platforms.
[Key Position & Outlook] Optimized for meetings and notes with improved reliability.

title: Anthropic IPO Said to Give Nothing to Most Institutional Buyers
title_en: Anthropic IPO Said to Give Nothing to Most Institutional Buyers
author: Bloomberg
article_content:
A version of this article appeared in CNBC's Inside Wealth newsletter, a weekly guide to the high-net-worth investor and consumer. Sign up to receive future editions, straight to your inbox.

The average Anthropic employee could be worth over $40 million after the company's IPO today, with over 400 employees likely to be worth over $100 million, according to SEC filings and investors.

At a share price of $83, Anthropic's market value would top $1.4 trillion, making it one of the 10 most valuable companies in the U.S. It will not only be the largest IPO in history by dollar amounts, but it is also shaping up to be one of the most rapid wealth creation events in history.

Follow CNBC' s live coverage of Anthropic's IPO and Nasdaq debut

Anthropic was founded just five years ago and has only 5,300 employees. According to SEC filings, the artificial intelligence company has generated 1.77 billion options for employees, with a strike price of $2.91 a share. It has also paid out over 1 billion restricted stock units.

If the stock trades at $83 a share, the combined wealth of Anthropic employees will be around $232 billion, based on their share count in the filings. The total works out to an average of $44 million per employee.

Yet because many of the employees are later hires, earlier employees could have supersized gains since they've accumulated more stock. According to investors in the company, at least 400 early employees will be worth $100 million or more at a $83 share price. Several could become billionaires, they said.

The employee total doesn't include the seven founders, who each own between 230 million and 240 million shares, which will each be worth around $20 billion based on a $83 share price.

While employees face complex lockup periods and vesting schedules, the wealth is likely to start making its way into the economy quickly, economists say. The first two areas will be the San Francisco real estate market and philanthropy.

Brokers say San Francisco's already red hot real-estate market will get a boost from hundreds of Anthropic employees who now have more liquid stock they can borrow against. An analysis by Redfin found that Anthropic's current and former employees will have enough post-IPO wealth to buy 9% of all the homes in San Francisco.

Anthropic's culture of effective altruism, along with its generous matching program for charitable gifts of employee shares, are expected to spark a wave of giving, especially to donor-advised funds. Employees hired before May 17, 2024 can pledge up to 50% of their vested shares for a 3-to-1 match by the company. Later hires can pledge up to 25% for a 1-to-1 match.

The seven co-founders have also pledged 80% of their wealth to charity.

"Philanthropy could be the piece that's different this time,"said Michael Faust, president of wealth management at Bailard Inc. "Some of the companies going public now really encourage their employees to give, and they match it. That could make a huge difference for Bay Area nonprofits for a long time to come."

title_zh: Anthropic IPO引发史上罕见财富增长
summary_zh: Anthropic上市估值超1.4万亿美元，员工及早期投资者资产大幅跃升，引发旧金山地产等行业连锁反应
article_content_zh:
本文的一个版本出现在 CNBC 的 Inside Wealth 时事通讯中，这是一份针对高净值投资者和消费者的每周指南。注册接收未来版本，直接发送到您的收件箱。

根据美国证券交易委员会 (SEC) 备案文件和投资者的数据，在公司今天 IPO 后，Anthropic 员工的平均身价可能超过 4000 万美元，其中 400 多名员工的身价可能超过 1 亿美元。

以 83 美元的股价计算，Anthropic 的市值将突破 1.4 万亿美元，成为美国最有价值的 10 家公司之一。这不仅将是历史上金额最大的 IPO，而且也将成为历史上最快速的财富创造事件之一。

关注 CNBC 对 Anthropic 首次公开募股和纳斯达克上市的现场报道

Anthropic 成立仅五年，仅有 5,300 名员工。根据 SEC 备案文件，这家人工智能公司已为员工产生了 17.7 亿份期权，执行价格为每股 2.91 美元。它还支付了超过10亿个限制性股票单位。

如果股票交易价格为每股 83 美元，根据文件中的股份数量，Anthropic 员工的总财富将约为 2,320 亿美元。总金额平均为每位员工 4,400 万美元。

然而，由于许多员工都是后来聘用的，早期员工可能会因为积累了更多股票而获得巨大收益。据该公司投资者称，以 83 美元的股价计算，至少 400 名早期员工的身价将达到 1 亿美元或更多。他们说，有几个人可能成为亿万富翁。

员工总数不包括七位创始人，他们每人拥有 2.3 亿至 2.4 亿股股票，按照 83 美元的股价计算，每人的价值约为 200 亿美元。

经济学家表示，虽然员工面临复杂的禁售期和兑现时间表，但财富可能会开始迅速进入经济。前两个领域将是旧金山房地产市场和慈善事业。

经纪人表示，旧金山已经炙手可热的房地产市场将得到数百名 Anthropic 员工的提振，他们现在拥有更多流动性股票，可以借用。 Redfin 的一项分析发现，Anthropic 的现任和前任员工在 IPO 后将拥有足够的财富来购买旧金山 9% 的房屋。

Anthropic 的有效利他主义文化，加上其慷慨的员工股票慈善捐赠匹配计划，预计将引发一波捐赠浪潮，尤其是捐赠者建议的基金。 2024年5月17日之前入职的员工可以质押最多50%的既得股份，由公司进行3对1的匹配。后来的员工可以承诺为 1 对 1 的匹配提供高达 25% 的奖励。

七位联合创始人还承诺将其 80% 的财富捐给慈善机构。

贝拉德公司(Bailard Inc.)财富管理总裁迈克尔·福斯特(Michael Faust)表示：“这次慈善事业可能会有所不同。一些上市公司现在确实鼓励员工捐赠，而且他们也做到了这一点。这可能会在未来很长一段时间内为湾区的非营利组织带来巨大的变化。”

title: The European Commission confirms a cyberattack that disrupted systems for 10+ days; CERT-EU says international hackers used AI penetration testing tool ARTEX (Gerardo Fortuna/Politico)
title_en: The European Commission confirms a cyberattack that disrupted systems for 10+ days; CERT-EU says international hackers used AI penetration testing tool ARTEX (Gerardo Fortuna/Politico)

inline_images.caption: Brussels Playbook
inline_images.alt: Brussels Playbook

inline_images.caption: infographic
inline_images.alt: infographic

author: Politico
article_content:
POLITICO’s must-read briefing on what's driving the day in Brussels, by Gerardo Fortuna, Nicholas Vinocur and Gabriel Gavin.

CIAO THERE. Gerardo Fortuna back with you on a day when millions will be glued to “GTA VI” — and half the Brussels bubble will be wondering which Commission directorate that is.

WHAT THE WORLD IS WATCHING THIS MORNING: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are due to begin their trilateral meeting in Shenzhen soon after Playbook hits your inboxes. Trump and Putin had an informal meeting a short while ago, which began with a warm handshake. “He’s my friend,” Trump said as he approached the Russian leader. Trump then headed for a bilateral with Xi before the three-way meeting begins around 7:30 a.m. Brussels time.

— Europe has picked its Ukraine negotiating team, but now comes a tougher challenge: getting the Coalition of the Willing to deliver.

— MEPs say Beijing is stepping up intimidation over Taiwan — and Roberta Metsola is putting their complaints to China.

On today’s Brussels Playbook Podcast: Zoya and Kathryn discuss the striking optics of Trump, Putin and Xi meeting in China as European leaders gather in Berlin to fight for Ukraine’s future.

**A message from the European Commission’s Directorate-General for Education, Youth, Sport and Culture: Europe's present and future are shaped in classrooms. On 20 November 2026, the European Education and Skills Summit will offer glimpses of the ‘Schools for tomorrow’ and discuss urgent action to future-proof education in the era of AI. Learn more and follow the Summit online here.**

— HUGE CYBERATTACK HITS THE EUROPEAN COMMISSION: The incident has potentially compromised swaths of personal data, left staff unable to input salary and leave information and prompted the most senior officials to discuss the crisis at their weekly meeting yesterday.

“The Commission believes it has contained most of the attack, but the full extent of any damage remains unclear,” an EU official, granted anonymity because of the sensitivity of the issue, told Playbook. “The systems may be coming back online. The answers are taking a little longer.”

Weapon of choice: The EU institutions’ cybersecurity watchdog, CERT-EU, detected earlier this month that international hackers used ARTEX, a publicly available AI-powered tool designed to identify vulnerabilities in IT systems. “Some actors misuse such tools and have targeted the Commission,” the EU official added. As a precaution, several applications were temporarily taken offline. Access to most has now been restored.

“The European Commission has taken the necessary steps in response to a detected cyber campaign,” Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier told Playbook. “Individual systems were targeted and, in line with our standard practice, we have informed those concerned.”

Investigators are still trying to establish whether staff data was compromised, according to the first EU official. The official said the uncertainty explains the limited communication to staff — because the Commission doesn’t yet know whether, or to what extent, personal information was hacked.

Disruption has lasted over 10 days. Sysper, the Commission’s HR platform for payslips, leave requests and timesheets, and MyPMO, its medical reimbursement system, were restored earlier this week — though Sysper briefly crashed again yesterday. Translation services were also hit on Tuesday, prompting one particularly inconvenienced official to admit to “swearing a lot.”

All the way to the top: The Commission convened its highest-level internal crisis-management body, the Corporate Management Board, for an urgent meeting over these “ongoing cyber incidents” earlier this month, according to a leaked internal mail seen by Playbook. The digital services department ordered stepped-up security checks. And tech commissioner Henna Virkkunen briefed counterparts at yesterday’s College of Commissioners meeting on the immediate response, two officials said.

This is the latest in a series of high-profile global cyberattacks or outages in recent days, including disruptions affecting Microsoft, large U.S. banks and America’s National Security Agency, as well as a hack that targeted popular websites such as those of Air France, the BBC and Zoom.

But did you get paid? Playbook asked around, and the answer was largely yes. While salaries landed as usual, some officials couldn’t submit timesheets or request leave. Three officials also complained about the lack of communication. In a reply to an issue with Sysper seen by Playbook, IT cited a general issue affecting the system’s functionality — without mentioning a cyberattack. Thanks to Max Griera, Nicholas Vinocur, Sebastian Starcevic and Zoya Sheftalovich, who assisted me with this report.

SPAIN’S ELECTORAL BATTLEGROUNDS: From Seville to Murcia and beyond, POLITICO crunched the results of every congressional election in Spain’s history to identify five places that could reveal where this month’s vote is heading.

DOWN TO THE WIRE: With just one day to go before Friday’s summit with the U.K., EU ambassadors failed to finalize a joint statement yesterday evening. Now they’ll need an extra round of talks to nail down the text and finish preparations.

In the meantime … this deep dive by my colleagues in London on Andy Burnham’s grand strategy on Europe is well worth a read.

GAME ON: “Grand Theft Auto VI” launches today, 13 years after the last edition came out — but why should Eurocrats care? POLITICO’s Eliza Gkritsi has six reasons why even they should pay attention.

EPP MOVES TO SUSPEND VUČIĆ’S PARTY: The EPP leadership wants to suspend the associate membership of the Serbian Progressive Party, the political home of former President Aleksandar Vučić, giving it a year to break with Moscow and Beijing and improve democratic standards or face expulsion.

EUROPE SEEKS SPECIFICS: We have an answer to the question “Who represents Europe in talks on Ukraine?” We don’t yet have answers to the questions “What will that look like?” and “Will it be effective?”

Double events: After the three-way talks between Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping — and as the Coalition of the Willing meets in Berlin today — Europe is trying to decide what its negotiators can and cannot offer if they get into a room with Russia.

The who: EU leaders last week settled on a team made up of officials from five major countries plus top officials from NATO, the European Commission and Council.

The what: But agreeing on which line the European team should take is proving divisive. Some countries, led by Austria, are advocating a looser approach involving the likes of limited or partial ceasefires to pave the way for a wider truce, or offering to set up an international forum to monitor any peace agreement, Nick and Zoya report.

Others disagree with that approach: “We have to agree on the ceasefire and, when the guns go silent, then we negotiate on the long-lasting peace,” Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys said.

Unwilling? Things are no more settled in the Coalition of the Willing, the alliance of more than 35 nations supporting Kyiv. As Tim Ross and Esther Webber write, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy will find himself among a motley assembly of countries, convened by two weak European leaders (Emmanuel Macron and Friedrich Merz) and a rookie without a mandate (Andy Burnham).

Budget protection: Merz, with an eye on the future, is pushing to make the EU’s long-term budget “Le Pen-proof.” Germany wants to lock into the MFF a durable funding scheme for Ukraine that will be difficult for potential opponents to veto, James Angelos and Gregorio Sorgi write.

**Europe’s health care sector is at a turning point. Join policymakers, industry leaders and experts in Brussels for POLITICO Health Care Summit on December 1–2 to explore how Europe can balance innovation, access and security as new health care policies take shape. Apply to join us onsite.**

On Friday, it’s the EU-U.K. summit in Brussels. Are such meetings new? Of course, the U.K. didn’t need a special summit when it was part of the EU. The first post-Brexit summit between the two sides was held in London in May 2025 (when Keir Starmer was prime minister) and focused on setting up a “new Strategic Partnership.” This year, new PM Andy Burnham wants a wider reset of ties with the bloc — and has even opened the door to a British return to the EU.

TALK TO PLAYBOOK: WhatsApp us on +32 491 050629 and listen from 7 a.m. to hear if we give you a shout-out.

** What's at stake at the EU-U.K. Summit? Join POLITICO’s policy experts on Thursday, Nov. 19, at 4 p.m. CET for an exclusive online Pro Briefing on what to watch on Friday and how the outcome could shape EU-UK relations. Sign up here. **

BRUSSELS FEELS A CHINA CHILL: European Parliament President Roberta Metsola contacted Chinese authorities after MEPs reported pressure from Beijing, her spokesperson Jüri Laas said.

Piling up: Seven MEPs told Max Griera and Carlo Martuscelli about what they described as intimidation inside Parliament offices as well as detention at the Chinese border and threatening letters, mostly concerning engagement with Taiwan.

“I have never encountered such behavior from foreign diplomats,” said Engin Eroglu, chair of Parliament’s delegation to China. The Chinese mission to the EU did not respond to a request for comment.

No grace period: The incidents come just over a year after Parliament and Beijing ended a four-year freeze in relations over China’s sanctions on lawmakers who criticized China’s human rights record.

Surprise visit: Patriots for Europe Vice Chair António Tânger Corrêa said a senior Chinese diplomat visited his office unannounced before a trip to Taiwan, warning that they “could not ensure” his safety. And lawmakers who attended a Taipei event received letters, seen by POLITICO, urging them to “refrain from any official exchange” with Taiwan.

Detained: Czech MEP Markéta Gregorová said she was held for 1.5 hours while entering China, had her passport confiscated and was forbidden from using her phone, in what she said could be a “deliberate intimidation tactic.” Gregorová demanded an explanation from Beijing and asked Metsola to bar Chinese representatives from Parliament if she doesn’t get one.

Morocco’s hopes of being included as a trusted partner in the Industrial Accelerator Act are vanishing quickly, leading Rabat to enact “Plan B” of cozying up to China to keep its car exports up, Jordyn Dahl reports.

SG BEEFS UP: The Commission’s Secretariat-General, reporting directly to Ursula von der Leyen, is getting another boost: The new sanctions office announced yesterday, which will be housed in the powerful presidential service, will need 50 to 60 officials, a senior Commission official said. Some 40 to 45 officials already working on sanctions across other DGs will be moving there, the official added.

GOING ROUND IN CIRCLES: The EU’s Circular Economy Act is stuck on the Berlaymont’s 13th floor, officials tell Playbook and Fiona McNally. DG GROW and DG ENV have finished their work, but interservice consultation hasn’t started. It’s not clear whether that puts the Dec. 2 presentation at risk.

WHO KNEW POLITICS WAS HARD? Elon Musk, the world’s richest man, has admitted he feels “foolish” after spending more than $440 million backing the Republicans in the midterms, my stateside colleagues write.

GENDER BACKLASH: Russia and the Vatican have been accused of blocking references to gender at the COP31 conference in Turkey, Zia Weise reports.

FOREVER CHEMICALS, TEMPORARY EXEMPTIONS: The EU’s chemical safety watchdog wants sweeping temporary exemptions from the planned PFAS ban to protect key manufacturing sectors, according to a draft obtained by POLITICO.

PATENT MYSTERY: The Commission has been accused of withholding internal emails explaining why it scrapped a controversial patent proposal. MEPs suspect the U-turn may have followed a meeting between von der Leyen and U.S. Vice President JD Vance.

ROBERT PATTINSON’S EU CONNECTION: Becoming the next James Bond surely doesn’t top the time the British actor featured heavily in a Commission webinar on how to fight deepfakes.

WEATHER: Light showers. High of 11C.

A MODEL DELIVERY DELAY: Remember the tactile miniature of the Europa building I was so excited about in yesterday’s Playbook? Well, the unveiling was canceled just an hour beforehand, “for reasons beyond the control of the Council of the European Union and the ONCE Social Group,” a note from the organizers read. The problem? The model itself never arrived.

Costa’s Christmas spirit: European Council President António Costa still met the ONCE Foundation’s Miguel Carballeda, joking in an Instagram reel that in Spain presents arrive on Three Kings Day on Jan. 6, so there’s still time for his gift.

Mystery solved: “The delivery company did not deliver on time. Which I am sure is relatable to many of us in Brussels,” a person familiar with the arrangements told Playbook, granted anonymity to avoid trouble with future parcels. The model is stuck at a logistics center but should eventually reach the Council for visitors to enjoy. Sooner or later.

CONVERSION THERAPY CONTROVERSY: Looking for a heated debate? Head to the European Parliament at 11:30 a.m., where an event on freedom of speech and conscience is raising eyebrows over its focus on so-called conversion practices aimed at changing or suppressing someone’s sexual orientation or gender identity.

Freedom for whom? Conservative MEP Paolo Inselvini defended the event to Playbook, arguing that while violence and coercion must be condemned, “we cannot equate abuse with the right of parents to bring up their children, of a priest to offer spiritual guidance.” Renew MEP Raquel García Hermida-van der Walle disagreed: “Blergh. Forcing people to give up their sexuality, often under severe pressure, is quite the opposite of freedom.” She added: “Love is not a disease.”

Brussels draws a line: A spokesperson for Equality Commissioner Hadja Lahbib declined to comment on the event itself but pointed to her previous call: “Ban conversion practices, now.” Parliament, meanwhile, stressed that the gathering is organized by an MEP, not the institution itself.

DON’T WASTE THIS REMINDER: The blue bag is for packaging, not your old sweater. Brussels residents tossed nearly 4,000 tonnes of the wrong stuff into blue bags in 2025, costing the capital almost €4 million. The usual suspects? Toys, clothes and e-cigarettes. Bruxelles-Propreté and Fost Plus are launching a campaign to sort things out. Literally.

SPOTTED … at Iosono il Piemonte in Ixelles for the inauguration of the Juventus Club EU, a new group established by Renew MEP Sandro Gozi to bring together Juve fans in the Brussels bubble: Former Juventus legend and Chief Club Affairs Officer Giorgio Chiellini; Juve Chair Gianluca Ferrero; Piedmont Region President Alberto Cirio; MEPs Matteo Ricci, Stefano Bonaccini and Andreas Schwab; ANSA’s Michele Esposito; and the Italian perm rep’s Alberto La Bella.

Berlin: While Friedrich Merz spends his day with foreign leaders, the SPD’s Manuela Schwesig is also in the capital, where she’ll be closely watched for any sign that she’ll run for the party leadership.

Paris: French Greens leader Marine Tondelier has opened the door to backing far-left candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon for president, proposing a week of talks with France Unbowed to strike a deal.

Madrid: A POLITICO Poll puts Pedro Sánchez’s Socialists almost neck and neck with the People’s Party — but with Vox’s support pushing the right-wing bloc to almost 50%, the center-left faces an increasingly narrow path back to power.

London: Andy Burnham will co-chair today’s Coalition of the Willing meeting on Ukraine — but it’s also an opportunity to nail down parts of the EU reset deal with Merz and Macron before tomorrow’s summit in Brussels.

Read more from our Playbook family: Washington … Ottawa … Canberra.

— Commission President Ursula von der Leyen is in Jordan for the EU-Jordan Investment Conference 2026. She’ll deliver a speech soon after 7:45 a.m. Watch live.

— Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin, hosted by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Von der Leyen, European Council President António Costa, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte are among those attending.

— General Affairs Council. Press conference around 3:15 p.m. Watch here.

— Education, Youth, Culture and Sport Council (Education and Youth). Press conference around 5:30 p.m. Watch live.

— 31st Accession Conference with Montenegro. Press conference with Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos at 4:30 p.m. Watch live.

— European Parliament President Roberta Metsola receives young entrepreneurs at 11:30 a.m.

— Commission Executive Vice President Raffaele Fitto and Economy Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis take part in the European Parliament hearing on the 2025 discharge for the Recovery and Resilience Facility. Dombrovskis also delivers a keynote speech at the BusinessEurope CEO Dialogue.

— Mediterranean Commissioner Dubravka Šuica meets Jordan’s King Abdullah II.

— Sustainable Transport Commissioner Apostolos Tzitzikostas meets Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenković.

— Consumer Protection Commissioner Michael McGrath meets European Economic and Social Committee President Séamus Boland and BEUC Director-General Agustín Reyna.

— Culture Commissioner Glenn Micallef meets Austria’s Europe Minister Claudia Bauer, Polish Culture Minister Marta Cienkowska and Wolfram Weimer, Germany’s federal government commissioner for culture and media.

— The Political and Security Committee meets at 8 a.m.

— The EU Court of Justice publishes First Advocate General Maciej Szpunar’s opinion, read by Advocate General Laulhé Shaelou, in case C-663/24 Streamz and others. The case concerns whether Belgian rules requiring online platforms and streaming services to pay press publishers, authors and performers are compatible with EU copyright law.

MEP Katarina Barley; former MEPs Elżbieta Kruk, Rory Palmer, Bogdan Brunon Wenta and Gianni Pittella; Denmark’s Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen; Twitter co-founder Jack Dorsey; Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, president of Egypt; POLITICO’s Nathalie Weatherald and Margaux Reisinger.

Playbook is brought to you by POLITICO’s EU Politics team: Gerardo Fortuna, Nicholas Vinocur, Gabriel Gavin, Zoya Sheftalovich, Max Griera, Mari Eccles, Hanne Cokelaere, Lucia Mackenzie, Gregorio Sorgi and Sebastian Starcevic. And: reporters Daria Zakharova and Thibault Krause, editors Alex Spence and James Panichi, and producers Dean Southwell and Hugh Kapernaros.

Under the theme ‘Schools for tomorrow: fit for the era of AI’, this year’s European Education and Skills Summit will focus on strong foundations for every learner, the future of teaching as a profession, and education and vocational training that keep up with the economy.
